## Change: pos-ux-refinements

Cierra la deuda de UX del POS de mostrador identificada en `docs/pos/17`, `18` y `19`. 4 sub-frentes resueltos sin tocar el dominio de ventas.

## Sub-frentes in scope
- **Estado visual de los 4 botones contextuales** (Asignar cliente, Ingresar monto recibido, Convertir a fiado, Cambiar método): Alpine store `posSidebar` centralizado reemplaza el `x-data="{...}"` inline previo. Bindings `:class` consistentes via `isButtonActive`.
- **Reactivación de paneles**: `usedPanels` + `markUsed` + `isButtonUsed` real + hint visual `used` en los 4 botones.
- **Typeahead de cliente en POS**: input con `x-model` + `@input.debounce.300ms` + dropdown renderizado desde `customerResults` + navegación por teclado (↓↑ Enter Escape) + `@click.outside`. Reutiliza `GET /pos/customers/search` existente.
- **Layout vertical del sidebar**: wrapper de altura fija (`max-h-[calc(100vh-12rem)] overflow-y-auto`) + `overflow-y-auto` interno por panel. Semántica de pin preservada verbatim.

## Excluido (out of scope, por diseño)
- Dominio de ventas (`CreateSaleService`, `PosSaleDraftBuilder`, `VoidSaleService`) — NO modificado
- Livewire — no introducido (UI sigue siendo Blade + Alpine.js)
- Spec `fiado-auto-config` — fuera de este change
- Recargas, XML, móvil, barcode físico (iteración 2)
- Semántica de navegación `Inventario` vs `Stock actual` (frente paralelo)
- Cobertura E2E automatizada
- Alta rápida de cliente desde el typeahead (Q2 cerrado como fuera de alcance)
- `localStorage` / `$persist` — persistencia solo en sesión (Q1, PII no debe filtrarse en POS compartido)

## Delivery: 6 chained PRs (feature-branch-chain)
| # | PR | Branch | Target | Líneas | Tests |
|---|----|--------|--------|--------|-------|
| 2 | 1a store + customer/payment | `feat/pos-ux-pr-1a-store-customer-payment` | tracker | 380 | 7 |
| 3 | 1a test coverage | `feat/pos-ux-pr-1a-test-coverage` | tracker | 156 | (del #2) |
| 4 | 1b received/credit | `feat/pos-ux-pr-1b-received-credit-bindings` | 1a | 149 | 5 |
| 5 | 2 reactivation | `feat/pos-ux-pr-2-reactivation` | 1b | 240 | 5 |
| 6 | 3 typeahead | `feat/pos-ux-pr-3-typeahead` | 2 | 64 | 3 |
| 7 | 4 layout | `feat/pos-ux-pr-4-layout` | 3 | 225 | 4 |

Todos los PRs mergearon con status MERGEABLE + CLEAN. Total: 1214 líneas de diff, 24 tests nuevos, todos los PRs bajo el budget de 400 líneas (PR 1a fue el más grande con 380, gracias al split del test file a PR #3 aprobado por el usuario).

## Artifacts SDD (en este change folder)
- `openspec/changes/pos-ux-refinements/proposal.md` — intención, alcance, enfoque, riesgos, rollback
- `openspec/changes/pos-ux-refinements/design.md` — shape del Alpine store, contrato de endpoint, arquitectura de PRs
- `openspec/changes/pos-ux-refinements/tasks.md` — checklist por PR, contracts entre PRs, review workload forecast
- `openspec/changes/pos-ux-refinements/specs/` — 5 delta specs (4 nuevas + 1 aditiva sobre `pos-sidebar-state`)
- Engram topic `sdd/pos-ux-refinements/apply-progress` — historial completo de los 6 PRs

## Testing
- Strict TDD mode activo: `cd backend && composer test`
- 24 tests nuevos en 5 archivos (PosSidebarStoreTest, PosSidebarReceivedCreditBindingsTest, PosSidebarReactivationTest, PosCustomerSearchTest extensions, PosSidebarLayoutTest)
- 3 tests pre-existentes fallando (Auth\RegistrationTest x2, ExampleTest x1) — fuera de scope, no introducidos por este change
- Regresión visual manual con `MinimarketDemoSeeder` documentada en cada PR body (4 escenarios de venta: simple, con cliente, fiada, pago mixto)

## Rollback
`git revert` del merge commit de este PR restaura el POS al estado pre-change (sin Alpine store, con `x-data="{...}"` inline original). Sin migraciones de DB ni cambios de dominio. `npm run build` si los assets frontend necesitan regeneración.

## Riesgos conocidos

## Summary
Three things on this branch.

### 1. Place the previously-unused atlas art
- `tile_atlas_defs.gd` / `overworld_tileset_service.gd` / `culture_types.gd`: register and place four orphaned overworld cells — a **Chapel** (10,1), **Domed Temple** (9,1) and **Grand Cathedral** (11,0) as human ambient structures on grassland (common→rare), and the lone craggy peak (9,0) as a rare dwarven **Craggy Tor** on mountains.

### 2. Held item on the player
- New `HeldItemService`: parents a "HeldItem" icon sprite to the player model, sized to a steady ~half-tile regardless of body scale. Each walkable scene tracks the selected hotbar slot (set on use, alongside the existing drink/eat/arm behavior) and refreshes the held sprite on selection, inventory change, rebind, and respawn. The hotbar shows a persistent gold "selected" outline.

### 3. Drag items to the ground to drop them
- Hotbar and backpack slots are drag sources (`set_drag_forwarding`) returning an `item_drop` payload + icon preview. Each scene adds a full-rect `MOUSE_FILTER_PASS` drop catcher under the map panel: a slot dragged onto open world drops one unit as a world object at the player's cell (or nearest free neighbour); walking onto it reclaims it (armed once the player steps off, so a fresh drop lingers instead of snapping back). Applied to both the town and the hold; only the scene mutates inventory/world.

- All files compile clean (`--check-only`, after refreshing the global class cache for `HeldItemService`).

- metadata-api CPU limit 4150m→4000m + request 1650m→3000m (stops CFS-throttle liveness trips)
- quiver-xtab worker pools widened (~150/s/pod) + memory request 2560Mi→5120Mi (stops MemoryPressure evictions)
- redis-ha PDB; sql-executor `DS_POOL_MAXCONNECTIONS=32`

**prod-small:** redis-ha PDB · **dev:** minor

## Notes
First of several PRs splitting the old umbrella branch into independently-landable pieces. This is the non-breaking sizing slice — deployable to an existing cluster without a rebuild. Excludes F-core-specific quiver tuning and load-test-only toggles.

author: mkceichelbeck
body:
## Summary
Adds **GitHub Copilot** as a registry-backed provider engine (`copilot`), modeled on the Pi provider: adapter + JSONL parser + registry/type/contract wiring.

The parser is grounded in the **real** `copilot --output-format json` schema (verified against CLI v1.0.69): dot-namespaced events with payload under `data`, `phase:"commentary"` → thinking / `final_answer` → text, and success derived from the terminal `exitCode`. Fail-open on unknown event types.

Also makes two capabilities genuinely functional (verified, not assumed):
- **thinkingMode** — commentary narration is surfaced as thinking, the final answer as text.
- **dockerIsolation** — `--docker` now auto-activates the *running* provider's credential preset (mount + env passthrough) in `isolation-manager.js`, so `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN` reaches the container with no `dockerMounts` change (also auto-mounts codex/gemini/opencode/pi creds; claude stays special-cased). A keychain-token provider with no token warns loudly instead of failing silently.

## Verification
- `npm run check:agent-cli-provider` 100/100; full unit suite green; adapter + docker preset/warning unit tests.
- Real-schema parser verified by replaying captured copilot output.
- A real `zeroshot run --provider copilot` cluster ran end-to-end (parsed streamed JSONL, wrote the expected file, fired completion).
- Offline `fake-copilot` e2e (`tests/e2e/copilot-provider.test.js`) as the committed regression.

The existing deployment verification steps only confirmed that the
Ansible playbook exited cleanly and that Kubernetes nodes were Ready.
After the TYO incident (GO-136), it became clear those checks are not
sufficient: the environment was announced as ready while the console was
unreachable via its public IP, BGP was advertising blackhole routes for
all floating IPs, operator IP whitelists were empty, Hedgehog still held
stale tenant networks from the previous deployment, and the VPN agent
was failing reconciliation on every tenant.

The gap between "infrastructure is up" and "the product works for a
user" needs to be explicitly closed before handing an environment to
customers.

author: robbie-c
body:
## Problem

Two production-blocking issues with the `ml-mirror-image-scrub` deployment, surfaced by the PodImagePullBackOff alert in prod-us ([Slack thread](https://posthog.slack.com/archives/C09KUMHT64A/p1783603069612189?thread_ts=1783603068.194359&cid=C09KUMHT64A)):

1. **The image cannot be pulled at all.** The charts-side Karpenter NodePool provisions arm64 (Graviton) nodes, but the image was built for `linux/amd64` only, so every pull fails with `no match for platform in manifest`.
2. **The sidecar is a monitoring blind spot.** It has good Prometheus instrumentation (`ml_mirror_image_scrub_*`: scrub latency, 500/503/413/422 outcomes, output-size histogram), but none of it is scraped: `/scrub`, `/metrics`, and the health probes all lived on a single Express listener bound to `127.0.0.1`, because the pod IP must never expose `/scrub`. Prometheus and kubelet probes hit the pod IP, so nothing could reach `/metrics`, `/_health`, or `/_ready` either.

## Change

- **Build a multi-arch image** (`linux/amd64,linux/arm64`). sharp ships prebuilt linux-arm64 libvips binaries (already in the lockfile), so adding the platform is enough.
- **Split observability onto its own listener** bound to all interfaces:
  - `/scrub` stays on `127.0.0.1` exactly as before, loopback-only, unchanged.
  - `/metrics`, `/_health`, `/_ready` move to a second listener on `0.0.0.0` (`IMAGE_SCRUB_METRICS_PORT`, default `9011`). It serves no image bytes, only counters + probes.
- `startServer` now returns `{ scrub, metrics }`; shutdown closes both. Tests assert metrics/health are served on the metrics listener and that `/scrub` is **not** reachable there (404), locking in the separation.

## Verification

`typecheck`, `oxlint`, `oxfmt --check`, and `jest` all pass in `ml-mirror-image-scrub-sidecar` (7/7 tests).

## Companion charts PR (required)

The charts release currently probes and scrapes port `9090` (values written for the deleted Kafka consumer worker, not this sidecar). The companion charts PR must:

1. Point `livenessProbe`/`readinessProbe` httpGet at `9011`.
2. Point Prometheus scraping at `9011` (`monitoring.prometheus.port`) and set `IMAGE_SCRUB_METRICS_PORT: "9011"`.
3. Drop the stale consumer-era env (Kafka/S3 placeholders) and relabel the app to the owning team.

Once that lands, the companion [grafana-dashboards PR #254](https://github.com/PostHog/grafana-dashboards/pull/254) can be extended with sidecar-level panels (scrub latency, 5xx rate, output-size regressions).

### Motivation
- Ensure the Web3D visual acceptance validator requires `tool0` presence in viewer-resolved frame positions and frame diagnostics even when `tool0` is not mesh-backed in the rendered diagnostics.

### Description
- Removed `"wrist_3_link -> tool0"` and `"tool0 -> gripper_base_link"` from `REQUIRED_RENDERED_MESH_ADJACENT_PAIRS` so only mesh-backed UR5 adjacency checks remain.

- Updated and added unit tests in `tests/test_workcell_web3d_visual_acceptance.py` covering presence of `tool0` in frame diagnostics (allowed to be absent from rendered mesh diagnostics), failures when `tool0` frame diagnostics or resolved positions are missing, and failures for implausible `wrist_3_link -> tool0` or `tool0 -> gripper_base_link` distances.

body:
## Why
DevOps teams at enterprise clients frequently **can't reach `public.ecr.aws`** (or policy forbids pulling from it) and must mirror images into their own registry (Harbor/ECR/Artifactory) and install offline. Today that means overriding 3–4 `images.*.repository` values by hand — the GitLab "per-subchart" cautionary pattern. This makes air-gapped install first-class.

## What changed
- **`global.imageRegistry`** — one value repoints **every** image at an internal registry via the `anyray.image` helper (`public.ecr.aws/anyray/gateway` → `my.registry:5000/anyray/gateway`; path preserved so a straight `crane cp` mirror works). Per-image `images.*` overrides still win. Default empty = **byte-identical** output.
- **`scripts/gen-image-bom.sh`** — renders the chart and prints the exact image bill-of-materials to mirror, **digest-pinned** (`@sha256`) when `crane` is on PATH. Always matches what the chart deploys (no drift).
- **Chart.yaml** — Artifact Hub links.

## Validation
```
# default — unchanged
helm template … → public.ecr.aws/anyray/{gateway,optimizer,proxy}, docker.io/postgres
# override — all repointed, path preserved
--set global.imageRegistry=my.registry:5000 → my.registry:5000/anyray/{gateway,…}, my.registry:5000/postgres
```
`helm lint` clean; BOM script `bash -n` clean and emits digest-pinned refs.

## Companion
Air-gapped install **docs page** ships in a monorepo PR (the 4-step mirror recipe using this knob + the BOM script). Artifact Hub **listing** still needs a one-time manual registration of `https://charts.anyray.ai` on artifacthub.io (like the Railway marketplace — dashboard-only).

author: nbellalou
body:
## What?

This PR adds an opt-in UCP rendezvous policy knob for intra-node CUDA tag transfers. When enabled, the policy prefers the shared-memory staged CUDA-copy pipeline path for CUDA-to-CUDA rendezvous on the same node, while keeping the default behavior unchanged.

## Why?

[internal issue](https://nvbugspro.nvidia.com/bug/6119327)

Workaround for a performance issue caused by a bad wireup bandwidth estimation model. Wireup model makes the RC/IB path look better than the staged CUDA-copy path, so UCX selects RC for intra-node GPU-to-GPU transfers even though the staged shared-memory path performs significantly better.
Existing UCX rendezvous knobs are not sufficient for this case. Broad knobs such as `UCX_RNDV_SCHEME` select a rendezvous scheme globally, but they do not express the policy needed here:

- apply only to intra-node CUDA tag rendezvous;
- prefer the staged shared-memory CUDA-copy pipeline;
- preserve explicit user-selected rendezvous schemes;
- avoid changing AM/RMA rendezvous internals;
- avoid disabling RC/IB globally, which would also affect unrelated and inter-node traffic.

The new knob keeps this behavior opt-in and scoped, so it can be used as a tactical workaround without changing default protocol selection for other environments.

## How?

- Add `UCX_RNDV_PIPELINE_SHM_CUDA_STAGING_FORCE` as an opt-in policy knob.
- Scope the policy to intra-node CUDA tag rendezvous while `RNDV_SCHEME=auto`.
- Force only the relevant staged receiver pipeline envelope and sender-side child selection needed for the copy-to-attached host-staged path.
- Preserve AM/RMA rendezvous provenance so those flows are not redirected by the tag-only policy.
- Keep synthetic proto-estimation rkey configs separate from normal runtime rkey configs.
- Add focused gtests for enabled, disabled, explicit-scheme, AM/RMA, and rkey-identity behavior.

author: yiliang114
body:
## What this PR does

This PR treats a main-assistant response that starts with leaked `<analysis>` or `<summary>` protocol tags as an invalid turn. The entire pure-text attempt is suppressed, excluded from chat-recording JSONL and in-memory history, and retried through the existing bounded invalid-stream retry path. A retry is successful only when the model returns a normal response without the protocol wrapper.

The detector buffers only the leading tag prefix so it works across arbitrary SSE chunk boundaries without parsing or recovering the protocol payload. Once ordinary response text is identified, streaming continues unchanged. Responses that contain tool calls are not retried, avoiding duplicate side effects.

## Why it is needed

The content inside a leaked `<summary>` is compaction protocol output, not the requested task result. Unwrapping that summary and presenting it as a successful assistant response stops the task before the expected follow-up tool calls and contaminates later context. The correct recovery is to discard the abnormal turn and replay the original request from clean history.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Verify that a split `<analysis>` response followed by an SSE disconnect retries without rendering the partial response, a completed `<analysis>...<summary>...</summary>` response is discarded and retried without persistence, and only a later ordinary response reaches the terminal and history. Also verify that normal HTML such as `<details><summary>...</summary></details>` and protocol-tag names appearing later in prose are not rejected.

Commands run locally:

```bash
cd packages/core && npx vitest run src/core/geminiChat.test.ts
npx eslint --max-warnings 0 --no-warn-ignored packages/core/src/core/geminiChat.ts packages/core/src/core/geminiChat.test.ts integration-tests/fake-openai-server.ts integration-tests/interactive/protocol-tags-interactive.test.ts
npm run typecheck
npm run build && npm run bundle
cd integration-tests && QWEN_SANDBOX=false npx vitest run interactive/protocol-tags-interactive.test.ts --retry 0
```

### Evidence (Before & After)

Before: the leaked summary payload could be stripped from its wrapper and treated as the final user-visible answer.

After: the complete tagged turn is rejected, never persisted, and retried; only an ordinary successful response is emitted.

### Tested on

| OS | Status |
| :-- | :-- |
| macOS | tested |
| Windows | not tested |
| Linux | CI |

## Risk & Scope

- Detection is intentionally limited to protocol tags at the beginning of a main-assistant response, after optional whitespace.
- Pure-text protocol leaks use the existing bounded invalid-stream retry budget.
- Tool-call turns are not retried, preventing duplicate side effects.
- Subagent and compaction sanitization behavior is unchanged.

## Linked Issues

Closes #6595

Related to #6023 and #6027.

author: fabiodalez-dev
body:
Addresses Uwe's in-app remarks (a real lending-library user): the opening list had no heading, results were only sortable by cataloguing date, and there was no sub-category filtering.

## What's new
- **Sort picker** — Newest / Oldest / Title A–Z / Title Z–A, sent as `sort=` to `GET /api/v1/catalog/search` (backend support: Pinakes PR #242). Changing sort resets pagination. The active order is shown as "Sort: <label>" in the results header.

author: paullatzelsperger
body:
## Summary

Replaces the short scope constants (`read`/`write`/`admin`, `siglet-read`/`siglet-write`) with their fully-qualified equivalents so the agents request the scopes the services actually enforce, and centralizes the agent scope set in the jwtlet activity so seeded scope mappings cannot drift from what the clients request.

## Changes

- **controlplane**: scopes become `management-api:{read,write,admin}`. Participant context lifecycle operations require `management-api:admin`.
- **identityhub**: credential operations use resource-scoped `identity-api:credentials:{read,write}`; participant context create/delete still require `identity-api:admin`.
- **issuerservice**: all operations require `issuer-admin-api:admin` — the token is bound to the issuer's participant context, so resource-level scopes are rejected with `No participant for 'sub = ...' found`.
- **siglet**: scopes become `siglet-mgmt-api:{read,write}`.
- **jwtlet activity**: introduces `agentScopes`, sourced directly from the API client constants. The deploy-time token-exchange verification now requests the full set, so a missing scope mapping fails fast at deploy rather than in a downstream agent.

- **Beco sem saída pós-pagamento no cadastro**: depois de aprovar o Pix simulado ou o cartão durante o wizard de cadastro, o código só chamava `router.refresh()` — que não faz nada útil numa página cujo estado é todo client-side (o wizard ficava parado na etapa 4 pra sempre). Agora redireciona para `/dashboard`.

### 2. UX / interação / acessibilidade
- **Sem navegação nenhuma no mobile**: o `SiteHeader` escondia os links de navegação abaixo do breakpoint `md` sem nenhuma alternativa — usuários mobile não conseguiam acessar Quem somos/Consultas/Como funciona/Dúvidas. Criei o `MobileNavMenu` (hambúrguer) reunindo navegação, login por perfil e o CTA "Iniciar consulta".
- **Dropdown "Entrar" sem semântica de menu**: faltava `aria-haspopup`/`aria-expanded`, não fechava com Esc e não devolvia o foco ao botão ao fechar. Corrigido, com `role="menu"`/`menuitem`.
- **Foco de teclado quase invisível em vários formulários**: os campos de login, cadastro, redefinição de senha e edição de paciente pelo admin usavam `outline-none` com só uma troca sutil de cor de borda como indicador de foco. Adicionei `focus:ring-2` visível, consistente com o componente `Input` compartilhado.

### 3. Erros no código
- `npx tsc --noEmit` e `npm run build` já estavam limpos antes desta PR; não usei `any`, `console.log` fora de scripts, nem padrões inseguros — nenhum erro de tipo/build adicional encontrado.

author: isilher
body:
## Problem

`detectInlineHook` reads the first byte of libc's `open` directly:

```cpp
unsigned char *addr = (unsigned char *) symbol;
if (addr[0] == 0xEA || addr[0] == 0xE9) { ... }
```

On **Android 10 (arm64)**, the `.text` of system libraries such as libc is mapped **execute-only (XOM)**. Reading it raises a hard `SIGSEGV`:

```
Cause: execute-only (no-read) memory access error; likely due to data in .text.
signal 11 (SIGSEGV), code 2 (SEGV_ACCERR)
  #00 librootjaildetect.so (NativeSecurityChecker_detectInlineHook+52)
  #08 com.rootjaildetect.RootDetection.isDeviceRooted
  #11 com.rootjaildetect.RootJailDetectModule.isDeviceCompromised
```

This is an **uncatchable native signal** — it crashes the whole process on launch and cannot be caught by a JS `try/catch`. XOM was enabled by default in **Android 10 only** and removed again in Android 11 ([AOSP docs](https://source.android.com/docs/security/test/execute-only-memory)), so the crash reproduces specifically on Android 10 arm64 devices.

## Fix

Read the prologue through a new `safeRead()` helper that follows [Google's guidance](https://source.android.com/docs/security/test/execute-only-memory#reading): add `PROT_READ` via `mprotect` **only when the page is genuinely non-readable**, then restore the original (execute-only) protection so the OS hardening isn't permanently weakened.

- On **Android 11+** the page is already readable → no protection change, behaviour unchanged.
- If the page can't be confirmed readable → returns `false` rather than risk a crash.

## While here: architecture-aware signature

`0xEA`/`0xE9` are **32-bit ARM** branch opcodes. On the arm64 ABI that ships today the check never matched (and could false-positive on a coincidental low byte). This matches the arm64 `B` and `LDR X16/X17` trampoline prologues, and keeps corrected ARM32 opcodes under `__arm__`.

## Testing

Verified on a Redmi M2004J19C (Android 10, arm64) that previously crashed in `detectInlineHook` on every launch: with this change the app launches through and `isDeviceCompromised()` returns correctly on a non-rooted device.

## Summary
This PR introduces a comprehensive design system refresh with a new reusable `SegmentedControl` component and updates the global styling to use CSS custom properties for consistent theming. The changes modernize the UI with improved visual hierarchy, better accessibility, and more polished interactions across the application.

## Key Changes

### New Components
- **SegmentedControl.svelte**: A reusable iOS-style segmented control component with smooth spring-feel animations, replacing inline toggle implementations in timetable and meals pages

### Design System & Styling (`app.css`)
- Added design tokens (CSS custom properties) for separators, surfaces, and page backgrounds that adapt to light/dark modes
- Introduced custom easing functions (`--ease-spring`, `--ease-out-quart`) for consistent motion
- Created `.card` component class for elevated surfaces with consistent styling
- Added `.material-chrome` class for translucent sticky headers with backdrop blur
- Implemented `.spinner` activity indicator with animation
- Refactored pressable interaction utilities with improved spring-back animation (0.35s ease-out-quart)
- Enhanced reduced-motion and high-contrast media query support

### Page Updates
- **Timetable** (`+page.svelte`): 
  - Replaced custom week toggle with `SegmentedControl` component
  - Added today's column highlighting (Mon–Fri only) with KST timezone handling
  - Refactored table styling to use CSS custom properties and improved visual hierarchy
  - Updated gradient overlays to use CSS variables instead of hardcoded colors
  - Improved period label typography and spacing

- **Meals** (`+page.svelte`):
  - Replaced custom meal type toggle with `SegmentedControl` component
  - Updated gradient styling to use CSS variables
  - Improved empty state messaging

- **Home** (`+page.svelte`):
  - Added `sectionHeader` snippet for consistent section headers with navigation links
  - Improved typography with better tracking and sizing
  - Updated card styling to use new `.card` class

- **Notice Detail** (`notice/[id]/+page.svelte`):
  - Redesigned back navigation with icon and improved styling
  - Updated loading/error states with better visual feedback
  - Improved article layout with better spacing and typography
  - Updated file list styling

- **Calendar** (`calendar/+page.svelte`):
  - Updated button styling to use new design tokens
  - Improved month navigation appearance

- **Admin** (`admin/+page.svelte`):
  - Updated form inputs and buttons to use new design system
  - Improved visual consistency with card styling

### Component Updates
- **NoticeCard.svelte**: Simplified styling using new `.card` class and improved hover states
- **NoticeGroup.svelte**: Updated typography and spacing for better visual hierarchy
- **NoticeFooter.svelte**: Redesigned footer buttons with improved spacing and interaction
- **ErrorState.svelte**: Enhanced with icon and better visual presentation
- **EmptyState.svelte**: Made configurable with message prop, added icon and improved styling
- **LoadingState.svelte**: Updated to use new `.spinner` component
- **Drawer.svelte**: Added rubber-band effect for drag interactions and improved drag detection

### Layout (`+layout.svelte`)
- Refactored navigation with data-driven approach
- Added scroll detection for conditional border styling on chrome
- Improved header styling and navigation link appearance

### Utilities
- Updated `getTypeColor()` in `lib/utils.ts` to use new color scheme

## Notable Implementation Details
- All gradient overlays now use CSS custom properties (`--surface`, `--page`) for automatic light/dark mode adaptation
- The `SegmentedControl` uses a sliding thumb animation with spring easing for smooth, iOS-like feel
- Today's column highlighting in timetable uses KST timezone conversion for accurate date detection
- Design tokens are centralized in `:root` with `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` overrides
- Accessibility improvements include proper ARIA labels, focus-visible states, and semantic HTML

author: shrey150
body:
## What

**Part 3 of 5 — stacked on #2338 (`vercel_ai_sdk`)** (base: `shrey/evals-harness-vercel-ai-sdk`; GitHub shows only this PR's delta). When the parent merges, retarget this PR's base and rebase.

Registers `--harness anthropic_sdk`: a hand-rolled `tool_use` loop via `@anthropic-ai/sdk` — the TS twin of the Python `while stop_reason == "tool_use"` loop that dominates real-world Anthropic usage (37.5M PyPI dl/wk) and of the Modal sandbox template's `agent.mjs`. No retries, no planning, no memory — deliberately: **the bareness is the instrument**.

- Anthropic models only (`anthropic/` prefix stripped; other providers rejected loudly).
- Step cap: shared 40 default, `EVAL_ANTHROPIC_SDK_MAX_STEPS` override; when the cap binds it's surfaced as the stop reason.
- Assistant text buffered per turn folds into the next tool call's `reasoning`; usage summed across turns.
- Adds the `@anthropic-ai/sdk` dependency (pinned 0.39.0, matching packages/core) — this PR carries its own lockfile delta.
- Testability: `client` injection seam (`messages.create` mock).

External harnesses design + usage: [`packages/evals/README.md#external-harnesses`](https://github.com/browserbase/stagehand/blob/shrey/evals-bareloop-harnesses/packages/evals/README.md#external-harnesses) (in #2337). Linear: STG-2515.

## Comparability fix (2026-07-09 audit)

Wired the caller's `AbortSignal` into `@anthropic-ai/sdk`'s native abort option (`messages.create(body, { signal })`) instead of only polling `signal?.aborted` between loop iterations — previously an abort mid-loop left an already-in-flight `messages.create()` call running to completion instead of cancelling the HTTP request. One new test asserts the signal is forwarded as-is to the client.

(anthropic_sdk's `step cap reached (N)` stop-reason shape was already correct here — it's the reference shape vercel_ai_sdk (#2338) and openai_agents_sdk (#2340) were fixed to match, per the same audit.)

## E2E Test Matrix

Live smoke ran on the pre-split combined branch (content identical to this stack's tip — verified by diff); results transplanted, not rerun.

| Command / flow | Observed output | Confidence / sufficiency |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `evals run b:webtailbench --harness anthropic_sdk -m anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5-20251001 -l 1 -t 1 -c 1` (local build, real ANTHROPIC + GEMINI keys, local Chrome via browse CLI) | Run completed (exit 0) **at the 40-step cap** (stop reason `step cap reached (40)`). 40 `browse` tool calls recorded; trajectory persisted; verifier graded: `outcomeSuccess=false`, `processScore=0.29`, 5 rubric criteria, **no verifierError**. Usage: 172k in / 2.6k out tokens | Bar met: harness completes, trajectory captured, graded outcome, no verifierError. Task pass/fail is NOT the bar (united.com flights). Cap-binding at 40 with haiku on a hard task is exactly the instrument behavior the design doc predicts |
| `pnpm exec vitest run` (this branch) | `Test Files 51 passed, Tests 376 passed` — adds `anthropicSdkRunner.test.ts` (multi-turn loop threading assistant/tool_result messages, tool_use → browse execution, step-cap stop reason, usage summing, model-prefix validation, SDK-error folding) | Mocked-model loop coverage; live behavior proven by the smoke row above |
| `tsc --noEmit` + prettier + eslint | clean | Types/style only |
| `pnpm exec vitest run` (this branch, post-fix) | `Test Files 51 passed, Tests 379 passed` — adds the AbortSignal-forwarding test | Proves the signal reaches `messages.create`'s options arg unchanged |
| `pnpm -w exec tsc --noEmit` + prettier + eslint (post-fix) | clean | Types/style only |

## Tier 1 fixes (post-review audit, 2026-07-14)

An independent audit found every non-`tool_use` stop reason -- including `max_tokens` (truncated output) -- was reported as a successful `"complete"`, tool-call failures had no native `is_error` signal, and `cache_creation_input_tokens` was never counted toward the total. Fixed here:

- **`max_tokens` truncation was indistinguishable from a real success.** Only `stop_reason === "end_turn"` now maps to `"complete"`; every other non-`tool_use` reason (`max_tokens`, `refusal`, `pause_turn`, ...) maps to `"aborted"` with the real `stop_reason` recorded as the stopReason.
- **Tool failures had no native `is_error`.** `tool_result` blocks now carry `is_error: !ok`, derived from `BareLoopToolRecorder.execute()`'s `{ ok, output }` (base PR) instead of silently dropping the failure signal.
- **Cache-creation tokens were never counted.** `AnthropicMessageResponse.usage` now tracks `cache_creation_input_tokens`; `providerTotalTokens` reports Anthropic's real total (input + output + cache_creation + cache_read) instead of undercounting via a recomputed input+output sum.

Verified: `pnpm --filter @browserbasehq/stagehand-evals build && lint && test:unit` -- `Test Files 56 passed, Tests 429 passed` (4 new tests: max_tokens-as-aborted, is_error propagation, cache-creation total, existing step-cap test updated to `"aborted"`).


No changeset: `packages/evals` is private.

Tam gaz kalkışta motor artık rölantiden serbest tırmanmak yerine önce konvertör-eşleşme (düşük dal) noktasında TUTULUR. Bu, iSCAAN'ın gözlenen "1023→1011 oyalanma → kopuş → ~2400 rpm" profiliyle örtüşür.

İki modlu konvertör dinamiği (calcStepPhysics):
- Her adımda teğet bölgesinde (~850-1350 rpm) net motor torku − pompa emişi fazlalığının minimumu bulunur (motorun oturduğu düşük dal noktası).
- Fazlalık CONV_MATCH_THRESHOLD (45 N·m) altındaysa motor eşleşme noktasında tutulur (engRate=0, oyalanma). Araç ~5-6 km/h'ye ulaşıp fazlalık eşiği aşınca düşük dal bozulur → motor KOPAR, serbest rev-up ataletiyle yüksek dala tırmanır. N_eng_dynamic düşük dalda eşleşme noktasına senkron tutulur, böylece kopuş sürekli (sıçramasız) başlar.

author: shrey150
body:
## What

**Part 4 of 5 — stacked on #2339 (`anthropic_sdk`)** (base: `shrey/evals-harness-anthropic-sdk`; GitHub shows only this PR's delta). When the parent merges, retarget this PR's base and rebase.

Registers `--harness openai_agents_sdk` via `@openai/agents` (6.8M PyPI dl/wk for the Python twin). Classification: **bare-ish** — one notch above the raw provider loops. The SDK runs its own agent loop (turn management, tool dispatch, tracing) but ships no behavioral scaffolding: everything the agent knows comes from the dev-supplied `instructions` string, which carries only the configured skill-arm prompt. **SDK defaults untouched except `maxTurns`** (the SDK's own default of 10 is far too low for a browse task; shared 40 default, `EVAL_OPENAI_AGENTS_SDK_MAX_TURNS` override).

- OpenAI models only (`openai/` prefix stripped; other providers rejected loudly).
- Tool parameters use a plain JSON schema instead of a zod schema to sidestep the SDK's zod version coupling (packages/evals pins zod v4).
- Usage summed from `result.rawResponses`.
- Adds the `@openai/agents` dependency (pinned 0.13.0) — this PR carries its own lockfile delta.
- Testability: `sdk` injection seam ({ Agent, run, tool } mock).

External harnesses design + usage: [`packages/evals/README.md#external-harnesses`](https://github.com/browserbase/stagehand/blob/shrey/evals-bareloop-harnesses/packages/evals/README.md#external-harnesses) (in #2337). Linear: STG-2515.

## Comparability fix (2026-07-09 audit)

`@openai/agents-core` throws `MaxTurnsExceededError` (`"Max turns (N) exceeded"`, `error.name === "MaxTurnsExceededError"` per `AgentsError`'s `this.name = new.target.name`) instead of returning a truncated result the way vercel_ai_sdk/anthropic_sdk do — the generic catch was folding that into `openaiAgentsSdkStatus: "error"`, reporting the shared step cap as a harness/SDK failure. Now detects it (by error name, with a message-shape regex fallback for robustness) and reports `status: "complete"` + the same `step cap reached (N)` stopReason `anthropic_sdk` (#2339) uses. The previous single "SDK errors" test (which happened to throw exactly this message and was silently exercising the bug) is now three tests: a genuine unrelated SDK error (still "error"), the real `MaxTurnsExceededError`-shaped throw hitting the cap, and the bare message-shape fallback without the SDK's error name.

## E2E Test Matrix

Live smoke ran on the pre-split combined branch (content identical to this stack's tip — verified by diff); results transplanted, not rerun.

| Command / flow | Observed output | Confidence / sufficiency |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `evals run b:webtailbench --harness openai_agents_sdk -m openai/gpt-5.4-mini -l 1 -t 1 -c 1` (local build, real OPENAI + GEMINI keys, local Chrome via browse CLI) | Run completed (exit 0). 10 `browse` tool calls recorded; trajectory persisted; verifier graded: `outcomeSuccess=false`, `processScore=1.0`, 5 rubric criteria, **no verifierError**. Clean final answer: "No reliable flight availability/pricing could be retrieved for United direct flights ..." Usage: 24k in / 0.5k out tokens | Bar met: harness completes, trajectory captured, graded outcome, no verifierError. Task pass/fail is NOT the bar (united.com flights); process=1.0 with outcome=false is the verifier saying "sound procedure, unreachable goal" |
| `pnpm exec vitest run` (this branch) | `Test Files 52 passed, Tests 380 passed` — adds `openaiAgentsSdkRunner.test.ts` (instructions === verbatim arm prompt only, maxTurns passthrough, JSON-schema tool execution against a real temp binary, usage summing, model-prefix validation, MaxTurnsExceeded folding) | Mocked-SDK loop coverage; live behavior proven by the smoke row above |
| `tsc --noEmit` + prettier + eslint | clean | Types/style only |
| `pnpm exec vitest run` (this branch, post-fix) | `Test Files 52 passed, Tests 385 passed` — MaxTurnsExceeded now correctly reported as `status: "completed"` + `step cap reached (N)` (2 new dedicated tests: real error-name shape, message-shape fallback); the pre-existing "SDK errors" test now throws a genuinely unrelated error to keep testing the generic-error path | Proves the cap is no longer misreported as a harness failure, without losing coverage of real SDK errors |
| `pnpm -w exec tsc --noEmit` + prettier + eslint (post-fix) | clean | Types/style only |

## Tier 1 fixes (post-review audit, 2026-07-14)

An independent audit found a live-reproducible bug: `sdk.run()` never returns on a max-turns exception, so `usage`/`modelTurns` stayed at their zero/undefined initial values -- a real 10-turn capped run persisted `input_tokens: 0, output_tokens: 0`. Fixed here:

- **Real usage/turn count recovered from the exception's own state.** The real `@openai/agents-core` `AgentsError` (base of `MaxTurnsExceededError`) carries a `state?: RunState` -- `RunState.usage` is a getter with real `inputTokens`/`outputTokens`/`totalTokens`, and `_currentTurn` is a public field with the real turn count. Both are now extracted in the max-turns catch branch instead of left at zero.
- **Step-cap runs reported `"complete"`, not `"aborted"`** -- same bug pattern as vercel_ai_sdk, same fix.
- **`total_tokens` now prefers the SDK's own `Usage.totalTokens`** over a recomputed input+output sum, on both the normal-return and exception paths.
- Updated the tool `execute` callback for `BareLoopToolRecorder.execute()`'s new `{ ok, output }` return shape (base PR).

Verified: `pnpm --filter @browserbasehq/stagehand-evals build && lint && test:unit` -- `Test Files 57 passed, Tests 437 passed` (2 new tests: state-based usage/turn recovery, totalTokens preference). Live: a real Browserbase local trial with `EVAL_OPENAI_AGENTS_SDK_MAX_TURNS=3` hit the real max-turns cap and the persisted trajectory recorded `"status": "aborted"` (not the old `0/0` usage bug -- confirmed the model's real tool calls, including a rejected `skills show` under `skillMode=none`, were captured).


No changeset: `packages/evals` is private.

author: shibosheng
body:
## Summary

Fixes #194

OpenCode imported history and subagent UI were leaking provider-specific logic across multiple layers. This change introduces the first `ExternalCliAdapter` and consolidates OpenCode behavior behind it, while preserving the product rule that ORGII-managed `cliagent-*` sessions own the sidebar and matching `opencodeapp-*` rows remain available only as backing history sources.

## Root Cause

### 1. Provider logic was scattered across unrelated modules

OpenCode-specific rules were split and duplicated between:

- `src-tauri/src/agent_sessions/event_pipeline/session_providers.rs` — imported-session matching, OpenCode DB history loading, subagent prompt fallback, and managed-parent aliasing.
- `src-tauri/crates/orgtrack-core/src/sources/opencode/history.rs` — imported history sync, listability, and parent-child mapping.
- `src-tauri/src/agent_sessions/event_pipeline/ingestion/prompt_backfill.rs` — generic fallback helpers that had to implicitly know about OpenCode-like ids.

### 2. The data structure was not a clean, centralized provider model

There was no single place where the OpenCode provider contract was defined. Instead, provider identity leaked into generic code through raw string prefixes (`opencodeapp-*`), direct SQL against `code_sessions`, and ad-hoc conversions from `cliagent-*` to `opencodeapp-*`. The same provider entity was represented differently in every layer:

```text
OpenCode SQLite DB     → ses_123
imported_history_cache → opencodeapp-ses_123
ORGII managed wrapper  → cliagent-abc
child subagent link    → opencodeapp-ses_child
```

Each layer had its own logic for mapping between these representations, so the shape of the provider was encoded implicitly in the code rather than in a single, explicit, well-organized data structure.

### 3. The design made the system fragmented, hard to test, and hard to extend

Because the provider contract was implicit:

- ID conversion, fallback priority, and listability rules were implemented in multiple places.
- Adding or fixing one behavior (e.g., hiding a managed mirror from the sidebar) required touching unrelated modules.
- Subagent prompt fallback had to be reasoned about in both the generic backfill path and the OpenCode-specific SQL path.
- Unit tests for the same provider identity were spread across crates.

When the left sidebar duplicated `cliagent-*` and `opencodeapp-*` rows, or when SubagentBlock showed generic text like “Assigned task to subagent”, the fix had to be made in several disconnected spots. The current design was not a clean, centralized data structure; it was a collection of provider-specific snippets stitched into generic code.

### 4. The new adapter design makes future CLI providers much easier to plug in

With `ExternalCliAdapter`, each provider now lives in one concrete module. The interface is small and provider-neutral:

```text
ExternalCliAdapter
  ├─ source()
  ├─ cli_agent_type()
  ├─ imported_session_prefix()
  ├─ load_history_events()
  ├─ resolve_subagent_prompt()
  └─ imported_parent_session_id()
```

To onboard a new CLI (Cursor, Codex, Claude Code, Windsurf, etc.), we only need to implement this trait and register it in the adapter registry. The facade in `session_providers.rs` and the history pipeline will automatically route the right sessions to the right adapter. No new frontend logic, no new prefix hacks, no duplication of the same provider contract across files.

## Fix

We extracted the live OpenCode behavior into a small, intentionally minimal adapter:

```text
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  cache_bridge / event_pipeline / history.rs  callers                 │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                                    │
                                    ▼
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  session_providers.rs  (compatibility facade, provider-neutral)      │
│  - skips_event_cache_save(session_id)                                │
│  - load_history_events(session_id)                                   │
│  - subagent_prompt(child_session_id)                                  │
│  - imported_parent_session_ids(parent_session_id)                     │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                                    │
                                    ▼
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  external_cli_adapter::adapter_for_imported_session(session_id)      │
│  - registry lookup by prefix (e.g., `opencodeapp-*`)                   │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                                    │
                                    ▼
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  OpenCodeAdapter (the first provider-specific impl)                  │
│  - source / cli_agent_type constants                                 │
│  - native ⇄ imported ID conversion                                   │
│  - load_history_events: OpenCode DB → ActivityChunk → SessionEvent   │
│  - resolve_subagent_prompt: explicit child-history → user_input → name fallback
│  - imported_parent_session_id: managed cliagent-* → opencodeapp-*    │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

### Files changed

- `src-tauri/src/agent_sessions/mod.rs` — exports `external_cli_adapter`.
- `src-tauri/src/agent_sessions/external_cli_adapter/mod.rs` — new adapter trait and registry.
- `src-tauri/src/agent_sessions/external_cli_adapter/opencode.rs` — `OpenCodeAdapter` implementation and focused tests.
- `src-tauri/src/agent_sessions/event_pipeline/session_providers.rs` — reduced to a facade that delegates OpenCode calls to the adapter.
- `src-tauri/crates/orgtrack-core/src/sources/opencode/history.rs` — keeps OpenCode DB reading and imported-cache semantics; adds managed-mirror detection from `code_sessions`.
- `src-tauri/crates/orgtrack-core/src/sources/opencode/history_tests.rs` — tests for managed-mirror hiding, external-history visibility, and conservative parent validation.

## The New Architecture: External CLI Adapter

The frontend already consumes a normalized schema (`Session`, `SessionEvent`, `ActivityChunk`, imported-history rows). The remaining gap was in Rust: how does each external CLI provider translate its own native identity, history, and subagent metadata into that normalized schema?

Our adapter design solves this by giving each external CLI a single backend-side adapter:

```text
Frontend (React)
        │ consumes Session / SessionEvent / imported rows
        │
        ▼
EventStore / cache_bridge
        │
        ▼
session_providers.rs (provider-neutral facade)
        │
        ├──────┬──────┬──────┬──────┐
        │      │      │      │      │
        ▼      ▼      ▼      ▼      ▼
   ┌──────┐ ┌──────┐ ┌──────┐ ┌──────┐ ┌──────┐
   │OpenCode│ │Cursor│ │Codex │ │Claude│ │Future│
   │Adapter │ │Future│ │Future│ │Future│ │ CLI  │
   │(live) │ │      │ │      │ │      │ │      │
   └──────┘ └──────┘ └──────┘ └──────┘ └──────┘
        │
        ▼
   OpenCode DB / native CLI history
```

Each adapter owns:

1. **Identity conversion** — e.g., `opencodeapp-ses_123` ⇄ `ses_123` ⇄ `cliagent-abc` (via `code_sessions`).
2. **History loading** — read the provider’s native history and convert to `ActivityChunk` / `SessionEvent`.
3. **Subagent prompt resolution** — know where to look for a real child task prompt when the parent event is missing it.
4. **Managed-parent aliasing** — map ORGII-managed wrapper IDs to their imported native IDs for replay/monitor.

## Why This Architecture Is Better

- **Single source of truth for provider rules.** OpenCode ID conversion, prompt fallback, and listability are no lon

author: yedidiasch
body:
## What

A one-liner that removes the `--workspace`/`--build`/`--packages` boilerplate for standard projects:

```bash
pandion build ./my-app -- ./build/app     # detect + upload + build + run
pandion build                             # cwd, build-only (start/ssh/debug after)
```

`pandion build [dir]` auto-detects the toolchain and delegates to `up` (way 2 / `sync: source`):

| Detected | Build command | Extra packages | C++ toolchain |
|---|---|---|---|
| CMakeLists.txt | `cmake -B build … && cmake --build build -j` | — | kept |
| meson.build | `meson setup build && meson compile -C build` | meson, ninja-build | kept |
| Cargo.toml | `cargo build --release` | cargo | skipped |
| go.mod | `go build ./...` | golang-go | skipped |
| package.json | `npm ci … && npm run build --if-present` | nodejs, npm | skipped |
| pyproject.toml / requirements.txt | `pip3 install …` | python3-pip | skipped |
| Makefile | `make -j` | — | kept |

- Detection is most-specific-first (a CMake project with a convenience Makefile is treated as CMake).
- Every `up` flag passes straight through (`--provider`, `--size`, `--id`, `--ttl`, …); a detected knob only fills what the caller didn't set.
- With no `-- <cmd>` it deploys + builds only (like `--no-run`) and prints the next steps.
- Clear, actionable error when no toolchain is recognized.

## Verification
- `go build`, `go vet`, `gofmt -l` clean; `go test ./...` green.
- Unit: `detectBuild` table test (every stack + precedence + unknown).
- Offline smoke: `build <go-project> --dry-run` shows the "detected Go" banner and forwards flags; an empty dir errors helpfully.
- e2e: `scripts/e2e_build.sh` — scaffolds a CMake C++ project, `build … -- ./build/app`, asserts the built binary's marker in the run log; Go detection via `--dry-run`; `down` cleans up (run by hand against real cloud).

author: tyy0829
body:
## Bug Fix: Layerwise KV Pool IndexError when MTP is enabled

### Problem
When using layerwise KV pool (MemCache backend) with MTP speculative decoding enabled, vLLM crashes with `IndexError: list index out of range` on the first inference request.

### Root Cause
1. `_infer_cache_group_metadata` counts ALL layer names (including MTP draft layers) in `group_num_layers`, causing `num_layers` to be inflated (e.g., 47 → 48 for GLM-4.7-Flash with 1 MTP layer).
2. `layer_save_tasks` / `layer_load_tasks` are initialized with the original `num_layers` (47), but iterated with the inflated `num_layers` (48) → **IndexError**.
3. `wait_for_layer_load` lacks the MTP guard that `save_kv_layer` already has, causing a second IndexError when MTP draft model executes.

### Fix
1. **Add `_extract_physical_layer_index` method**: identifies MTP layers by name pattern (`mtp.N.xxx` → `num_hidden_layers + N`), which maps to an index >= `num_layers`.
2. **Skip MTP layers in `_infer_cache_group_metadata`**: MTP layers (`phys >= num_layers`) are excluded from `group_num_layers`, so `num_layers` stays at the correct value (47).
3. **Add `wait_for_layer_load` MTP guard**: `if self.current_layer >= self.num_layers: return`, matching the existing guard in `save_kv_layer`.

### Verification
Tested with GLM-4.7-Flash (TP=4) + MTP + layerwise MemCache:
- Service starts successfully (no IndexError)
- Inference works correctly
- KV pool cache hits on repeated requests (`hit_blocks=8/8`, External prefix cache hit rate: 45.4%)

### Note
This fix is already validated on the `feature/multi-group-v0.23` branch (commit 170094407). This PR cherry-picks the relevant changes to `releases/v0.23.0`.

- vLLM version: v0.23.0
- vLLM main: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/ee0da84ab9e04ac7610e28580af62c365e898389

author: blahmonkey
body:
## What does this PR change?

### Change

Fixes a boot deadlock introduced in v0.68.0 (#102). The launcher wires `ModeController`, `positions_lock`, and `state.risk.lock` to a single shared `threading.Lock`. Since v0.68.0, `reconcile` / `evaluate_risk` / `apply_health_and_risk` acquired `state.risk.lock_cm()` inside the already-held mode lock — so under that shared wiring they re-entered the same non-reentrant lock and hung the boot thread in `reconcile` before it reached the run loop, and shutdown then hung on the nexus-thread join.

- `_risk_reads_cm` returns a no-op context manager when `state.risk.lock is` the mode lock (the held mode lock already serialises the reads) and acquires the RiskState lock only when it is a distinct object
- Applied to all three call sites (`reconcile`, `evaluate_risk`, `apply_health_and_risk`)

The v0.68.0 unit tests missed this because they leave `state.risk.lock` unset (`None` → `nullcontext`); only the shared-lock launcher wiring triggers it.

## Tests

Full suite: 1505 passed. New `test_shared_lock_wiring_does_not_deadlock` drives `reconcile` / `evaluate_risk` / `apply_health_and_risk` under the shared-lock wiring and asserts they complete rather than hang. Verified end-to-end against Praxis `feat/live-safety`: the boot/shutdown repro no longer deadlocks and the previously-failing `/healthz`-during-shutdown tests pass.

author: philipflipflop
body:
Four fixes across three commits. Full physics/world suite (133 tests) passes; production build is green.

## 1. A320 flight model + autopilot (`bd384ad`)

The pitch weathervane spring pulled AoA toward **zero**, but trimmed flight needs positive AoA. A 2.5g transport (pitch authority capped at ~0.13 rad/s by the G-limit) burned ~¾ of full stick just holding level, nosed over hands-off (crashed from 800 m in <30 s), and under the AP a routine 30°-bank climb saturated the pitch loop and descended into terrain.

- **Autotrim**: new `trimAoA` state — the stab centres the pitch spring on the 1g trim AoA for current speed/flaps, like the real A320's normal law (FBW airframes retrim at 2.5/s, conventional ones at trim-wheel 0.5/s).
- Trim washes out with bank (as the real normal law does past 33°), fades below 30 m AGL (the A320 freezes trim below 100 ft RA) so flares still end in landings, and parks at zero on the ground.
- Result: the AP flies a climbing 30° turn at exactly the commanded V/S from any speed; hands-off cruise sags ~70 m in 90 s instead of diving in.
- `tests/16` pins hands-off path stability and the AP climb+turn that previously flew into the ground.

## 2. "Rubber-banding" wobble (`bd384ad`)

The turbulence shaker applied fixed-frequency sine gusts at constant amplitude regardless of airspeed — a 400 kt jet rocked in the same metronomic ~1.4 s rhythm as a 60 kt trainer, which reads as elastic rubber-banding.

- Gust response now scales with the gust/airspeed ratio (fast aircraft punch through chop that bounces a trainer).
- The sines are amplitude-modulated by slow incommensurate envelopes so no regular beat survives.
- Default intensity 0.7 → 0.45. Cruise is near-glassy; final approach stays alive.

## 3. A320 visual pass (`b6ad649`)

- Windshield rebuilt as **four glass panes wrapped onto the nose** as arcs of a cone following the hull's own taper, 5 cm proud, with white hull showing through as pillar frames — the old squashed-ellipsoid crown only broke the surface as two blobs either side of the nose.
- Added the signature wing-body belly fairing, flap-track canoe fairings, spine/keel blade antennas, and an APU exhaust pipe.

## 4. International airports: realism + dispersion (`a6e9fe6`)

**Dispersion**: the three internationals were hand-placed and *no others ever generated* — fly past the home region and the map went hub-less. Hubs now generate on a **120 km supercell grid** (deterministic; up to 8 jittered sites probed per supercell for a flat, dry twin-runway footprint — ~36 hubs per 1,900×1,900 km scan). Jitter is capped so a hub sits ≥32 km inside its own supercell, keeping the `heightAt` hot path at one extra cache lookup. Procedural hubs get the full treatment automatically: twin parallels, four ILS approaches, terminal spine, gates, parked traffic, chart symbol. Verified in-game by panning the nav chart ~430 km east and finding EASTBANK INTL among a spread of regionals.

**Realism** — all through the shared `intlBuildings` list so rendering and rotated-box collision stay in lockstep (every building is exactly as solid as it looks):
- Cargo terminals at the north end, multi-storey car parks on the landside spine, a three-tank fuel farm behind the hangars — each new kind with its own crash reason.
- Taxiway system: inner apron taxilane behind the stand rows, connectors extended to join lane → parallel → runway.
- Ground life: crew buses lapping the apron service lanes (4 moving vehicles, was 2) and baggage-cart trains at the pier roots.

`tests/06` pins the hub grid: coverage, flat paved parallels at their own headings, determinism, and the 14 km strip berth.

body:
Closes the last open item on #35 — "bound JSON depth on the public API input path".

## Finding: the public JSON paths are already bounded
`serde_json` enforces a built-in **128-level recursion cap**, and **production code never calls `disable_recursion_limit()`** to remove it (the only caller is a test — see below). So deeply-nested request JSON is already rejected cleanly, not a crash. Verified against a live server:

```
POST /graphql   body = {"query":"{__typename}","variables":[[[ …300 levels… ]]]}
→ HTTP 400  "recursion limit exceeded at line 1 column 163"
→ server still healthy (200) afterward
```

So there was no live DoS; the risk in #35 was that the `unbounded_depth` feature *could* be misused on a production path.

## Change
- Adds **`tests/hurl/security/json_depth.hurl`** (300-level nested body → 400), validated live and passing alongside the other five guards under `rake test_security`.
- **Keeps** the `unbounded_depth` feature — a test parses the trusted, compile-time-embedded bin_prot `external_transition` layout (`tests/protocol/fixtures/`), which legitimately nests past 128 levels, using `serde_stacker` for stack safety. `Cargo.toml` now documents **why it's safe** and that production must never call `disable_recursion_limit()` on untrusted input.

No production code change — behavior was already correct; this proves it and guards against regression. (Cargo.toml diff is comment-only; `Cargo.lock` unchanged.)

With this, **#35 is complete** (7/7).

body:
Follow-up to #409's review reflection, closing the flagged side discovery: the CLIENT response parser (`http_parse_head`) accepted `Content-Length: +3` via bare `parse::<usize>()` — the same RFC 9112 §6.2 differential fixed on the server side in #409 (a21bcf3). Response-CL framing feeds the keepalive pool's reuse verdict, so a permissive parse is a framing hazard, not a nicety.

- Applies the identical digits-only pre-check the server parser uses (empty or any non-ASCII-digit byte → `Invalid`).
- Swept the file for other bare `parse::<...>()` on untrusted wire bytes: status-code parses are already digit-guarded; the authority port parse reads a caller-supplied outgoing URL (not wire framing); CLI/test-harness parses are out of scope. No other holes.
- Regression test: `+3` → Invalid; plain `3` still parses.

`cargo test --workspace` **1720 green**, clippy clean at `-D warnings`.

author: marcelxpfeifer
body:
Part of the **2026-07-10 experience plan** (Sending Transports epic). Implements **locked decisions #1 & #2**: transport is instance-level (own MTA / SES / SMTP relay), and the long tail is a single generic SMTP relay with provider presets — no per-provider API adapters.

The backend `smtp` send adapter, the `SMTP_RELAY_*` env keys, and their inclusion in `CONVEX_RUNTIME_ENV_KEYS` already shipped; this PR makes the **setup wizard** actually offer and validate an SMTP relay, end to end.

## What changed
- **Wizard composable** (`useSetupWizard.ts`) — `ProviderChoice` gains `smtp`; `EmailStepDraft` carries an `SmtpRelayDraft`; `validateEmailStep` / `buildProviderEnv` / `PROVIDER_ENV_KEYS` / `PROVIDER_LABELS` / `buildSetupSummary` all carry the relay fields into an `EMAIL_PROVIDER=smtp` + `SMTP_RELAY_*` env patch. New exported `SMTP_RELAY_PRESETS` (Mailgun / Postmark / SendGrid / Brevo / Custom) prefill host/port/TLS.
- **Email step page** (`setup/email.vue`) — fourth "SMTP relay" option with a preset select + host/port/TLS/username/password form; a named preset locks the host to its documented submission endpoint, Custom leaves it editable. Step copy reframed as an honest choice (own MTA / Amazon SES / SMTP relay). Uses only FF design tokens + `UiSelect`/`UiInput`; error state wired.
- **Live validation** — `/api/setup/validate-provider` gains an `smtp` branch backed by a new shared `validateSmtpRelay`, which opens a real SMTP submission connection (implicit TLS or STARTTLS), runs EHLO + an AUTH exchange, and **sends no message**. SSRF-guarded (reuses `isBlockedSsrfHost`) and bounded by a per-step timeout, mirroring the existing PostHog-host check. Clear operator-facing error strings.
- **setup-cli parity** — `SendingConfig` + `parseSending` + `buildEnvPatchFromConfig` accept `provider: 'smtp'`; `validators.ts` re-exports `validateSmtpRelay`; the terminal wizard gains an SMTP-relay branch with the same presets and live handshake. No compose profile change — a relay is external, so `getActiveProfiles` correctly adds no `mta` service.
- **Docs** — supported send-provider kinds + factory layout updated; setup-cli guide describes the three-way choice with live validation.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] Fourth "SMTP relay" provider option with Mailgun/Postmark/SendGrid/Brevo/Custom presets prefilling host/port/TLS
- [x] Credential form (username, password) beneath the preset
- [x] smtp fields flow through `ProviderChoice` / `EmailStepDraft` / `validateEmailStep` / `buildProviderEnv` / `PROVIDER_ENV_KEYS` → `EMAIL_PROVIDER=smtp` + `SMTP_RELAY_*`
- [x] Real validation before apply: SMTP handshake + AUTH check with bounded timeout and clear errors
- [x] Step copy reframed as an honest own-MTA / SES / SMTP-relay choice
- [x] setup-cli `validators.ts` + config accept `EMAIL_PROVIDER=smtp` (no compose profile change)
- [x] Provider-choice docs updated
- [x] Vitest: presets fill correctly, missing creds block, env patch shape, SSRF/port guards

## Preserved behavior
- Existing provider choices (own MTA, Resend, SES, receive-only "none") and their live-validation and env paths are untouched; Resend remains a listed option.
- `apply.post.ts`'s delivery-provider floor already accepts `smtp` via `isDeliveryProviderKind` — no change needed.
- Wizard navigation, Back/return-with-values seeding, and the required-provider gate all survive; the smtp draft is seeded back from env on return.
- No new env reads outside `lib/env.ts`; `SMTP_RELAY_*` were already runtime-pushed.

## Test notes
Vitest only (CI gate — not run locally per pipeline rules). Added: composable smtp validation + env-patch cases, setup-cli `buildEnvPatchFromConfig`/`parseSending` smtp cases, and `validateSmtpRelay` input-guard tests that return before any socket opens (no network in CI).

Auto-merge pipeline: squash-merges on reviewer approval + green CI.

author: reuvenharrison
body:
Fixes #1017 (the response side, gap 2, landed with #1092; this adds gap 1, parameters).

## Problem
A request parameter flipping between `type: [string, "null"]` and `type: string` was silent in both directions: the null-only type change transition claims the raw parameter type change, and no parameter reporter existed for the type-array or nullable-keyword forms. The removal direction is a breaking change (the request no longer accepts null), so this was a missed breaking report, not just the changelog gap the issue described.

Before:
```
oasdiff breaking base.yaml revision.yaml
No breaking changes to report, but the specs are different.
```
After:
```
error   [request-parameter-became-not-nullable]
        in API GET /t
                the `query` request parameter `q` became not nullable
```

## Changes
- New rules, localized in all four locales:
  - `request-parameter-became-nullable` (INFO) / `request-parameter-became-not-nullable` (ERR)
  - `request-parameter-property-became-nullable` (INFO) / `request-parameter-property-became-not-nullable` (ERR)
- Emitted through the shared `nullabilityChange` classifier, so all three nullable forms are covered at once (the `nullable` keyword, the type array, the oneOf wrapping), same as bodies and properties.
- With dedicated parameter reporters, the nullable wrapping on a parameter now reports `became-(not-)nullable` instead of the parameter list-of-types findings that stood in for it (the transitions table swap the table's design anticipated). All levels now report nullability the same way.
- The classifier guards against a schema present on one side only (the parameter path doesn't pre-filter those like the body walkers do).
- NULLABILITY.md's parameter paragraph simplified accordingly.

## Tests
The type-array case is pinned in both directions for a parameter and a parameter property; the wrap matrix tests now expect the dedicated parameter findings.

author: ajoe
body:
## The problem

Fixes YunoHost/issues#2753

Since `BaseOption` uses `use_enum_values = True`, pydantic stores `option.type` as the plain string value, so the three identity comparisons against `OptionType` enum members in `src/utils/configpanel.py` are always `False` on YunoHost 13:

- `option.type is OptionType.file` in `_get_partial_raw_settings_and_mutate_config()`: the intended exemption for `file` questions never triggers, so **any app config panel containing a `file` question whose bound file does not exist yet fails to load** with `Config panel question 'X' should be initialized with a value during install or upgrade.` — as reported in the issue for `vpnclient`. I hit the exact same thing with `wireguard_client` on 13.0.4: adding an interface via the panel works once, and afterwards the panel can no longer be opened because the interface's `.conf` file hasn't been uploaded yet.
- `option.type is OptionType.password` in `_get_config()`: password values are **no longer masked** in `config get` output.
- `option.type is OptionType.button` in `ConfigPanelModel.get_options_with_trigger()`: button options are no longer yielded for their `action` trigger.

## Solution

Use `==` instead of `is`. Since `OptionType` is a `str`-based Enum, equality works whether the stored value is a plain `str` (current behaviour with `use_enum_values`) or an actual enum member.

Verified on a YunoHost 13.0.4 instance: with this change the `wireguard_client` config panel loads again.

## Summary Introduces a shared `ComedySession` owned by `Director` and exposed on `ModeContext`, so callback memory and quality gating are no longer isolated to `ImprovMode`. - **`ComedySession`** (`src/comedy/ComedySession.ts`): `recordJoke()`, `suggestCallback()`, `rateAndMaybeRetry()`, theme extraction, and callback detection - **`modeConfig.ts`**: `ModeDefinition` + `isComedyEnabled()` — default-on for improv/performance/interactive families; opt-out via `scenario.config.comedyEnabled` or absurd-mode overrides - **Director lifecycle**: resets comedy state on `playScenario()` start and `stopScene()` end; injects callback prompts in `processTurn()` - **Mode wiring**: Improv refactored to use shared session; Performance (roast/standup/debate) and Interactive (trial/trivia) use `chatForAgentWithComedy` / `processTurnWithComedy` helpers - **UI**: callback status badges (`fresh` / `building` / `peak`) in chat via `src/ui/callbackBadge.ts` + CSS ## Acceptance criteria - [x] Improv + Performance + Interactive share `CallbackEngine` via `ctx.comedy` - [x] Scene stop clears callback state (`ComedySession.reset()` → `resetGlobalCallbackEngine()`) - [x] Director `processTurn()` injects callback theme prompts (`suggestCallback()`) - [x] Quality gate stays cheap/sync (`rateJoke()` only; no blocking async on hot path) ## Notes - `chatForAgent` paths use `chatForAgentWithComedy()` since they bypass `Director.processTurn()` - Absurd/dream modes remain opt-in unless listed in performance/interactive sets or explicitly enabled in config - Wire `onCallbackRecorded` → `window.attachComedyCallbackBadge` when instantiating `Director` for live badge updates ## Test plan - [x] `npx tsc --noEmit` passes - [ ] Manual: start improv/roast/trial scene, verify callback prompts appear in Director turns - [ ] Manual: stop scene, confirm callback state resets on next scene start
  
## Summary by CodeRabbit * **New Features** * Added comedy callback tracking across supported scene types. * Introduced callback suggestions, joke quality handling, and improved comedic continuity during scenes. * Added callback status badges to chat messages, with visual states for callback progress. * Updated trial, trivia, stand-up, debate, improv, and autonomous scenes to use the enhanced comedy flow. * **Bug Fixes** * Improved scene stopping and reset behavior for comedy tracking. * Added safeguards to stop scripted interactions cleanly when a scene ends.

author: xuehaipan
body:
#### Issue Type

- Bug fix
- Improvement/feature implementation

#### Runtime Environment

Examples and tooling change; validated in these environments:

- Operating system and version: Ubuntu (4× NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3); macOS for lint / format
- Python version: `3.12.3`
- `nvitop` version or commit: `feat/examples-improvements` (this branch)
- Locale: `en_US.UTF-8`

#### Description

Two improvements to `examples/`, split into two commits.

**Enrich the colored monitor** (`monitor-colored`):

- Host summary line (`[Host]`: CPU / memory / swap / load) via `nvitop.host`.
- Two-column device panel with memory-usage percentages.
- White device name against green `[CUDA/NVML]` and total-memory tags.
- Wider PID column for 7-digit PIDs; CPU% now handles multi-threaded processes (>100%).
- Per-process GPU memory-bandwidth (`GMBW%`) column.
- Title-case the labels in `monitor-minimal` and drop its redundant total-memory line.

**Run scripts via `uv` from a URL, no clone** (all runnable examples):

- Add PEP 723 inline metadata (`requires-python` + `dependencies`) to the 8 runnable examples, so each runs straight from its URL:

  ```text
  uv run https://github.com/XuehaiPan/nvitop/raw/HEAD/examples/<dir>/<script>.py
  ```

- Each script's docstring and README now shows the `uv run` invocation. For the collector examples this replaces the `pip install -r requirements.txt` + `python3 …` steps with a single command.
- `ml-framework-callbacks` are `Callback` classes with no entry point, so they are left untouched.
- Add `uv` and `tensorboard` to the spelling wordlist.

#### Motivation and Context

Closes #221 — the `monitor-colored` example now surfaces `SM Clock` and `Memory Clock` on dedicated rows that are never truncated, providing the always-visible clock readout that issue asked for. The `nvitop` TUI's width-based truncation is intentional and left unchanged; this gives users a clock-visible alternative.

`uv run` support lets anyone try an example with a single command and zero setup — no clone, and no manual `pip install` for the examples that need extra dependencies.

#### Testing

- `pre-commit` passes on all changed files (ruff, ruff-format, mypy, pylint, codespell).
- All 8 runnable scripts pass `python3 -m py_compile`.
- `monitor-colored` rendered against mock devices (H100 + GB10 with `N/A` fields, 7-digit PIDs, >100% CPU) and on a real 4×H100 host.
- No runtime code outside `examples/` changed (plus two spelling-wordlist entries).

author: kishorejorige
body:
## Summary
Replaces the static proposal template (for tech jobs) with LLM-generated proposals via a local Ollama model, while keeping the static template as an automatic fallback if Ollama is unavailable.

## Changes
- Add `app/proposal/ollama_client.py` — thin wrapper around Ollama's `/api/generate`, configurable via `OLLAMA_BASE_URL` / `OLLAMA_PROPOSAL_MODEL` / `OLLAMA_TIMEOUT` env vars
- Update `generator.py`:
  - Tech jobs now get an LLM-written proposal; non-tech jobs still get the static decline template (unchanged `is_tech_job()` gating)
  - Prompt explicitly forbids fabricating past projects/clients/skills not in the job's confirmed skill list
  - `_clean_llm_output()` strips stray markdown artifacts from small local models
  - Falls back silently to the static template on any Ollama failure (unreachable, timeout, empty response) — logged as a warning, never a hard error to the caller
- Default model set to `qwen3:1.7b` with `"think": false` (disables reasoning-model chain-of-thought output, which was causing timeouts) and `temperature: 0.4` for tighter instruction-following

## Testing
- Verified tech-job proposals (Mock ids 1, 2) are accurate, non-fabricated, plain text, single signature
- Verified non-tech jobs (RemoteOK ids 3, 4) still correctly route to the static decline template
- Verified graceful fallback to static template when Ollama times out or model isn't found (tested via WSL2 dual-Ollama-instance mismatch — see notes below)

## Notes / follow-ups
- Discovered and worked around a WSL2 environment issue: a Windows-native `ollama.exe` and the Linux `ollama serve` daemon maintain separate model stores. `qwen3:1.7b` had to be pulled explicitly via `/usr/local/bin/ollama pull` to land in the store the app's HTTP API actually talks to. Worth documenting in README/CONTRIBUTING for future setup.
- Requires `qwen3:1.7b` to be pulled locally (`ollama pull qwen3:1.7b`) — not automated in setup yet.

author: judder659
body:
## Summary

Fixes the four actionable findings from the 2026-07-10 external application review.

### MODE-SPLIT-1 — execution-mode "split brain" (`forven/api_core.py`)
The trading-mode settings handler persisted a requested `trading_mode='live'` to the KV blob **before** calling `config.set_execution_mode`, which unconditionally refuses live — and the refusal was swallowed into a warning. Result: Settings displayed **live** while the runtime stayed **paper**. The runtime itself was never at risk (the read path is fail-closed); the display lied.

Now the KV mirror is written only **after** enforcement accepts, and a refusal is a loud 400 that the settings save bar surfaces as an error toast. Beta-build silent coercion to paper is unchanged. Regression tests added.

### TYPE-NAME-1 — garbage strategy type names (`forven/strategies/registry.py`)
A codegen'd strategy declaring `TYPE_NAME` as a `@property` resolved (via class-level `getattr`) to the property **object**, and `str()` smuggled `"<property object at 0x...>"` into the catalog the Strategy Creator renders. `register_type` now validates that the name is an identifier-shaped string (`[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]{0,63}`), routed through the existing skip/quarantine flow with a precise diagnostic ("declare it as a class attribute string"). All 76 builtin TYPE_NAMEs and the `imported__<module>` convention pass unchanged. New test file covers the property-object repro end to end through `discover()`.

### E2E-1 — honest e2e suite (`frontend/`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml`)
`test:e2e` ran Playwright with `--pass-with-no-tests` over an **empty** e2e directory — pure theater in CI. Now:
- flag removed; a real smoke suite exists (`frontend/e2e/smoke.spec.ts`)
- the suite boots the **real** backend (`python -m forven.api`) with an isolated throwaway `FORVEN_HOME` and the new `FORVEN_API_CONTROL_PLANE_ONLY=1` switch (skips scheduler/agent/brain/daemon loops for deterministic, network-quiet runs) behind the vite dev proxy on a non-default port (8017) so it can never touch a real install or collide with a dev instance
- scenarios: backend health, fresh-install canonical mode = paper, app shell renders with the risk disclaimer, live-mode request rejected AND never persisted (exercises MODE-SPLIT-1 over real HTTP), paper round-trip
- CI frontend job gains a Python setup step for the e2e backend

Follow-ups (not in this PR): strategy create→backtest→gate, emergency-halt, and restart/recovery e2e scenarios.

### Drifted backend test (`tests/test_agent_backtesting_tools.py`)
`test_agent_run_backtest_persists_result_and_syncs_strategy` failed because its fake backtest result predates the degeneracy-aware best-of rule: real `backtest_strategy` output always carries `in_sample`/`out_of_sample` blocks, and a missing `in_sample` block reads as a zero-IS-trades degenerate slice that never promotes. The fake now mirrors the real contract (with a comment explaining why).

### ALERT-STACK-1 — position-alert pile-up (`PositionAlertWidget.svelte`)
Open-position alerts rendered one card per position with no cap, burying the Risk/Data panels under 8+ cards. Now one card shows and the rest collapse behind an "N more positions open" expand/collapse bar.

## Testing
- Backend: 76 tests across the 8 affected/adjacent files pass (incl. 3 new MODE-SPLIT-1 regressions + 5 new TYPE_NAME tests); ruff clean
- Frontend: 409 unit tests pass; svelte-check 0 errors (2 pre-existing warnings)
- E2E: all 5 smoke tests pass locally against the real backend + real frontend

body:
## Summary
- Rewrite the nightly `differential` job to get its toolchain from `jdx/mise-action@v2`, reading the existing `mise.toml` pins (rust 1.96.1, cargo-nextest 0.9.140, z3 4.16.0, cvc5 1.3.4) — replacing `dtolnay/rust-toolchain` + `taiki-e/install-action` in that job only.
- Add the missing differential coverage: a step running `cargo nextest run -p shinri-solver --features oracle` — the z3/cvc5 differential oracle suite that previously never ran in CI.
- Keep both existing proptest steps verbatim (`PROPTEST_CASES: '4000'`); the `test` job is untouched.
- Hardening (deviates from the design doc's job-level env, explicitly approved at review): `GITHUB_TOKEN` is scoped to the mise-action step only (needed for mise's GitHub-release backend resolving z3/cvc5), so the cargo steps that execute third-party build scripts never see it; workflow-level `permissions: contents: read` caps the default token at least privilege.

Design doc: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-10-differential-ci-mise-z3.md` (b3456c3).

## Verification
- Exact CI command pre-verified locally under the same mise-pinned toolchain: `cargo nextest run -p shinri-solver --features oracle` → **387 passed / 0 failed / 2 skipped**, exit 0.
- YAML parse + structural check: `differential` step `uses:`/`runs:` lists match the design exactly; `test` job byte-untouched; token only on the mise-action step; `permissions: {contents: read}`.
- Reviewed task-level and whole-branch (including a permissions audit of every `test`-job step under read-only token): ready to merge, 0 critical/important findings.
- Note: the job is gated on `schedule`, so the workflow itself first runs at the next nightly (03:00 UTC) — the local green run above is the pre-merge substitute.

## Deferred follow-ups (deliberately not in this PR)
