author: shavindra
body:
## What

Adds `.github/workflows/pr-title.yml` — a CI check that fails a PR when its title is not a valid Conventional Commit subject.

## Why

The PR title becomes the squash-merge subject on the default branch, so a malformed title puts a non-conforming commit straight onto `develop`. AGENTS.md already required Conventional Commits for PR titles ("The PR title must itself be a valid Conventional Commit subject … a non-conforming title breaks the convention on the default branch"), but no workflow enforced it. This closes that gap without adding a separate rule set — the check reuses the repo's own `commitlint.config.js`, so what CI enforces stays byte-for-byte aligned with the local `commit-msg` hook.

## How

- New workflow mirrors `branch-name.yml` for consistency:
  - same triggers (`opened`, `reopened`, `edited`, `synchronize` — re-checks when the title is edited),
  - same SHA-pinned actions (`actions/checkout@9c091bb`, `actions/setup-node@48b55a0`, Node 24, `cache: npm`),
  - same minimal permissions (`contents: read`).
- The title is read via `env: PR_TITLE: ${{ github.event.pull_request.title }}` and piped to `commitlint` through `printf '%s' "$PR_TITLE"` — never inlined into the shell step. A title crafted with backticks / `$(...)` therefore stays a data payload and cannot re-enter the shell.

## Verification

Ran commitlint locally with the repo's config against representative titles:

| Title | Result |
|---|---|
| `ci(hooks): validate PR title against conventional commits` | ✅ exit 0 |
| `Add PR title check` (no type) | ❌ exit 1 — `subject may not be empty` / `type may not be empty` |
| `wip(chrome): thing` (bad type) | ❌ exit 1 — `type must be one of [build, chore, ci, docs, feat, fix, perf, refactor, revert, style, test]` |
| `feat(x): thing\`; echo PWNED` (injection attempt) | Handled as literal string — no shell re-parse, no `PWNED` in the log |

Also updates AGENTS.md so the enforcement point is named alongside the branch-name gates.

## Note on the merged base

Both prior clean-up PRs (`#166`, `#167`) landed on `develop` before this one, so this branch already has the enforced hooks locally — every commit here passed through them without `--no-verify`.

author: franctech-com
body:
The mesh fragmented at 6-8 players: on any transient ICE failure the client called closePeer() and permanently dropped that pair with no reconnect path, so the graph collapsed to a small connected core (the "only three connect") while other devices ended up with zero peers and showed "waiting for others to join". A discovery race (a peer stuck on the mic-permission prompt) could also miss the initial JOIN.

Rewrite the mesh for reliability, client-side only (the signalling DTO already supports JOIN/LEAVE/OFFER/ANSWER/ICE + toUserId):
- PERFECT NEGOTIATION (deterministic polite/impolite per pair via userId) so simultaneous offers no longer wedge a connection; driven by onnegotiationneeded with implicit rollback on the polite side.
- ICE RESTART on a failed connection (up to 3 tries) instead of dropping the peer — a transient TURN/NAT blip now self-heals.
- PERIODIC RE-ANNOUNCE (JOIN heartbeat every 12s) so missed or previously dropped peers are rediscovered and reconnect; steady-state stays quiet (already-connected peers ignore the heartbeat).

frontend tsc clean. Web-only as before (native unaffected).

author: raulpfo
body:
Closes #35 

## Que cambia

El grafo de dependencias del reporte HTML deja de renderizarse con Mermaid (estatico, sin zoom/pan ni resaltado) y pasa a usar [vis-network](https://visjs.github.io/vis-network/), embebido inline en el HTML generado:

- **Zoom/pan y arrastre de nodos**: soportados de forma nativa por vis-network (`interaction: {dragNodes, dragView, zoomView}`).
- **Resaltado al hacer hover**: al pasar el raton sobre un servicio se atenua (`opacity`) el resto de nodos/aristas no conectados y se engrosa el trazo de las aristas conectadas; al salir se restaura.
- **Anomalias visualmente distinguibles en el propio grafo** (antes solo en las tablas aparte):
  - Naranja: servicio con endpoint(s) huerfano(s).
  - Rojo: servicio con version desactualizada (Spring Boot o dependencia).
  - Morado: ambas anomalias a la vez.
  - Nodo diamante gris + arista roja punteada: consumidor sin destino resuelto (antes invisible en el grafo).
- **Reporte auto-contenido**: la libreria vis-network (~640 KB, minificada, dual MIT/Apache-2.0) se vendoriza en `spring-analyzer-reporter/src/main/resources/static/vis-network.min.js` y se inyecta inline en el HTML junto con el JSON del grafo, sin ningun `<script src="...">` externo (mejora respecto al Mermaid anterior, que dependia de un CDN).

`GraphDataRenderer` sustituye a `MermaidGraphRenderer`: construye `GraphNode`/`GraphEdge` a partir del `DependencyGraph` y las anomalias de version (`VersionAnomalyDetector`), y los serializa a JSON con Jackson. El JSON se embebe en un `<script type="application/json">` escapando `</` para evitar que un nombre de servicio/endpoint pueda cerrar prematuramente la etiqueta.

## Fuera de alcance

- No se anaden filtros interactivos por tipo de anomalia ni exportacion de imagen del grafo (no estaban en los criterios de aceptacion del issue).
- No se cambia el formato de reporte Markdown (solo existe el HTML actualmente).

## Tests

- `GraphDataRendererTest`: nodos/aristas para grafo vacio, nodo normal, arista con etiqueta metodo+path, nodo en grupo `orphan`/`outdated`/`both` segun anomalias, arista de consumo huerfano hacia nodo sintetico `unknown` (con y sin `targetService` conocido, agrupando los de destino desconocido bajo un unico nodo).
- `HtmlReportGeneratorTest`: el `<script id="graph-data">` contiene los nodos/aristas esperados; la libreria vis-network se embebe inline y no hay ningun `script[src]` externo.
- `EndToEndAnalysisTest` (spring-analyzer-boot): actualizado para verificar el JSON del grafo en vez del texto Mermaid.

## Verificacion manual

Generé un reporte de muestra con datos representativos (incluyendo las tres anomalias) y lo cargué en Chromium headless (Playwright): el grafo renderiza sin errores de consola, la libreria `vis` esta disponible como global, y el hover/zoom disparan sin excepciones. Captura:

- Nodo `order-service` en naranja (endpoint huerfano), `user-service` en rojo (version desactualizada) con tooltip nativo, `billing-service` como diamante gris (destino no resuelto) conectado con arista roja.

author: bewithgaurav
body:
### Work Item / Issue Reference

> ADO Work Item: Fixed [AB#47261](https://sqlclientdrivers.visualstudio.com/c6d89619-62de-46a0-8b46-70b92a84d85e/_workitems/edit/47261)

-------------------------------------------------------------------
### Summary

the subprocess shutdown/teardown tests in `test_013_SqlHandle_free_shutdown` and `test_024_context_manager_transaction` intermittently segfault on the qemu-emulated linux arm64 CI legs and force reruns. the crash is a latent use-after-free in odbc handle-teardown ordering (an unclosed DBC handle finalized by gc at interpreter shutdown after the process-lifetime ENV handle is gone, so `SQLFreeHandle` touches freed ENV memory); it is benign on native hardware and only turns fatal under qemu's page reuse plus altered gc timing, which is why it is flaky and clears on rerun.

test-only, two changes:

- fix `is_qemu_emulated()` in `conftest.py`. the old check only matched `CPU implementer 0x51`, which never appears under `multiarch/qemu-user-static` (the emulated aarch64 process sees the x86_64 host's `/proc/cpuinfo`, which has no arm implementer field). it now flags an aarch64 process when cpuinfo advertises implementer `0x51` (qemu-system) or lacks the arm-only `CPU implementer` field entirely (qemu-user host passthrough); native arm64 and x86 stay unflagged. the existing `test_013` skip was dead because of this and now takes effect.
- add a class-level `skipif(QEMU)` to `test_024`'s `TestContextManagerCommit` (all 24 cases run the subprocess-teardown path).

the conftest docstring documents the underlying teardown-order uaf as the known-failure case. that root-cause bug is tracked separately and is unaffected by this skip; native legs still run these tests, so a regression there is not masked.

Arc **A4** of the PL flow spec — delivered as the *safe* variant.

`_loanRenderKyc` now shows three labelled sections — **Identity · Income · Address & documents** — via `_loanKycSection()`, so the long KYC screen reads as clear steps instead of one wall of inputs.

## Why this variant
The spec's A4 splits KYC into 3 separate *screens*. But that screen holds **income + employment — the inputs that feed the BRE** — and `_loanKycAndOffer` reads ~15 fields straight from the DOM. A true screen-split means fields live on different screens, so the submit would need rewiring to read from persisted state — a real regression risk **on the money path**.

author: exitstatus
body:
`images/down.png` appears to the left of the signal bars whenever something is
being fetched over WiFi, and clears when it finishes.

## What counts as "fetching"

Each of the three network users gained a `Busy()`:

- **WeatherApi** — current conditions, forecast, and the condition-icon download.
- **NewsApi** — the RSS feed.
- **NtpClient** — a sync that has been asked for and not yet answered.

`Busy()` is a plain `bool`, not a locked read. It is one aligned word, written by
a worker task and read by the loop thread, and a value one frame stale costs
nothing on a display that repaints at 20 fps.

### NTP needed different treatment

There is no call to sit inside: `configTzTime()` starts a background SNTP poller
and returns immediately. Polling `sntp_get_sync_status()` does not work either --
`SNTP_SYNC_STATUS_COMPLETED` is reset back to `RESET` the moment the sync lands
(the header says so explicitly), so a loop that does not happen to look inside
that window never observes it at all.

It uses `sntp_set_time_sync_notification_cb()` instead, re-registered after each
`configTzTime()` because that call reinitialises the service. A 15 s timeout
closes out a sync that never answers, so an unreachable server cannot leave the
arrow stuck on forever.

## Repaint

A fetch can begin and end between two minute rollovers, so the arrow gets its own
term in the repaint gate. Without it the icon would appear late, and with
`blink_colon = off` it would often never be drawn at all.

## The Icon class

Ported from the WeatherS3 project. Three changes were needed to build here:

- It defined its own `PNG decoder`. `src/WeatherIcon.cpp` already defines one, so
  that would be a duplicate symbol -- and the object is ~40 KB, which we cannot
  afford twice. It now shares the existing decoder. Both users decode on the loop
  thread, so no locking is needed, but nothing may decode from a worker task.
- Its draw callbacks returned `void`. PNGdec 1.1.6 declares
  `typedef int (PNG_DRAW_CALLBACK)(PNGDRAW *)`, returning 1 to continue.
- Its `ICON(...)` table named a dozen images this repo does not have.

## RenderHighQuality

The ported `Render()` uses `getAlphaMask(pDraw, mask, 255)`, which reduces alpha
to **one bit per pixel** at a threshold: a pixel on an antialiased rim is either
painted solid or dropped entirely. At 24 px the icon is mostly rim, and it read
as jagged.

`RenderHighQuality()` ignores the mask, reads the destination pixel back out of
the sprite, and alpha-blends the source over it, so a rim pixel at 40% alpha
lands as 40% of the icon colour over whatever is behind it.

`down.png` turned out to be an **indexed-palette** PNG (colour type 3) with a
`tRNS` chunk, so its per-pixel alpha is not in the pixel data at all: it is a
palette lookup at `pPalette[768 + c]`, the RGB triples occupying the first 768
bytes. Straight RGBA (colour type 6) is handled too. Any other layout falls back
to the masked draw rather than guessing at the byte order and rendering garbage.

It is slower -- a pixel at a time, with a read-back and a blend each -- which is
fine for 576 pixels drawn only while a fetch is in flight, and would not be for a
large image.

## Also

`images/down.png` was **not tracked by git**. It is added in this branch;
without it `board_build.embed_files` points at a file a fresh clone would not
have, and the build fails at link.

Cost: RAM +144 bytes, flash +3 KB.

## Verified

Both environments build. The linker emits `_binary_images_down_png_start/_end`
with `_binary_images_down_png_size` = 0x4e8 = 1256 bytes, matching the file. On
hardware the arrow appears during the boot NTP sync and weather fetch, clears
when they finish, and the blended edge is visibly cleaner than the masked one.

Not covered: the arrow during a *failing* fetch (the 8-10 s timeout path), and
the NTP 15 s timeout actually firing.

author: bartlett-ops
body:
## Summary

Fixes the bug where a replaced pod strands a user's old CIDR in the allowlist forever.

Two flaws compounded, both confirmed read-only against the live cluster:

1. **The ConfigMap was sharded by pod hostname.** `sphinx-users` held exactly one key, `sphinx-585dcdf6f8-4frvs`, while the running pod was `sphinx-86b5c85949-vk5zv`. A new pod reads only its own key, finds nothing, and starts empty — the previous pod's records are orphaned but its CIDRs stay in the middleware.
2. **The middleware was an append-only accumulator.** `unionStrings` merged new CIDRs into the existing `sourceRange`, so nothing was ever removed. Live proof: 2 CIDRs, 1 user record.

The redesign makes the middleware a **derived projection** of a single authoritative store, rather than a mutable accumulator. Records are keyed by email, so a user has exactly one CIDR by construction; re-authenticating replaces it.

## Design

- One shared ConfigMap document (`users.json`), keyed by email, not by pod. Multiple replicas share it safely.
- Compare-and-swap on `resourceVersion` with bounded retry and backoff. Server-Side Apply is gone — it was the root cause of the pod-sharded keys.
- Every write to the middleware **replaces** `sourceRange` with the full projection of the store. Stale CIDRs cannot survive a reconcile.
- A generation counter, stamped on the middleware as an annotation, prevents a slow pod from writing a stale projection over a newer one. The guard is *strictly older* — an equal generation proceeds, which is what lets the background loop repair drift.
- The generation is scoped to a **store lineage UID**. Without it, recreating the ConfigMap restarts the counter and every subsequent write is skipped, wedging the allowlist permanently.
- A background reconcile loop repairs drift; a write-skip cache keeps the hot `/auth` path (which Traefik ForwardAuth fires on *every* HTTP request) from hammering the API server.
- Migration converts the legacy pod-sharded layout in place. If two legacy keys disagree about a user's IP, that user is dropped and must re-authenticate — guessing would be worse than a re-login.

Expiry is deliberately out of scope; records persist indefinitely.

## Also fixed

- **`--trusted-proxies` constrained nothing.** The old code read the leftmost `X-Forwarded-For` entry verbatim, so any caller could choose which CIDR got allowlisted. Now resolved through gin's `ClientIP()`, which honours the trusted-proxy set. A startup warning fires when the set is empty or catch-all (`0.0.0.0/0`, `::/0`), because gin then trusts every hop and falls through to the client-controlled leftmost entry.
- **IPv4/IPv6 host CIDRs.** `net/netip` with `Unmap()`, so `/32` for v4 (including v4-mapped-v6) and `/128` for v6.
- **`/ready` no longer lies.** It requires both a recent successful reconcile *and* live Gets against the middleware and ConfigMap. Freshness alone leaves a 3-interval window where a pod whose API access just broke still reports ready.
- **Graceful shutdown.** `http.Server.Shutdown` on SIGTERM instead of blocking in `router.Run`, which served auth traffic against a frozen reconciler until the kubelet killed the pod.
- `make dev` now targets scratch resources. It previously pointed at the production middleware with `0.0.0.0/0`.

## Verification

Unit tests throughout, validated by mutation testing — flipping the generation guard to `<=`, caching before `Apply` succeeds, deleting the reconcile cache rebuild, forcing `migrated()` true, and resolving the leftmost XFF entry were each introduced deliberately, and each was caught.

End-to-end against a live cluster using **scratch resources only**; production was never mutated and was verified unchanged afterwards. Confirmed: migration with the conflicting-IP drop, stale CIDR pruning, re-auth removing the old CIDR, drift repair at equal generation, the lineage-wedge scenario, `/ready` returning 503 the instant the middleware is deleted, and a clean exit 0 on SIGTERM.

## Deployment note

The live `sphinx-allowlist` currently holds an unbacked `192.168.x.x/32` left over by `unionStrings`. The initial reconcile will prune it. That is correct, but it is a real access change — whoever owns that address will need to re-authenticate.

## RBAC

Now requires `get, create, update` on both `middlewares` and `configmaps`.

author: piiidosu
body:
This PR fixes a bug in early difficulty reduction for the reading skill, where adding more objects in the first 60 seconds of a map can decrease difficulty.

## The Bug:

reducedNoteCount is equal to the number of objects in the first 60s. As index/reducedNoteCount was used to determine the ratio for the nerf, increasing the objects in the first 60s increases reducedNoteCount, and decreases the ratio, which increases the nerf to the object, leading to cases where adding more objects decreases difficulty.

## The Fix:

Use StartTime instead of index so that an object at a given start time will receive the same nerf regardless of the number of objects preceding or following the object.

### Notes:
This significantly nerfs short maps (shorter than 40s, see below), as the original nerf would rescale the nerf window to the length of the map if the map was shorter than 60s.
The reduction period was changed from 60s to 40s to compensate.

author: krisztiankoos
body:
## Summary — Refs #4220

Second judgment slice of the #4220 grow arc. First slice = auto_merge (**PR #4888** ledger + **#4889** adjudication); that pair is this ledger's **format precedent** (matched: row schema, precedence-partition buckets, seeded sampling gate, documented deviations, reject=0).

**Scope (verified):** the **7,182** `needs_review` records whose `reason` is *exactly* `'unresolved pos'` (of 8,639 total needs_review). The 1,457 missing-definition / heritage-combo records are **out of scope** (later slices) and untouched.

**Artifact:** one file — **`data/lexicon/grow-triage-ledgers/2026-07-10-second-grow-needsreview-pos-ledger-batch.yaml`** (7,182 rows). No manifest/registry/db mutation.

> **📍 Location correction (vs the task brief):** the brief said `source-inventory-review-decisions/`, but that path is now **stale** — PR **#4893** relocated grow-kind ledgers to `data/lexicon/grow-triage-ledgers/` because the decisions dir is schema-validated (`atlas_source_inventory_review_decisions`) and a grow-kind file there turns main red for every subsequent code PR (the #4888/#4889 → #4893 incident). This PR is **rebased onto current main** and lands the ledger in the correct dir per that dir's README contract. (My first push, on a pre-#4893 base with the file in the old dir, correctly went red on `test_default_committed_decision_files_validate` — fixed by the relocation.)

## Root cause of "unresolved pos"

The surface strings in this bucket are predominantly **inflected FORMS** (`серйозних→серйозний`, `позіхаю→позіхати`), not headwords. The pipeline's `grow_lexicon_from_content._vesum_pos` resolves pos via a **headword-only** lookup (`verify_lemma → WHERE lemma=base`), so a surface form returns no pos → `'unresolved pos'`. This slice resolves pos via a **word_form** lookup against `data/vesum.db` (`WHERE word_form=key(surface)`), then applies the #4888 triage predicates. Cross-checked against `mcp__sources__verify_words`.

## Decision buckets (precedence partition — sums to 7,182)

| bucket | decision | n | meaning |
|---|---|---:|---|
| approve | approve | **6984** | resolved to a single coherent pos (incl. 64 benign `{adj,noun}→adj` substantivization) |
| flag:form-anomaly | deferred | 141 | comma-merged lemma pairs (`англійська,англійський`); driver splits |
| flag:not-in-vesum | deferred | 31 | proper nouns (19) + coverage-gap attested (8) + fragments (3) + unattested (1) |
| flag:pos-ambiguous | deferred | 22 | genuine cross-lemma homographs (`краю→край/краяти`); fail-closed |
| flag:formof | deferred | 2 | orthographic variants (`жоден→жодний`, `західній→західний`) |
| flag:heritage | deferred | 2 | `classification=unknown` heuristic gap (`схоже`, `шоці`) |
| | **total** | **7182** | 6984 approve / 0 reject / 198 deferred |

approve pos distribution: noun 2820 · verb 2292 · adj 1803 · numr 68 · adv 1.

## ⚠️ Headword yield (no silent inflation)

The **6984 approve ROWS cover only 3919 distinct base lemmas** — the remainder are duplicate surface forms of the same lemma (14 rows are already-headwords; 6970 are forms). **True new-headword yield ≤ 3919**, further reduced by base lemmas already registered. `base_lemma` is recorded per row; the driver's registry step **must re-key surface→base and dedup** before insert.

## reject = 0 (evidence-driven deviation)

Step 3 predicted `not-in-vesum → reject` (russian_shadow junk). The **data contradicts it**: this scope carries **zero heritage warnings** by construction (any `russian_shadow`/`calque` flag would change the reason string → out of scope). All 31 not-in-vesum words were heritage-checked (**кобета protocol**) via `search_heritage` + `query_wikipedia` and confirmed **authentic** → deferred, never rejected:
- `прийом` = Грінченко (pre-Soviet), `окраїна` = ЕСУМ, `поліцейський` = Голоскевич 1929, `спотіти`/`шепеляти`/`нічо` = Грінченко, `надоїдливий`/`світлобоязнь` = СУМ-20
- proper nouns `венеція`/`шухевич`/`сакартвело` = Wikipedia-attested
- only `непереносимість` has no attestation (russian-pattern `-имість`) — held **fail-closed** (deferred, closest to reject), driver adjudicates

(#4888's reject bucket was also empty — consistent precedent.)

## Sampling gate (#4888 pattern)

- Seed **4220**, n = **349** (5.00% of approve), **0 errors (0.00%)** — under the 2% stop threshold.
- Each sampled approve independently re-verified via a *fresh* `WHERE word_form=key` lookup (not the cached resolution) confirming `resolved_pos ∈ VESUM pos` + meaning sanity.
- MCP cross-check: `mcp__sources__verify_words` → 24/24 found, pos matches resolution 24/24.

## Validation

- YAML loads; row count == 7182 == in-scope count; decision/bucket counts reconcile with the header.
- `pytest -k "ledger or intake" -q` → **102 passed**.
- `pytest tests/test_source_inventory_review_decisions.py -q` → **13 passed** (ledger correctly lives outside the schema-validated decisions dir).

## Driver next steps

1. **RE-KEY + DEDUP** — insert each approve's `base_lemma` (not the surface form); 6984 rows collapse to 3919 distinct base lemmas, minus any already registered.
2. **Adjudicate the 198 deferred** — split the 141 comma pairs; proper-noun inclusion policy + add the 8 attested coverage-gap words with hand-set pos + normalize 3 fragments + decide `непереносимість`; pick pos for the 22 pos-ambiguous by attached gloss; 2 formof parent-resolution; 2 heritage clears.
3. Run #4532 fill-first headroom gate **before** publishing (publishing is gated).
4. Publish to atlas thin pages / practice-hub veins #4505/#4506.

**No auto-merge** — left for cross-family review + human merge.

author: pawelktk
mat-hek
body:
The main goal for this PR was to add `handle_push_error` callback, called when `push_server_event` fails. It's done, and the callback receives the last assigns passed to `update`, so it can roll back its state. Achieving this in the current state of the JS part of LLV was extremely convoluted and relied very much on the LLV internals, thus I made the following changes:
- Instead of patching fake view's methods (`pushWithReply`, etc), now we're injecting a fake transport that forwards messages to Popcorn. The transport API is not public either, but it's basically the WebSocket API, so it's simpler and less likely to change. That required some additions extending the LLV `server.ex` unfortunately, but it aligns with the original impl so maybe we can reuse it in the future?
- Instead of using `hostView.pushEvent`, we're now using a hook to push events to the server. Since LiveView freezes all updates on the hook's element until an event is ACKed by the server, we can't use the LLV's hook, as it would effectively freeze the LLV until the event is handled. Thus we have a dedicated empty `div` with a simple hook that's only job is to send events.
- The two points above made it impossible to have the `phx-target=@server`, so I removed it and `push_server_event` is the only way now. I think keeping `phx-target=@server` wasn't worth the hassle and we may figure out how to re-introduce it if it's missed.

author: grantim
body:
Replaces the self-hosted EC2 Windows Unity runner with a GitHub-hosted matrix and moves the Unity test project into the repo (test_unity/NugetTestProj).

- Matrix: windows-latest (blocking gate); ubuntu-latest / macos-latest / macos-15-intel non-blocking (continue-on-error) until proven -- together they cover the win-x64, linux-x64, osx-arm64 and osx-x64 natives shipped in the nuget package (linux-arm64 has no Unity editor to test with).
- Test project is minimal (37 files, ~130 KB): no scene, no template leftovers. The playmode test builds a 30000-vertex sphere and decimates it through the package, so the native library must load and compute. Verified locally with Unity 6000.0.79f1 (the pinned editor version) against MeshLib from nuget.org.
- The editor is installed per run by SHA-pinned buildalon/unity-setup (version from ProjectSettings/ProjectVersion.txt) -- the only third-party action, and it runs before any secret is in reach.
- License: Personal, activated by driving the official Unity.Licensing.Client bundled with the editor (--activate-ulf --include-personal on start, --return-ulf on job end) with UNITY_USERNAME / UNITY_PASSWORD secrets; the manual .ulf web flow no longer offers personal activation. Credentials pass only through this first-party step. Checkout runs with persist-credentials: false.
- A prime editor session runs before 'nugetforunity restore': on a fresh runner the NuGetForUnity asset postprocessor must be compiled into Library before the natives are imported, otherwise the plugins keep placeholder all-disabled import settings and P/Invoke fails with DllNotFoundException (reproduced locally; the EC2 runner was immune only because its Library persisted).
- Tests run via the plain Unity CLI; the step fails on Unity's exit code, the editor log prints unconditionally, results.xml + logs upload as artifacts on failure.
- AWS start/stop jobs and OIDC roles are removed. EC2 decommission is a follow-up after this proves out on a real release.

Test plan: this PR carries build-release-windows + upload-binaries (+ skip-image-rebuild), so unity-nuget-test runs the new workflow against the pr-test draft release produced by this run. The windows leg must pass; linux/macos legs are informative.

author: raphyduck
body:
## Changements

### Client AcoustID (`lib/acoustid_api.rb`)
- **Throttle** : les requêtes respectent la limite AcoustID (~3 req/s) via un intervalle minimal de 0.4 s partagé entre instances (même mécanisme que le client MusicBrainz).
- **Retry/backoff** : les échecs transitoires passent par `with_retries` ; un 429/503 avec `Retry-After` est honoré (plus de risque de ban).
- **Seuil de confiance** : plancher relevé de 0.5 à **0.85** (constante `MIN_SCORE`), configurable via `music.acoustid_min_score`. Un match sous le seuil est traité comme un échec : on n'écrit jamais une identification douteuse dans une bibliothèque propre.
- **`identify(path)`** : variante de `lookup` qui rapporte le statut (`identified` / `low_confidence` / `no_match` / `no_fingerprint`) et le score, pour le rapport de la nouvelle commande.

### Nouvelle commande `music identify` (`MusicLibrary.identify_untagged`)
Passe ciblée sur les fichiers « nus » (ni artist ni title en tags) — ceux que le matching texte MusicBrainz/iTunes ne peut pas identifier :
- **Dry-run par défaut** : rapport pur (`identifié` / `faible confiance` / `non identifié`, avec scores), aucune écriture ni déplacement.
- **`--apply=1`** : pour chaque fichier identifié avec confiance, les tags récupérés sont d'abord **écrits dans le fichier** (`TagWriter`, `only_missing` : un tag existant n'est jamais écrasé), puis le fichier est organisé dans la bibliothèque. L'écriture AVANT l'organisation est délibérée : les tags embarqués priment sur le parsing des noms, donc l'identification par empreinte l'emporte sur les noms de dossiers parasites (`-11-16`, `1966`, …).
- Les matchs sous le seuil ne sont **jamais** écrits.

### Config
- `config/conf.yml.example` : documentation de `music.acoustid_min_score` (0.85).

## Tests
- `test/lib/acoustid_api_test.rb` : +9 tests (statuts d'identify, seuil configurable, throttle, retry sur 429 avec Retry-After honoré) — 15 tests verts.
- `test/app/music_library_test.rb` : test de la passe identify (rapport dry-run, apply n'organise que le match confiant, only_missing, fichiers low/miss intouchés) — 64 tests verts.
- Suite complète : mêmes résultats que la baseline (échecs préexistants d'isolation/environnement uniquement, aucun dans les classes touchées).

## Non inclus (action hôte, hors repo)
La clé API AcoustID reste un secret local (`~/.medialibrarian/conf.yml`, `music.acoustid_key`) — jamais commitée.

Stops Dependabot from reopening the eslint 10 major bumps (#195, #202, now closed).

eslint 10 is blocked upstream: `eslint-plugin-react` (latest 7.37.5) still peer-caps at `eslint ^9.7`, and our flat config uses `react.configs.flat.recommended`, so eslint 10 can't install without `--legacy-peer-deps` against a plugin whose maintainer declares it incompatible. `eslint-plugin-react-hooks@7.1.1` already supports eslint 10, so the sole blocker is `eslint-plugin-react`.

Adds a `version-update:semver-major` ignore for `eslint` and `@eslint/js` to the root npm ecosystem entry. Minor/patch eslint 9.x bumps still flow. Revisit when eslint-plugin-react ships eslint 10 support.

author: sandstream
body:
## MCP-runtime adoption — step 2 of 5

Second increment of `pillar3-mcp-runtime-adoption-5.0.md` §5. Builds on #312 (the `[scope].enforce_runtime` opt-in).

### What changed
- **`secrets.generate` declares its honest own effect** — the `.env.local` write. So under `enforce_runtime` it's now *mediated* against the signed `[scope].fs` instead of migration-passthrough. The configured **vault CLI resolves secrets in its own subprocess**, whose network I/O is the CLI's — not kit's — and out of the exec-broker's reach (documented, like `kit_run`'s command). So `fs` is the declarable effect; egress/env are **not** falsely claimed.
- **`cwd` threaded** through `runGovernedBrokered` → `runBrokered` so the *right* project's `[scope]` governs (previously the signed source resolved against the MCP server's process cwd). All four governed ops now pass their tool `cwd`; `runGovernedBrokered`'s `context` widened to `BrokerContext` so call sites can declare effects.

### Non-breaking
Without `enforce_runtime`, everything is migration-passthrough (unchanged). The `fsWrites` declaration is inert until a signed scope opts in.

### Verification
- `tsc` clean · `eslint src` 0 errors · build clean
- Full suite **2709 pass / 0 fail** — 4 new end-to-end tests via the in-memory MCP client:
  - in-scope `.env.local` write **allowed**;
  - off-scope (`[scope].fs = ["src"]`) write **denied**;
  - `enforce_runtime` + **unsigned** → fail-closed **denied**;

author: goodmood-creator
body:
Addresses #3442; follow-up to #3443/#3444 per @Yeachan-Heo's review.

Every blocking finding from the #3444 review is addressed below.

## 1 (P1) — the advertised remediation now executes the cleanup

The merge logic is extracted into `src/installer/claude-md-merge.ts` as the single source of truth and exposed via a small `merge-claude-md` CLI entry (`src/cli/commands/merge-claude-md.ts`, built to `dist/cli/commands/merge-claude-md.js`). `scripts/setup-claude-md.sh` — what `/oh-my-claudecode:omc-setup` runs — now **delegates its CLAUDE.md merge to that entry** instead of its own bash/perl merger. So the slash setup path strips legacy guides exactly like `install()`.

It fails loudly (aborts, backup intact) if the built entry or node is missing, rather than silently falling back to a non-cleanup merge. New shell-path regressions start from both a **marked** and an **unmarked** 583-line guide and assert the file shrinks, the guide is gone, and `@USER.md` survives.

## 2 (P1) — EOL-only normalization (no more deleting edited bytes)

`normalizeTemplateLines()` now normalizes **only** line endings (CRLF/CR → LF, drop one trailing newline) — no trailing-whitespace stripping. A guide edited with Markdown hard-break trailing spaces (or a tab) no longer hashes to a historical template and is preserved. The 29 signatures were recomputed under this rule (line counts unchanged; the historical blobs happen to carry no trailing whitespace, so the fixtures still match). Regressions cover both the hard-break-spaces and trailing-tab cases.

## 3 (P2) — one structural, line-anchored marker parser

`parseOmcMarkerStructure()` validates ordering, pairing and nesting using whole-line anchoring (never substring `includes`), and is shared by both the mutation path and doctor. Malformed structure **fails safe**: `mergeClaudeMd` preserves the whole file under the recovered-content header, and doctor reports `hasMalformedMarkers` + still flags any legacy content. The adversarial `START / current / START / exact legacy guide / END` is now detected (both a merge regression and a doctor regression).

## 4 (P2) — companion aggregation

`checkClaudeMdStatus()` no longer returns on the first marked companion or when the main file has markers. It scans the main file and **every** present/referenced companion and ORs their legacy/malformed results. Regression: clean `CLAUDE-a.md` first, legacy content in `CLAUDE-z.md` → reported.

## 5 (P2) — manifest anti-drift

`src/installer/__tests__/fixtures/legacy-template-manifest.json` records `{blob, lineCount, sha256, heading, markerAbsence}` for all 29 markerless revisions. A **history-independent** test (`legacy-template-manifest.test.ts`) asserts the shipped code constant matches the manifest and that the fixtures normalize into it. `scripts/generate-legacy-template-manifest.mjs [--check]` regenerates/verifies the manifest from git history for CI/maintenance.

## Retained v2 behavior

Exact-match removal, fail-closed on near-misses, multi-block removal without spanning, fingerprints-inside-markers not flagged, the `install()` smoke (file shrinks, backup written, `@USER.md`/`@RTK.md` preserved) — all still covered.

## Verification

Focused installer/doctor/setup suites: 112/112 pass (incl. all new blocker regressions). `npx tsc --noEmit` clean. `npm run lint` 0 errors (19 pre-existing warnings, none in changed files). `npm run build` succeeds and emits `dist/cli/commands/merge-claude-md.js`; a manual run of the real built entry removes the 583-line guide (23,148 → 113 bytes) and preserves `@USER.md`. `scripts/generate-legacy-template-manifest.mjs --check` passes.

Full `npm run test:run`: 10,178 passed / 8 skipped / 4 failed — the 4 failures are the known parallel-load flakes (`runtime-watchdog-retry`, `session-end-timeout`, `standalone-hook-reconcile`, shared-`/tmp` state), all of which pass in isolation and are unrelated to this change (the #3444 review noted the same shared-`/tmp` flake).

Per the no-generated-artifacts policy, `dist/`/`bridge/` are not committed (`git restore`d before commit); the maintainer rebuilds them at merge, which also produces the `merge-claude-md` entry the shell resolves in production.

author: morpheums
body:
## FEAT-009 — Self-Improvement Loop + session fixes (v2.12.0)

Builds the mechanism Nazgul was missing: a durable, self-feeding improvement loop, plus the concrete conductor/session fixes surfaced while dogfooding FEAT-008. Runs on the **sequential** engine (the Conductor is the subject of several of these fixes and demonstrated its bugs live, so it was not used to drive its own repair).

### Shipped
- **Post-loop self-audit gate** (`scripts/self-audit.sh`, `agents/self-audit.md`, stop-hook gate) — mines each objective's own signals (review rejections, retries, blocks, best-effort token cost, TODO/FIXME deltas, first-party findings) into a durable append-only backlog at `nazgul/improvements.md`. Never fails the run; bounded ≤3-attempt backstop. Opt out with `self_audit.enabled: false`. (ADR-001)
- **First-party finding-raise channel** (`scripts/lib/raise-finding.sh`, RULES §14) — any Bash-capable sub-session (implementer, team, debugger, conductor) can `raise_finding <severity> <category> <title> <detail> [fix] [evidence]`, appending one `jq --arg` (no-eval), `flock`-guarded, newline-neutralized JSON line to `nazgul/logs/findings.jsonl`, ingested by the self-audit. So no improvement candidate is lost when a sub-session exits.
- **`models.conductor`** (default `sonnet`) — pins the Conductor's own tier so it no longer silently inherits the launching session's model (the FEAT-008 ~85%-cost problem).
- **`models.review` split** into `models.review_orchestrator` / `models.review_default` (fallback: new key → legacy `models.review` → hardcoded `sonnet`/`haiku`).
- **H1 — conductor-owned per-unit fan-out** (`conductor-router.sh`, ADR-004): parallel file-disjoint waves dispatch as concurrent per-unit `subagent` implementers by the conductor itself, never delegated to the non-spawning team-orchestrator (which silently serialized). Team backend deprecated on the mutating path; closes the RULES §12 "Layer 1 vs Layer 4" limitation.
- **H3 — rework-guard own-scope exemption** (`conductor-rework-guard.sh`, ADR-006): the actively-dispatched unit may write inside its own `file_scope`; still blocks writes into a *different* committed unit's scope. Fail-closed on ambiguity.
- **Hygiene bundle** — stale conductor markers self-heal on fresh start; new plan archives the prior objective's `tasks/`; CLAUDE.md command-form + stale migration-name refs corrected.
- **Config schema v21 → v22** additive migration (`migrate_21_to_22`) + `/nazgul:status` conductor-mode view.

### Deferred to FEAT-010 (documented, NOT shipped)
Both are a command-string-parsing arms race — the fix belongs at the git layer, not a hand-rolled tokenizer:
- **TASK-004** base-branch-commit-guard cwd fix — 4 bypass classes across 3 review rounds.
- **TASK-011 / H2** conductor pre-merge review-verdict guard — ~10 bypasses across 3 rounds; **the fail-closed redesign still leaked** (shell param-expansion in the subcommand slot, backslash line-continuation). Reverted; `conductor.enforce.premerge_guard` config key stripped as orphaned; ADR-005 marked DEFERRED.

### The loop already paid off
On its first run the self-audit + finding channel captured **7 real findings** from this session into `nazgul/improvements.md`, and the learner distilled 2 enforceable candidate rules (git-level guard enforcement @90; haiku reviewer stall-retry @78). These seed FEAT-010.

### Verification
- `tests/run-tests.sh`: **65/65 files pass**.
- TASK-008 (release + docs): Review Board **APPROVED 4/4** (conf 92), evidence + provenance validated, `require_all_approve` honored, security-reviewer never skipped.
- Post-loop gates all satisfied: doc-verifier PASS, comment-verifier PASS, learner distilled, self-audit recorded.
- Deferral-honoring axis verified: `git grep -i premerge` outside `nazgul/` returns only the CHANGELOG "NOT shipped" note.

body:
… graphics

RHI:
- Device picks an async compute queue at creation: a dedicated compute-only family when the GPU has one, else a second graphics-family queue, else the graphics queue aliased (asyncComputeAvailable() = false). Adds immediateSubmitCompute() for setup-time compute work (future BLAS/TLAS).
- BufferDesc::shareGraphicsCompute creates buffers CONCURRENT across the two families, so per-frame cross-queue buffers need no ownership transfers.
- Barrier.h gains bufferQueueTransfer/imageQueueTransfer release/acquire helpers for EXCLUSIVE resources that migrate rarely (images, RT phase).

Renderer:
- The frame is now three submissions chained by timelines (diagram in Renderer.h): graphics batch 1 (upload flush + aux + shadow, signals the new upload timeline at its transfer stages), the point-cloud compute batch on the async queue (waits the previous frame's timeline for the per-pixel buffers and this frame's upload timeline for streamed cloud chunks), and graphics batch 2 (scene + resolve + backbuffer, waits the compute timeline at FRAGMENT). Batch 1 also waits the previous compute value at transfer stages - the WAR guard for the Morton-resort in-place ring copies.
- PointCloudPass::recordCompute(cmd, asyncQueue) drops the cross-frame and compute->fragment barriers on the async queue (the semaphore chain owns that ordering; their graphics stage bits are illegal on a compute-only family) and keeps the internal copy/clear->compute barriers.
- Cloud storage (PointCloudGpu), the per-pixel buffers and the dispatch staging/device pair are CONCURRENT-shared.
- Single-queue GPUs and the panel toggle fall back to inline recording, decided per frame; both desktop and XR paths use the same flow.

App/GUI: Settings.render.asyncCompute (default on) applied each frame, async-compute status in the Diagnostics panel, toggle in the Point Clouds panel. docs/TODO.md section G entry marked done; CLAUDE.md updated.

## Fix for #797 — Predictable OAuth State Token → CSRF + Account Takeover ($150)

### Vulnerability
OAuth state parameter uses auto-increment integers / timestamps. Attacker predicts next state value, crafts malicious OAuth link to hijack accounts.

### Fix
1. **Cryptographically random** — `secrets.token_bytes(32)` + SHA256 hash
2. **Session binding** — state tied to user's session ID

4. **Time-based expiry** — 10-minute window
5. **Cleanup** — expired states automatically removed

author: r2205
body:
## Summary

A follow-up bug sweep to PR #34: every finding from the previous audit's `BUG_HUNT_REPORT.md` was re-checked against current code (25 of 29 already fixed), and a fresh hunt across all subsystems — plus an adversarial review of this branch's own commits — produced ~30 fixes in four commits.

### Data loss / corruption

- **"Replace existing" CSV import could silently wipe the entire session log.** A semicolon-delimited Excel re-save (or any file where zero rows parse) bypassed the empty-file guard, committed `deleteAll()`, and reported "Imported 0 sessions" as success. Zero parsed rows on a replace-import now roll the wipe back with an explanatory error. Related: Excel's UTF-8 BOM broke header matching, a revoked file grant reported success, replace-import leaked every receipt file, and impossible dates (`2023-2-29`) were clamped instead of skipped.
- **A failed undo-restore permanently destroyed the data being restored** — the pre-restore snapshot (the only remaining copy during an undo) was overwritten before the wipe transaction committed. The snapshot is now staged and promoted only after commit.
- **Heavy users' backups could become un-restorable**: export is unbounded but restore capped total decompression at 100 MiB — including the automatic pre-restore snapshot, so "Undo last restore" failed exactly when needed. Raised to 2 GiB; zip-bomb defense still holds via the per-entry (25 MiB) and entry-count (5000) caps.
- **GPS-autofilled coordinates were silently discarded on save** (misclassified as a manual address edit); one stored NaN/Infinity bricked every backup export *and* restore; shared vehicle photos were deleted out from under the other row; in-flight receipt copies were dropped by a quick Save and stranded on disk.

### Crashes / wrong numbers

- "Select all → Assign to trip" crashed with `too many SQL variables` past ~1000 sessions (ids now chunked inside one transaction).
- Date-only CSV/XLSX imports (every row stamped midnight) made the odometer walk double-count distance and paired efficiency legs backwards; session timelines now tie-break on `(sessionStart, id)` everywhere, including the DAO adjacency queries and interleaved-charge checks.
- Vehicle "Avg power" divided all sessions' energy by only-some sessions' charge time; the $/min ⇄ $/hr toggle mutated the typed value (1 → 1.002); fractional battery % ("82.5") silently saved as null; an unformatted XLSX battery cell of exactly `1` imported as 100%.

### Lifecycle / navigation

- Switching the default vehicle wasn't atomic (a process death could leave two defaults and quick-track attached sessions to the wrong car); a moved session silently re-attested `continuesPrevious` against a neighbour the user never vouched for — while a flag ticked in the same edit that moves the session is now kept.
- Notification deep links: a tap while a *different* session's edit screen was open was silently swallowed (wrong-row data entry); a Recents relaunch could re-fire a days-old tap.
- Rotation/process death: the trip edit dialog discarded everything typed, the "replace existing on import" checkbox reset (turning replace into a full-log duplicate), the quick-track permission round-trip was dropped, and the map picker's exit latch could permanently brick its buttons. Backup export/restore are now non-cancellable so back-navigation can't truncate a backup mid-write.
- The map's first-open backfill could stamp one station's coordinates onto physically different stations sharing only a brand, and never retried partially-located stops; it now groups by (stop, exact geocode inputs).

## Testing

- 169 unit tests pass locally (16 classes), including 20 new regression tests covering the DAO continuity/tie-break semantics, default-vehicle atomicity, timeline determinism, non-finite parsing, strict date resolution, and CSV formula-defusing round-trips.
- Unit tests were run via a standalone JVM harness (Gradle 9.x distributions weren't downloadable in the sandboxed dev environment); the Compose UI files were changed surgically and hand-reviewed plus adversarially machine-reviewed — this CI run is the first full `testDebugUnitTest` + `assembleRelease` pass, so it's the authoritative check.

author: lockhinator
body:
## What & why

There was no way to ask the guard **"would this command be gated, and why?"** without running it — an agent (or human tuning config) had to execute a command and observe the reaction, which is exactly what you don't want to do with a `delete`. `doctor` reports interception/posture, not the decision for a specific command.

`kubectl-guard explain [--json] -- <kubectl args...>` runs the guard's real decision logic (`guard.Check`) **without** executing kubectl, prompting, or auditing, and reports the outcome + the matched rule:

```
$ kubectl-guard explain -- delete pod nginx --context prod-cluster
decision:  needs-confirmation
reason:    protected context "prod-cluster"
verb:      delete (state-altering)
context:  prod-cluster
namespace: default
```

Closes #75.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] `explain -- delete pod x` prints the decision + reason without running kubectl, prompting, or auditing
- [x] `--json` emits a structured decision object matching the runtime `--json` (`JSONResult`)
- [x] Covers allow / needs-confirmation / blocked / denied / dry-run outcomes (and every v0.6.0 policy)
- [x] `go test ./...` passes

## Design

`guard.Explain(args) ExplainResult` calls `Check` (the authoritative, side-effect-free decision) and takes the **decision straight from it** — `explainFrom` only *derives the reason* by re-evaluating the same policy predicates in the same precedence. So explain's decision is byte-identical to runtime and can **never under-report** a restriction (a false "allow" would be the dangerous case). `--json`'s `reason` field carries the machine-readable matched **rule** (`protected-context`, `blast-radius`, `unknown-verb`, …) — a stable token, strictly more informative than the runtime needs-confirmation reason (`aborted`). Secret flag values are redacted in the output.

## Tests

`guard/explain_test.go` — the decision→rule mapping for every Result (allow/needs-confirmation/blocked/denied/setup-required/dry-run-skip, and sensitive/blast/unknown reasons), the verb classification, the JSON shape (reason = machine rule), and a no-audit + valid-decision end-to-end assertion. Full suite green (`build`/`vet`/`test -race`/`gofmt`/`golangci-lint`).

## Review summary

Dual adversarial + dedicated security review, verified empirically with a fake kubectl that marks any target-verb exec. Both reviewers confirmed the core safety property: across **25+ cases** spanning every policy type, explain's decision **matched the real guard exit code exactly** (never weaker), it **never exec'd the target command** (only the read-only `config current-context`/`config view` lookups `Check` legitimately does), wrote **no audit entry**, redacted secrets, and honored the actor/config identically (actor policies are monotonic, so no actor mismatch can make explain permissive when runtime gates). No decision mismatch or under-report found.

Findings (all LOW, addressed or benign):
- The `--json` `reason` was prose while runtime uses machine tokens, and the machine rule was dropped — **fixed**: `--json` now emits the machine rule token (block-mode/resource tokens aligned with runtime).
- Test-quality note — **addressed**: the end-to-end test now pins a valid decision + populated reason/rule.
- A reason-wording edge for an unknown verb gated purely via a baked-in protected namespace (labels `unknown-verb` vs runtime prompt's `protected-namespace`) — benign, the **decision is identical** and both labels are truthful.

## Caveats

- `explain` performs the same read-only resolution the real decision does (context lookup; cached `api-resources` discovery when protected resources + discovery are configured) — it never runs the target command.
- Human output goes to stdout (a query); the runtime `--json` goes to stderr. Same `JSONResult` schema.

Please **merge with a merge commit (do not squash)**.

author: kaecer68
body:
## Problem

The Docker build logs showed:

```text
fatal: not a git repository (or any of the parent directories): .git
```

This happened because `.dockerignore` excludes `.git/`, so the `git describe --tags --always` shell substitution inside the Dockerfile failed silently. The build still succeeded, but the binary was left without meaningful embedded version metadata.

## Solution

1. **Dockerfile**: declare `ARG VERSION` and `ARG BUILDTIME`, and use them in the Go ldflags. When the args are not supplied (e.g. local `docker compose build`), they default to `dev` and the current UTC timestamp.
2. **CI workflow**: add a `Set build metadata` step that produces `VERSION={{ github.ref_name }}-{{ github.sha }}` and `BUILDTIME=YYYYMMDDhhmmss`, then pass them to `docker/build-push-action` via `build-args`.

## Verification

- Local `docker compose build atlas` completes without the git error.
- CI Docker image build still passes (pending).

- `Dockerfile`
- `.github/workflows/ci-cd.yml`

﻿## Summary
- Cloudflare Pages only adds its own `Cache-Control: public, max-age=0, must-revalidate` header on requests with no `Authorization`/session credential. author: josephnef
body:
## What

The 802.11 MAC inserts its live TSF into every **beacon** at the instant of transmission — a genuine sub-µs **hardware TX-egress timestamp**. Bench-measured at **0.289 µs** RMS against an independent receiver, versus **117–473 µs** for any host-side "read the clock after `send`" shortcut. Paired with the per-frame hardware **RX** timestamp (`RxAtrib.tsfl`), it is the primitive for **one-way hardware time distribution** — the only sub-µs option on Wi-Fi silicon that exposes no host-reported TX-egress timestamp.

This lands the library support for that primitive, plus the measured writeup of how devourer's TSF sync compares to NTP/PTP over Wi-Fi.

## Library

- **`Packet::TxEgressTsf()`** — parse the sender's hardware egress TSF from a received beacon / probe response (any AP, not just a devourer transmitter), returned alongside `tsfl`.
- **`TsfSync`** (`src/TsfSync.h`) — a running least-squares fit over `{remote egress, local arrival}` pairs → `SkewPpm()`, `OffsetUs()`, and `LocalForRemote()` / `RemoteForLocal()` clock translation. Feed it a `Packet` and beacons are picked automatically. Header-only, chip-neutral.
- **`AdapterCaps`** `hw_rx_timestamp` / `hw_beacon_txtsf` flags (surfaced in the `adapter.caps` event), hardware-verified per generation (J2/J3 stamp beacons; J1 has no `StartBeacon` → `hw_beacon_txtsf=0`).
- `rxdemo` emits `tx_tsf` on beacons; `docs/logging.md` documents it.
- **Headless selftest `tsf_sync_math`** (ctest): skew/offset recovery within 1 ppm, clock translation round-trip, the 32-bit TSF wrap, and the beacon pick.

## Docs

- **`docs/timing-accuracy.md`** — measured NTP-vs-TSF (~0.76 ms vs ~0.25 µs, ~3000×), why hardware PTP can't run on Realtek Wi-Fi (stock driver exposes no HW timestamps; TX egress is firmware-blocked), the lone ath9k exception, a real-PTP-hardware cross-check against the on-board Intel I226 (TSF tracks it to ~290 ns — its quantization floor — at +42 ppm), and the TX-egress-shortcut benchmark. Includes source links so the state can be re-checked if it changes.
- **`tests/txegress_{witness.cpp,analyze.py,bench.sh}`** — the single-witness benchmark behind the 0.289 µs / 117 µs / 473 µs figures.

## Test

`ctest` 16/16 green (adds `tsf_sync_math`). No chip HAL behavior change beyond the two additive caps flags; OFF-config builds unaffected.

author: pandas-studio
body:
## Summary

Final PR of the proxy first-user improvement plan (⑧, depends on #653/#654/#656/#660, all merged). Makes registration/connectivity failures self-diagnosable for a first-time user and closes a secret-leak surface in probe error output.

Four parts:

1. **Staged probe results** — `_probe_one` no longer collapses connect → initialize → list_tools into one boolean. A new stdlib-only `proxy/staged_status.py` defines a `ProbeStage` ladder (`configured → transport connected → MCP initialized → tools discovered`) and a frozen `StagedProbeResult`, returned instead of raised (the exception has already unwound the ladder by the time a caller could classify it). `mms health` names the last successful stage on `DISCONNECTED` lines; `health --json` gains additive `stage`/`failed_stage`/`transport` keys (legacy `connected`/`tools`/`overflowing`/`error` shapes unchanged).

2. **Central string sanitizer** — `utils/redact.sanitize_secrets` scrubs free-form exception/probe strings (which bypass the mapping redactors) against a server's own `env`/`headers` values and URL credentials. Single-pass regex, longest-first, empty-safe, min-length-4 (trivial values like `"k"` would corrupt ordinary text). Applied at the `_probe_one` choke point so every probe consumer inherits it; schema-validation errors in `health`/`doctor` are scrubbed too.

3. **`mms doctor`** — read-only diagnostic aggregating the existing checks (config file/JSON/schema, per-transport required fields, prefix conflicts, staged probe, cache policy, LTM) as one PASS/WARN/FAIL report with a copy-paste `next:` action per problem. Exit 1 on any FAIL, 0 on WARN-only (the scriptable quickstart success gate); LTM never FAILs (only surfacing depends on it). Reuses the same shared validators/probe the runtime enforces (pinned by source-inspection tests).

4. **Docs** — `docs/cli.md` doctor section + staged-health notes; README Quick Start success criterion becomes "`mms doctor` exits 0 + first tool listed"; CHANGELOG entries.

## Behavior change

- `mms health` disconnected lines and `add --validate` failures now name the stage reached; `health --json` server entries carry additive `stage`/`failed_stage`/`transport` keys.
- Probe/exception strings surfaced by `health`/`doctor`/`add --validate`/import no longer echo configured `env`/`headers` values or URL credentials.
- New commands: `mms doctor`. No existing command's output shape shrinks or renames.

## Testing

- CI-filter suite green (4551 passed, 3 skipped); `ruff check`/`format` and `mypy` clean on `src` (new module is pure stdlib, Windows-safe).
- New coverage: sanitizer rules incl. multi-secret cascade + placeholder-backslash; probe stage progression, teardown-after-discovery success, malformed-result classification, short-secret non-corruption, header/URL-cred redaction end-to-end; `TestDoctor` over the ratified scenarios (healthy / bad JSON / bad transport / prefix conflict / offline server / LTM unset) + `--json` purity + exit codes + source-inspection wiring pins.
- Manual E2E: `mms doctor` on a clean temp HOME gates the quickstart correctly (FAIL→`mms init` before add, all-PASS+LTM-WARN→exit 0 after); secret-header config never leaks the token in text or `--json`.
- Two rounds of codex diff review (NEEDS-FIX×2 → SHIP): fixed sanitizer cascade, URL-cred components, teardown/malformed-result staging, and schema-error redaction.

`POST /api/propose` は **mood_tags（気分タグ）非空で 500・空で 200**。#110 の1次修正（try/except 防御・フォールバック）を入れても本番で直りきらなかった。真因の再特定と根治を行う。

## 1次修正(#110)が不十分だった理由
- #110 は「collect_context の例外を握り潰さず output_context を必ず設定」という防御を入れたが、**そもそも例外は発生していなかった**（本番ログにフォールバック警告も再送出ログも出ていなかった観測と一致）。
- #110 の失敗注入テストは層3 `search()` を **同期・即時例外** にしていたため、`collect_context` がフォールバックで即完了してしまい、本番の失敗様態（**遅い層3による合流レース**）を再現できていなかった。→ テストは通るのに本番で直らなかった。

## 確定した真因（証拠付き）
ADK 2.3.0 Workflow の **合流バリア欠如によるスケジューリング競合**。CancelledError でも state 非伝播でもない。

- 旧配線 `((collect_context, collect_vision), generate)` の合流先 `generate` は素の `FunctionNode` で `_requires_all_predecessors=False`。
- `Workflow._buffer_downstream_triggers`（`_workflow.py`）は、合流先が `JoinNode`（`_requires_all_predecessors=True`）でない限り、**先に完了した片方**の前段ノードの完了時点で下流トリガーをバッファする（else 分岐）。
- **mood_tags 空** → 層3ベクトル検索は `query_text` 空でスキップ（`context_retriever._get_similar_snippets`）→ `collect_context` が高速完了 → レース非顕在 → 200。
- **mood_tags 非空** → 層3（本番 Memory Bank）が ~7秒かかる間に、画像なしで即完了する `collect_vision` が先に `generate` をトリガー → `generate` が `output_context` 未設定を検知して防御 `RuntimeError`（=500, ~7.8秒）。観測された7つの事実（成功ログ無し/フォールバック警告無し/再送出ログ無し/generic "Node execution failed" のみ/generate の RuntimeError のみ traceback）とすべて整合。

ローカル再現: 層3を「遅い async」にするだけで（例外を投げなくても）500 を確定再現。→ 遅延レースが真因である直接証拠。

## 根治内容（採った案と理由）
**案B（合流の state 伝播/スケジューリング是正）を採用。** 合流を JoinNode にするのが直接の根治で、並列性も維持できる。
- `orchestrator.py`: `generate` の直前に `JoinNode(collect_join)` バリアを挿入し、`collect_context` と `collect_vision` の**両方完了まで** `generate` を起動しない。冗長で複雑さを増すだけの `parallel_worker=True` を撤去（START fan-out で並列は担保／`_ParallelWorker` はサブブランチ化するだけ）。
- あわせて**案A**も併用（多層防御）: `context_retriever._get_similar_snippets` を `asyncio.wait_for`（既定5秒・`VECTOR_SEARCH_TIMEOUT_SEC` で調整可）でタイムアウト＋`BaseException` フォールバック。Memory Bank のハング/例外/キャンセルでも層1/層2と生成を継続。`CancelledError` はタスクキャンセル尊重のため再送出。→ goal 4（Memory Bank ~7秒対策）も同時に達成。
- `collect_context` の防御 `try/except` を `BaseException` に拡張。

**層1（アレルギー・未所持器具）の決定的フィルタは一切変更なし。** 層3（加点要素）のみ隔離。

## 本番失敗様態を再現する回帰テスト
`tests/integration/test_orchestrator.py` に追加:
- `test_orchestrator_run_survives_slow_context_retrieval`: 遅い `collect_context` でも 500 にならない。**JoinNode バリアを外すと FAIL・入れると PASS を確認（load-bearing）**。
- `test_orchestrator_run_survives_slow_and_failing_memory_bank`: Memory Bank が ~7秒ハング後に失敗しても 200・3案・層3空・層1（卵）維持。
- `test_layer3_timeout_falls_back_to_empty`: 層3がタイムアウト超過ハングでも空フォールバックし成立。

## pytest 結果
`uv run pytest` 全体 **350 passed**。stash 検証で fix を外すと新規回帰テスト2件が落ち、入れると通ることを確認済み。

## 残リスク
- Memory Bank の恒久復旧（Agent Engine プロビジョン・`gemini-embedding-001`）は #79 管轄でスコープ外。本 PR は「落ちている間も提案は必ず成立」を保証するのみ。
- `VECTOR_SEARCH_TIMEOUT_SEC` 既定5秒は本番 Memory Bank の正常応答時間に応じて調整余地あり（正常応答が5秒超だと毎回タイムアウトで層3が効かなくなる。復旧後は要チューニング）。
- 依存追加なし（stdlib のみ）→ requirements.txt 同期不要。
- 本番検証は親側で実施（本 PR 作業では本番を叩いていない）。

author: shashwat-nandan1
body:
### Motivation
- Remove committed secrets from the repository and provide a safe, placeholder-only `.env.example` while preserving the environment variable names the app expects. 
- Fix local date calculations so `todayISO()` and `weekStartISO()` use local date components and a Monday week start to avoid timezone drift (important for locales like India). 
- Prevent unsafe text interpolation in profile search and stop duplicate active friend relationships from being created in either direction. 
- Ensure weekly/custom-weekly habits cannot be over-marked and avoid loading unlimited historical completions on the Today page. 

### Description
- Removed the committed `.env` from the repo, added `.env` and `.env.*` to `.gitignore`, and added `.env.example` with placeholder Supabase keys while keeping the original variable names (`SUPABASE_*`, `VITE_SUPABASE_*`).
- Replaced UTC `toISOString().slice(0,10)` usage with a `formatLocalDateISO()` helper and updated `todayISO()` and `weekStartISO()` in `src/lib/plants.ts` to use local date parts and Monday as week start. 
- Added a Supabase SQL function `public.search_profiles(search_query text)` (migration `supabase/migrations/20260710120000_harden_friend_search_and_requests.sql`) that escapes wildcards, excludes the current user, limits results to the safe set of columns (`id, full_name, email, avatar_url`), and granted execute to `authenticated`.
- Added a DB-level unique index (via the same migration) on `LEAST(requester_id, receiver_id), GREATEST(requester_id, receiver_id)` for `status IN ('pending','accepted')` so active friend relationships cannot be duplicated in either direction while allowing declined requests to be retried.
- Updated onboarding friend search to call the new RPC (`supabase.rpc('search_profiles', { search_query })`) with the existing UX (minimum 2 characters, loading/empty/error states) and updated friend request insertion to detect duplicate constraint violations (`23505`) and show a friendlier toast.
- Modified Today page loading in `src/routes/_authenticated/today.tsx` to fetch only: today completions, current-week completions, exact total completions count (head/count), and a capped latest list for garden rendering; added client-side guards so a habit cannot be completed twice in a day, and weekly/custom-weekly habits cannot exceed their weekly target; optimistic updates are used and duplicate-insert DB errors are handled with user-friendly toasts.
- Updated generated types to include the new `search_profiles` function signature so RPC usage is typed. 

### Testing
- Attempted `npm run lint` (which runs `eslint .`) and it failed to complete because project dependencies are not installed (`@eslint/js` not found in `node_modules`).
- Attempted `npm run build` (which runs `vite build`) and it failed to complete because `vite` is not installed in `node_modules`.
- Verified file-level changes and created the migration SQL file `supabase/migrations/20260710120000_harden_friend_search_and_requests.sql` which includes both the safe search function and the unique index preventing duplicate active friend pairs.

author: abigailbramble
body:
## Problem

Zendesk tickets carry tags, and teams rely on them to categorize and filter their support queue. The historical Zendesk import fetches the full ticket payload (which includes the `tags` array) but silently discards it, so imported tickets arrive untagged and teams lose that categorization.

## Changes

Newly imported tickets now get their Zendesk tags, wired into PostHog's product-wide tag system (`Tag`/`TaggedItem`) rather than stored as loose strings:

- Each ticket's `tags` array from the Zendesk payload is normalized the same way the live tagging API does (`tagify`: lowercase + strip, empties dropped, deduped per ticket). No extra Zendesk API calls - the tags are already in the `show_many` response the import fetches.
- Tag names resolve to team-scoped `Tag` rows via `get_or_create`, matching the live apply path (`set_tags_on_object`): existing tags are reused, new ones created, never duplicated per team.
- `TaggedItem` links are bulk-created inside the import transaction after tickets get their IDs.

Because tags land in the shared tag system, imported tickets immediately work with everything tags already support: the ticket list's `tags`/`tags_all`/`tags_exclude` filters, tag display, and cross-product tag queries.

> [!NOTE]
> The `TaggedItem` links use `bulk_create`, which skips `save()`/`full_clean()` and signals on purpose - the same no-signals rule as every other historical write in this import. Tags are applied only to tickets the import creates; already-imported (skipped) tickets are deliberately untouched.

## How did you test this code?

- Added one test covering the matrix: normalization (`"Billing"`, `" URGENT "` → `billing`, `urgent`), empty tags dropped, a pre-existing team tag reused instead of duplicated, one `Tag` row shared across tickets in a batch, and untagged tickets staying untagged. No existing test exercised tags in the import, so this catches regressions in the mapping, normalization, or per-team dedupe.
- Ran the full `zendesk_import/tests/test_activities.py` suite locally: 25 passed.
- Manually verified on a local stack: ran an import against Zendesk and the newly imported tickets came in with their tags applied.

## Automatic notifications

- [ ] Publish to changelog?
- [ ] Alert Sales and Marketing teams?

## Docs update

## 🤖 Agent context

**Autonomy:** Human-driven (agent-assisted)

- Authored with PostHog Code (Claude). Skills invoked: `/writing-tests`.
- Scoping decision (confirmed with the driver): tags apply to newly imported tickets only. Backfilling tags onto already-imported tickets on re-import was considered and rejected - skipped tickets are never re-fetched from Zendesk today, so backfill would add a fetch to the skip path for a one-time repair.
- `Tag` rows are resolved with `get_or_create` before the ticket transaction to keep the lock window narrow; a `Tag` row left behind by a failed batch is harmless and reused on retry.

implementing the naming interface, with real Rust conventions where they
differ from C++ — `member_name`/`value_name` are genuine snake_case/
SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE conversions (not a reuse of C++'s lowerCamelCase), and
`escape()` uses Rust's own keyword list + `r#...` raw-identifier escaping
(not C++'s trailing-underscore convention). `type_name`/`synthetic_name`
reuse the same PascalCase transform as `CppBackend` — coincidental overlap
between ASN.1/Rust/C++ type-naming conventions, not an assumption baked into
the interface.

New test (`tests/codegen/test_backend_naming.cpp`, ctest `backend_naming`):
exercises both backends against the same ASN.1 names, asserts the
divergences are correct, and constructs a `Generator` with the injected
`RustBackend` (3-arg ctor) to prove the seam is real — construction only, no
`generate()` call, since that would still emit C++ text with Rust-flavored
names today (misleading, not real Rust output).

Per user direction, this is now the prerequisite for #225's pairwise
migration (CppBackend construct → RustBackend construct, starting with
#226/#234 for ENUMERATED) rather than a one-shot full-schema stub.

**Verification:** ctest 59/59 (58 previous + this one). No changes to
`Generator.hpp`/`.cpp` — purely additive.

author: jakepre
body:
## What

Stage 1 of #813: a shared `_floor_tile_scene()` hook on `MinigameView3D` so a game can tile its arena with a different in-repo Kenney block (grass / snow / stone) instead of the default grey `platform.glb` — the owner's "use the grass, use the stone!" ask. Mirrors the existing #589 `_floor_tint()` hook: a one-liner per game, no scene work.

## The thickness problem (and why vertex data)

`platform.glb` is a thin ~0.195 slab; the full `block-grass`/`block-snow` blocks are ~1.0 tall. A fixed vertical offset (the old hardcoded `FLOOR_TILE_THICKNESS = 0.195`) would sink or float a swapped block. `_build_floor` now measures the tile's top surface from its **mesh vertices** (`_mesh_top`) and seats it at y=0, so any block sits flush with no per-game offset.

Vertex data is used deliberately: I verified that both `Mesh.get_aabb()` and `MultiMesh.get_instance_transform()` read **0 in a headless / pre-render context** (the RenderingServer hasn't drawn the mesh yet) — which is exactly why the original code hardcoded 0.195. The vertex measure is render-independent and reproduces 0.195 for the platform exactly, so **existing floors are unchanged**.

## Reference conversion

King of the Hill now tiles with the grass block (a grassy hill), dropping its former moss *tint* since the block carries its own green.

## Tests

- `_mesh_top` measures platform (**0.195**) vs grass (**1.0**) — the exact offsets `_build_floor` negates (the platform=0.195 assertion is also the no-regression guard).
- The mesh-swap override is honored (KotH's floor mesh ≠ the base platform).
- `gdformat`/`gdlint` clean; full suite green (**1891**). The Render CI check on this PR is the visual confirmation.

## Note

Stage 2 (per-game floor-mesh + props/dressing fan-out) stays a **Sonnet** claim. Touches `src/minigames/_api/` (§5) — rebased before merge.

> **Race transparency:** a second Opus session claimed #813 within ~9s of me (their comment first, my branch push first — a dead heat). Their branch is an empty marker; this is the complete tested implementation, opened to avoid a rebuild. See the issue thread; happy to defer if they'd started locally.

body:
Implements #98 — the user-facing Session Wake control surfaces. Parent epic #94.

## Important context: dependency status

#98 is specified to sit **over the shared native coordinator from #95–#97**. Those three issues are still **open** — no merged PRs — and #96 is being implemented concurrently in another worktree (uncommitted `MeterBar/SessionWake/Wake*` quota-gate primitives). This PR is therefore built as a **self-contained UI seam**:

- It compiles against `master` and does **not** import the uncommitted #96 types.
- Its vocabulary (states, block/skip reasons, run outcomes) is aligned to the emerging #96/#97 types so integration is frictionless.
- `SessionWakeCoordinator` is the seam the real coordinator subclasses later; the interim `shared` is an **honest inert stub** (no subprocess/filesystem work — the dry-run "no mutation" invariant holds trivially).

No automation logic lives in views (per the issue's explicit constraint).

## What's included

- **`SessionWakeStatus`** — presentation lifecycle: Off · Idle · Armed · Scanning · Waiting · Quota Unknown · Running · Stopping · Completed · Needs Attention. Each state has a distinct label, so nothing collapses into "Watching". Plus `SessionWakeRunSummary` and `SessionWakeEligibility`.
- **`SessionWakeSettingsStore`** — UserDefaults-backed. Separates **feature enablement** from **watcher intent**; persists an **explicit** `wakeAccountID` (never inferred from order/activity/`~/.claude-active-account`); first-enable **and** separate permission-bypass acknowledgements; notify prefs; account-removal reconcile that safely suspends the watcher; fail-safe load (an armed watcher never resurrects while the feature is off).
- **`SessionWakeNotificationDecider`** — pure; gated on the global notification switch **and** Claude provider visibility **and** per-event Session Wake prefs.
- **Views** — `Settings → Automation` pane (feature toggle with first-enable safety sheet, explicit account picker, permission-bypass confirmation, notify toggles); shared `SessionWakeStatusView` / `SessionWakeStatusBadge` / `SessionWakeWatcherControl`; and a menu-bar `SessionWakePopoverCard` exposing the same Wake Watcher kill-switch. Both surfaces bind the **same** shared singletons. Native Liquid Glass card surfaces, adaptive light/dark tone colors.

## Acceptance criteria mapping

- Feature off prevents background discovery/resume, Preview still allowed → store gating + stub `preview()` works regardless of feature state.
- Master-off cancels watcher intent → `setFeatureEnabled(false)` forces watcher off.
- Settings + menu-bar controls share one binding → both use `SessionWakeSettingsStore.shared` / `SessionWakeCoordinator.shared`.
- wakeAccountID persists and is explicit; removing/changing it suspends the watcher → `selectWakeAccount` / `reconcile`.
- Running/stopping/failure/quota-unknown states are visible, not collapsed → distinct `SessionWakeStatus` cases + tests.
- Notifications respect global + provider + Session Wake prefs → `SessionWakeNotificationDecider` + tests.
- Store and SwiftUI hosting tests cover standalone Settings **and** embedded/dashboard surfaces → included.

Live discovery/quota/runner wiring, `WakeQuotaState`/runner-outcome → presentation mapping, and app-delegate notification posting are deliberately deferred to the #95–#97 / #99 integration.

## Verification

- `swift test`: **407 passed, 0 failures** (38 new: store, status, decider, coordinator, and SwiftUI hosting across every status + standalone/embedded Settings).
- `swiftlint lint`: clean (project-wide).
- Coverage gate: **38.4%** (CI floor 19%).

author: axelander
body:
## Web search as a tenant-configured external MCP provider

  Replaces the built-in Tavily integration with a provider-agnostic web-search boundary: a dedicated external MCP server marked `purpose=web_search`. Eneo manages connection, activation, tools, and security. Provider-specific configuration
  (search depth, engines, domain rules) stays with the provider. An administrator can register Tavily, Exa, or a SearXNG bridge without any Eneo code changes, and switching provider is a single activation.

  > Stacked on `feat/agentic-rag-knowledge-mcp`.

  ### Provider catalog and activation

  - MCP servers gain a `purpose` discriminator (`general` | `web_search`). Existing rows are unaffected.
  - A tenant may save several web-search providers, but only one can be active. This is enforced by a partial unique index (`tenant_id WHERE purpose = 'web_search' AND is_enabled = true`) and switched atomically via `POST
  /mcp-servers/{id}/activate-web-search/`, which deactivates the previous provider in the same transaction and rejects unreachable or tool-less servers.
  - New admin page `/admin/web-search`: active provider summary, add/activate/deactivate, connection validation, tool sync with schema-change review, per-tool enablement, identity-forwarding warning, masked credentials. The generic MCP admin
  page shows general servers only and links there.

  ### Configuration and runtime model

  - Web search flows through the ordinary admin → space → assistant inheritance, surfaced as a "Webbsökning" switch in a new **Kapaciteter** section on space settings and assistant edit (no provider identity shown, it is an admin concern).
  - At ask time the attached web-search server acts as a **capability marker, not a provider pin**: it is stripped and the currently active provider is resolved and attached in its place, with the admin's tenant-level tool toggles applied.
  Provider switches propagate everywhere immediately, and stale markers survive without blocking unrelated saves.
  - End users toggle search per message through a capability row in the chat tools popover (globe icon, no server framing), riding the existing `disabled_mcp_server_ids` mechanism. Built-in tools (knowledge, files) remain always active.
  - The `use_web_search` request field and the `SHOW_WEB_SEARCH` frontend flag are removed. Configured provider availability is authoritative.
  - All existing MCP security machinery applies unchanged: tool approval, schema-change review, security classification, identity forwarding only when explicitly enabled.

  ### Authentication

  - New `api_key_header` auth type (`{header_name, token}`) alongside `none`/`bearer`. Header names are validated against HTTP token syntax and a deny-list of transport, forwarding, and session headers; tokens are rejected on control characters.
  Credentials stay encrypted (Fernet) and masked, never in URLs or logs.

  ### Legacy removal and data migration

  - Hard-removed: `web_search.py`, `tavily-python`, `TAVILY_API_KEY` (config, `backend/.env.template`, and the deployment env template), the tavily type stub, the eager search call, prompt injection, the `web_search_results` write path and table, and the legacy `web_search_references` field on conversation messages (the chat-debug turn projection now reads citations from `mcp_tool_references` only).
  - Historical citations migrate into `mcp_tool_references` with their original UUIDs preserved (`mcp_tool_name=legacy_web_search`, `meta.sourceType=web-search`), so stored inline `<inref>` references keep resolving. The frontend renders them as
  external links with favicon and title.

  ### Tool display names (generic)

  - Admins can rename how any MCP tool is presented (`display_name` on `mcp_server_tools`, inline editor in the tools panel). Display-only: the protocol-level name is untouched and sync never overwrites it. The proxy prefers it over the remote
  title, so renames flow into tool traces and approval cards.

  ### Migrations

  `202607101000` (purpose + partial unique index) → `202607101001` (citation migration + drop `web_search_results`) → `202607101002` (tool display_name). All tested up/down/up. The chain is appended after the stacked base's migrations: develop head `202607311000` → `202607262000` (#464) → `202607061000` (#538) → these three, single alembic head.

  ### Verification

  - Backend: 1367 unit tests passing, ruff clean, pyright strict clean (pre-commit).
  - Frontend: `svelte-check` 0 errors/0 warnings across all workspaces, lint clean.
  - Manually verified end to end: provider registration and activation, atomic provider switch, capability toggles at space/assistant level, chat search toggle, live Tavily search with citations, tool rename reflected in the tool trace.

  ### Notes for reviewers

  - `use_web_search` is dropped from the conversation API without deprecation; unknown fields from older clients are ignored by Pydantic.
  - Synced with develop through #690 (2026-08-05) via the stacked base; the branch carries develop's object-storage and chat-debug work with no conflicts.



Fixes #723
