body:
Previously when using `-cl-fast-relaxed-math` flag along with `fhonor-nans` or `fhonor-infinities` the honor flags did not override the relaxed math flag. This behaviour is something that is not seen in case of ffast-math for general targets.

This patch makes adjustments to how the driver and cc1 handles the relaxed math flag for opencl. The flag was in the path of `fast-math` so when someone used the `-cl-fast-relaxed-math` flag they were ultimately overriding everything with fast-math. This was the main reason why honor flags were not overriding relaxed math (atleast that's what I have understood from my time working on this).

I have added tests for this as well and modified CodeGen cc1 tests according to the changes in the patch.

I have personally not tested this on any AMD targets myself yet. So I am unsure about this breaking anything (hopefully it should rather fix).

closes #178514

author: duyhuynh-vn
body:
## Summary

Ports **`@on(action, skip_schema_validation=True)`** from the mobilityhouse/ocpp reference into the Rust `ActionDispatcher`, closing gap 1 that the routing conformance audit (#272) pinned as a documented divergence.

The reference records a `_skip_schema_validation` flag **per route** in `create_route_map()` and `_handle_call()` consults it **per action** for validation ([`ocpp/routing.py`](https://github.com/mobilityhouse/ocpp/blob/master/ocpp/routing.py), [`ocpp/charge_point.py`](https://github.com/mobilityhouse/ocpp/blob/master/ocpp/charge_point.py)). Until now the Rust `ActionDispatcher` (`crates/ocpp-messages/src/dispatcher.rs`) carried at most **one dispatcher-global** `SchemaValidator` — all-or-nothing across every registered handler, with no way to validate `BootNotification` while waving through a vendor `DataTransfer` on the same dispatcher.

`Closes #275`

## Real use case

A CSMS wants strict schema validation on standard OCPP actions but needs to accept a vendor-specific action (or a `DataTransfer` payload) whose shape isn't described by a bundled FINAL schema. Before this change the only analog to `skip_schema_validation=True` was standing up a *second* dispatcher with no validator — coarse, and it fragments routing. Now one dispatcher validates its standard routes and skips the one that opts out.

## What changed (production)

- **`crates/ocpp-messages/src/dispatcher.rs`**
  - New private `Route { handler, skip_validation }` — each `@on` entry stores its handler alongside a per-route skip flag (default `false`, matching the reference), the port of `create_route_map()`'s per-action entry.
  - `on(handler)` and new **`on_skip_validation(handler)`** both delegate to a shared private `register(handler, skip)`; the erasure logic is unchanged and shared (no duplication).
  - `dispatch()` now **resolves the route first, then validates** unless that route opted out. Reordering lookup-before-validate is behaviour-preserving for unknown actions — `validate_call` itself returns `NotSupported` there, the same error the handler-lookup miss produces (verified: no test attaches a validator *and* dispatches an unknown action).
  - New **`skips_validation(action)`** introspects the per-route flag (mirrors `has_handler` / `has_validator`).
  - Doc updates on the `validator` field, `on`, and the new methods.

  The public `on()` signature is unchanged, so all existing call sites (`ocpp-cp`, `ocpp-transport`, tests) compile untouched. The `handlers` field is private; nothing outside the module reaches into it.

## What changed (tests — part of the port)

- **`crates/ocpp-messages/src/dispatcher.rs`** — 6 new unit tests: bypass on a skipped route, the validated control rejecting the identical payload (`SchemaViolation(MaxLength)`), per-route isolation (skip on one route, sibling still validated), no-validator equivalence, last-write-wins on re-registration, and `skips_validation` on unregistered actions.
- **`crates/ocpp-conformance/tests/routing.rs`** — the two "documented gap 1" pins (`validator_is_dispatcher_global_not_per_handler`, `unvalidated_dispatcher_is_the_skip_validation_analog`) are **replaced** with assertions of the real behaviour: `skip_schema_validation_is_per_route` (one dispatcher, `BootNotification` skips while `Heartbeat` is still validated) and `unvalidated_dispatcher_skips_all_routes`. Module doc updated — gap 1 marked closed; gap 2 (`NotImplemented` vs `NotSupported`, #276) still tracked.

The discriminator across the tests: `chargePointVendor` has `maxLength: 20`, so a 21-char vendor **passes serde** (a valid `String`) but **fails schema validation** — cleanly separating a validated route (rejects it) from a skipped one (runs the handler).

## What was ported

- Reference: [`ocpp/routing.py`](https://github.com/mobilityhouse/ocpp/blob/master/ocpp/routing.py) `on(..., skip_schema_validation=...)` and [`ocpp/charge_point.py`](https://github.com/mobilityhouse/ocpp/blob/master/ocpp/charge_point.py) `_handle_call()`'s per-route flag consult.

## Test plan

- `cargo fmt --check` — clean.
- `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` — clean.
- `cargo test --workspace --all-features` — **1458 passed, 0 failed**. `dispatcher` unit tests: 19 (6 new); `routing` conformance: 8.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] A registered handler can opt out of schema validation independently of other handlers on the same dispatcher.
- [x] Default remains validate (flag defaults to `false`).
- [x] `routing.rs` asserts: flagged action bypasses validation, sibling action still validated by the same dispatcher.
- [x] `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace --all-features` pass.

## Known gaps / notes

- No new dependencies. Diff is well under the ~500-LOC target.
- The design question the issue raised ("`on_skip_validation` method vs an `on_with(RouteOptions)` builder") is resolved in favour of a dedicated `on_skip_validation` method — it mirrors the existing `on` ergonomics and keeps the common (validated) path the terse default. A `RouteOptions` builder can be layered on later without breaking this API if more per-route options appear.

body:
## Summary
Follow-up to #5. That PR limited the sweep to the radar nearest the view centre by **raw distance**, which ignores each radar's range: standing just outside a small nearby radar but well inside a large distant one still lit the small one — the wrong coverage. Selection is now range-aware.

## Changes
- **`RadarSweepLayer.selectSweepIndex`**: a radar whose range ring *contains* the view centre outranks one that doesn't; the physically nearest breaks ties within a containment tier; when the centre is inside no ring, the nearest overall is drawn so a sweep always shows. Comparison is squared-distance vs squared-range (no sqrt).
- **Docs**: `apps/game/CLAUDE.md` and `README.md` updated to describe the coverage-first rule and its no-coverage fallback.

- `pnpm --filter sector-north-game typecheck` — passes.

body: Signed-off-by: Ruihang Xia I hereby agree to the terms of the [GreptimeDB CLA](https://github.com/GreptimeTeam/.github/blob/main/CLA.md). ## Refer to a related PR or issue link (optional) ## What's changed and what's your intention? TL;DR: store actual integer value as integer, in `__metric_int_` col, and other non-integer float values remain float type. This can bring ~40% storage size reduction with my test data (real data generated by nodeexporter). From `12,705,806,208` MB to `7,428,214,444` MB. In my test data, >94% are actual integers: This makes sense because from Prometheus semantics, metrics like counter, histogram bucket etc can only generate actual integer, only a few types of metrics can possibly be non-integer. We only need to split actual-integer and float into two physical columns to make use of this priori knowledge. Integer can easily achieve way much better encoding efficiency than floats. For write performance, this newly introduced split way has almost the same encoding time with original plain float64 manner: And for query performance, it also has no regression: Notice this is not a forward-compatible change, once upgraded in this manner, new generated data files can't be handled by previous greptimedb. ## PR Checklist Please convert it to a draft if some of the following conditions are not met. - [x] I have written the necessary rustdoc comments. - [x] I have added the necessary unit tests and integration tests. - [ ] This PR requires documentation updates. - [ ] API changes are backward compatible. - [ ] Schema or data changes are backward compatible.

author: bimvoice
body:
## Problem

In `GltfSerializer::finalize()`, three parallel blocks attach the scene roots to their wrapper transform nodes. The `north_rotation_` and `ecef_transform_` blocks dereference their own optional, but the third block is a copy-paste slip: it is guarded by `if (z_up_transform_)` yet dereferences `(*ecef_transform_)`.

These are `boost::optional<json>` (`GltfSerializer.h`). When a separate Z-up node is requested (`SeparateZUpNode`) without ECEF export (`WriteGltfEcef`), `ecef_transform_` is empty, so `operator*` on it is undefined behavior (reads an uninitialized `json`, then writes `["children"]` into it).

## Fix

One token: align the dereference with its guard so the body uses `z_up_transform_`, matching the two blocks above it.

```diff
 if (z_up_transform_) {
-    (*ecef_transform_)["children"] = roots_;
+    (*z_up_transform_)["children"] = roots_;
 }
```

## Notes

The Z-up node already has its children set and is pushed earlier in the function, so this trailing assignment is effectively redundant; the practical effect of the change is removing the latent UB, not altering valid output. Found by reading the serializer (no linked issue). Compilation is covered by CI's `build-ifcopenshell`; I have no local kernel build, so this is a static-analysis fix.

author: farizakb
body:
Closes out the Phase 2 final whole-branch review (no Criticals; 2 Important + 3 fix-now Minors, all fixed here with TDD).

## Fixes

**Important**
- **Never-raise contract:** `_safe_remove` now tolerates any exception during container cleanup (was `NotFound`-only) — a daemon hiccup during removal can no longer clobber an already-computed `SandboxResult` and crash `verify()`.
- **Path containment (security):** `_copy_patched_file` rejects absolute and root-escaping `target_file` values before any filesystem operation. `target_file` is LLM-controlled and the sandbox runs *before* the policy gate in the graph, so this layer must contain it itself — `../../.env`-style traversal now yields a failed `SandboxResult` ("escapes repository root") instead of shipping host files into the container.

**Minor**
- Exception paths preserve already-captured before/after metrics in the failed `SandboxResult` (evidence quality for the future HITL brief).
- `ProposedAction.workers` bounded `ge=1, le=16` — bad scale proposals fail validation at propose time instead of surfacing as a misleading HTTP 422 at verify time.
- Sandbox app containers now publish on `127.0.0.1` only (was 0.0.0.0) — the deliberately-broken app with unauthenticated fault triggers is no longer LAN-reachable.

## Verification
- Unit: `tests/test_sandbox_executor.py` 9/9 (5 new, red→green each)
- Canonical suite (`-m "not docker"`): **106 passed** (100 baseline + 6 new)
- Docker smoke (`test_restart_clears_memory_leak`): 1 passed with loopback-only binding, no port-discovery changes needed

Deferred findings from the review are recorded in the SDD ledger with owner phases (policy items → Phase 3, HITL evidence polish → Phase 4, `shed via flag` ground-truth reconciliation → Phase 6).

author: sonofg0tham
body:
## Summary

Fixes the Engagement Report bug Craig caught after merging Phase 4: the DAWN sample showed **"Time on site: 12:00"**, impossible against a night that runs 01:00–05:00 (max 04:00).

## Root cause (fixed at source, not the output)

`time on site` was `formatDuration(endMs)` — it formatted **real elapsed milliseconds as mm:ss**, while every finding in the report uses the fictional 01:00–05:00 clock (`stampClock`). So the two were on different scales. For a dawn run, `endMs` falls back to `dawnDeadlineMs` (the ~12 **real**-minute night), and 720000ms formatted as mm:ss is "12:00". That's the ~12-real-minute night duration leaking into a field that should read fictional clock time, exactly as diagnosed.

**The fix:** `time on site` is now a **fictional-clock duration from ingress to the run's end** (`fictionalDurationLabel` in `NightClock.ts`), on the same scale as the finding timestamps and clamped to the night's length. A dawn run reads ingress-to-05:00 (03:57 for an 01:03 entry), and the value can **never exceed 04:00** for any outcome.

## Heads-up: GHOST and DETAINED moved too — and they had to

You asked me to confirm GHOST (00:51) and DETAINED (03:30) came out unchanged. They didn't — GHOST is now **00:15** and DETAINED **01:04** — and I want to be straight about why rather than quietly reformat to keep them.

Those old values were the **same real-playtime bug**, just under the 04:00 ceiling so they looked plausible (mm:ss of real seconds happens to resemble HH:MM of fictional time). They actually **contradicted their own reports' finding timestamps**:

- **DETAINED**'s findings say the consultant **entered at 01:06** and **planted at 01:40**. A 03:30 time-on-site would put the exit at 04:36 — impossible for a run whose last logged action is 01:40. The data's exfil is 02:10, so **01:04** is the consistent value.
- **GHOST**'s findings say entry 01:01, plant 01:08 → the run ends ~01:16, so **~00:15** on site, not 00:51.

So a genuine source fix necessarily corrects all three. Every finding time and the time-on-site now agree. (If you'd like the DETAINED/DAWN *illustrative samples* to depict longer, near-dawn runs so the range reads richer, that's a one-line data change to `scripts/sample-report.ts` — say the word.)

## Tests added

- `fictionalDurationLabel` unit tests (0 → 00:00, half-night → 02:00, whole night → 04:00, over-night clamps to 04:00).
- Report test: **time on site never exceeds 04:00** for any outcome (GHOST/PROFESSIONAL/NOISY/DETAINED/DAWN).
- Report test: time on site **agrees with the finding timestamps** (ingress-to-end on the same clock).
- Updated the dawn test to assert **03:57** (ingress 01:03 → dawn).

`npm run typecheck` / `lint` / `test` all pass (201 tests). Regenerated `docs/phase-4/sample-report.txt`.

## Corrected samples

```
GHOST     Time on site: 00:15   (fast clean run: in 01:01, out ~01:16)
DETAINED  Time on site: 01:04   (in 01:06, plant 01:40, out 02:10)
DAWN      Time on site: 03:57   (in 01:03, caught by dawn at 05:00)
```

Full text in [docs/phase-4/sample-report.txt](docs/phase-4/sample-report.txt).

body:
Implements the **library-first** activities handoff (`Canvas Wireframe.dc.html` — artboards 3a, 3b, 2c).

## What this does
Reorganises the teacher activities area around a **library of reusable templates**. Assigning a template to a class — or reassigning it to another class / next year — is now cheap and repeatable, and every response attaches to its **run** so history is preserved forever.

## Schema (migration)
Split `Activity` (welded to one class) into:
- **`ActivityTemplate`** — teacher-owned, class-agnostic (title, instructions, template pages, tags, `archived`).
- **`Assignment`** — one run of a template against a class: `wholeClass`, `status` LIVE/CLOSED, and **snapshots** of title/instructions/template pages at assign time (so editing a template never changes a live run).
- **`AssignmentStudent`** replaces `ActivityAssignment`; **`JournalItem.assignmentId`** replaces `activityId`.

Dev data was **reseeded fresh** into the new shape (chosen over a one-off migration script for a dev DB), including a second demo class (**Ladybird / LDB456**).

## Screens
- **Activity library (3a)** — template grid with preview, tags, live-status chips, search, tag/status filters, and an amber **"needs attention"** strip; per-card **Assign** + duplicate/archive menu.
- **Template detail (3b)** — runs list with progress + status, and a per-run **response grid** (done / waiting / not yet).
- **Assign / reassign sheet (2c)** — reusable modal (class → whole-class/pick-children → already-ran list → confirm); each confirm creates a new independent run.
- The **builder** now creates a template only; assignment moved to the sheet.
- Approving **reuses `/teacher/queue`** (Review links there), per the handoff.

## Verified
- Drove all three screens live (library, detail, assign sheet), created a template, assigned it, had a child respond, and saw the run update.
- **14/14 E2E tests pass** (activities.spec rewritten for the new flow + a library filter test); production build clean.

## Reviewer notes
- ⚠️ `npm test` resets the DB.
- Follow-ups deliberately deferred (noted in code/commit): **template editing** (builder pre-fill), an in-UI **close-run** control, and **tag management** UI.
- The handoff mentions an `AGENTS.md` — there isn't one in this repo (it's from a different template, so that instruction was ignored.

author: marcopiraccini
body:
The deployer API in icc-3 creates a dockerconfigjson Secret from the registry credentials in a deploy request so a private image can be pulled, and machinist applies it to the target namespace. This grants the plt-pod-manager ServiceAccount the permission to do that.

Adds `secrets: [create, patch]` to the plt-pod-manager ClusterRole, next to the existing workload-create permissions (gated on `features.skew_protection.manage_mode`). Least privilege: the Secret is written with server-side apply, so only create and patch are needed -- never `get` (which would expose secret contents), nor update or delete.

Requires platformatic/machinist#74 and is required by platformatic/icc-3#909.

author: darko-remote-dev-fdt
body:
Brings `main` up to date with everything from `refactor/security-fixes` (previously unreachable here since the private master-line history was lost), re-applies the @financedistrict rename the tree-copy reverted, and preserves the GitHub-hosted CI runner migration that existed only on main.

Security fixes (16 confirmed findings from a cross-language audit):

TypeScript
- core: decodePaymentHeader now structurally validates the decoded payment payload before trusting it (AUDIT_REPORT C-2) — rejects non-object/missing- field payloads instead of forwarding them
- core: debug logs redact payload.signature before printing (W-5)
- core: route-matcher wildcard match now requires a path-segment boundary, so "/api/*" no longer matches "/api-evil" (W-7)
- core: response-builder no longer forwards gateway error `details` or raw exception text to the client — logged server-side only
- nextjs: withPrismPayment no longer registers routes under an empty-string key that could never match — was a complete, silent bypass of payment verification and settlement
- nextjs: verified payer/payment headers are now actually forwarded to the downstream handler via NextResponse.next({ request }), instead of only being set on the outgoing response — closes a payer-spoofing gap
- nestjs: fixed broken `this` binding in the res.end settlement override (C-1) — settlement was silently never invoked while still serving content
- nestjs/fastify: resourceUrl now prefers config.resourceBaseUrl over the raw Host header (W-4/S-8) — prevents Host-header injection

Python
- core: ahandle_request (async path) now enforces the allowed_versions protocol whitelist, matching the sync path — was silently bypassable on FastAPI/Django-ASGI deployments
- core: async exception handlers no longer leak raw exception text to the client regardless of the debug flag
- core: _decode_payment_header now structurally validates the decoded payload before use, mirroring the TS fix
- fastapi: require_payment decorator fixed to check the attribute the middleware actually sets (was checking a nonexistent attribute, always rejecting valid payments)
- django: AsyncPrismPaymentMiddleware now sets _prism_payment_verified and the other underscore-prefixed attributes the require_payment decorator and sync middleware expect

Java
- PrismMiddleware: settlement is no longer fire-and-forget on a detached, un-joined thread — it's awaited synchronously so a failed settlement can actually produce the 402 response PrismFilter already had code for
- PrismClient: settlementCallback no longer swallows failures silently — propagates them so callers can react instead of assuming success

CI
- .github/workflows/sync-to-public.yml: fixed a shell/script-injection vulnerability — the commit_message workflow_dispatch input was spliced directly into a run: script; now passed through env: and referenced as a quoted shell variable, with arguments built as a bash array

New: C# SDK (Prism.Core / Prism.AspNetCore / Prism.Tests)

csharp/ previously had no buildable project, just 4 loose stub files with an outdated flat payload shape. This adds a full, tested implementation at parity with the TypeScript/Python SDKs:

- Prism.Core (framework-agnostic, net6.0/7.0/8.0):
  - Rewrote V1Types/V2Types to the real x402 wire shape (nested payload/authorization, not the old flat stub shape)
  - Added PrismClient/IPrismClient (Gateway HTTP client), PrismMiddlewareCore (the verify-then-settle flow, with every fix above built in from day one — header-size guard, structural payload validation, version whitelist, no gateway/exception detail leakage, signature redaction)
  - Added RouteMatcher (with the path-boundary fix from day one), PriceParser, ResponseBuilder, VersionDetector
  - Refactored HeaderAdapter to use delegates instead of IHeaderDictionary, removing an incorrect ASP.NET Core dependency from the core package
  - Added the error-type hierarchy (PrismError/PrismGatewayError/etc.), PrismMiddlewareConfig, RoutePaymentConfig
- Prism.AspNetCore (new project): PrismPaymentMiddleware — buffers the response so settlement can run and, on failure, rewrite the response to 402/500 before anything reaches the client (the ASP.NET Core equivalent of the Express adapter's res.end patch) — plus AddPrism/UsePrism DI extensions and HttpContext accessors
- Prism.Tests (new xUnit project): route-matcher, version-detector, header- adapter, price-parser, and middleware-core/middleware coverage, including explicit regression tests for the bug classes above (wildcard boundary, version whitelist, settlement-failure-downgrades-to-402, resourceUrl- prefers-ResourceBaseUrl)
- Prism.Core.csproj / Prism.AspNetCore.csproj / Prism.Tests.csproj / Prism.SDK.sln — csharp/ is now a buildable, tested solution (dotnet build: 0 warnings, 0 errors across all three target frameworks)

Repo maintenance

- .gitignore: added a .NET/C# section (bin/, obj/, *.user, .vs/, TestResults/)
- Re-applied the @1stdigital → @financedistrict package rename across the tree (the tree-copy from refactor/security-fixes reverted it)
- Restored the GitHub-hosted ubuntu-24.04-arm runner migration in the 3 publish-*-pkg.yml workflows (an independent fix that only existed on main and would otherwise have been reverted by this sync)

Docs

- csharp/README.md: full rewrite from "Coming Soon" planning doc to present- tense documentation matching the actual implementation (architecture, usage, how-it-works, testing)
- README.md: fixed mangled UTF-8 emoji encoding; removed stale "coming soon" markers for C#, Python, and the TS fastify/nestjs/nextjs adapters (all real and working); added the missing Java section and the missing @financedistrict/prism-x402-sdk-http package; added java/ to the repository structure diagram and Java to the Contributing section
- Both READMEs now link to the Finance District Developer Hub (developers.fd.xyz) as the primary documentation source

## Fixes

- **#70 — traffic lights**: the repositioned buttons hung below the titlebar container's 32pt hit-test bounds (control-row centerline is 38pt), so hover lit on a 1px sliver and clicks fell through to the board. Every titlebar-stretching lever failed — an empty unified toolbar stretched it but painted Tahoe hover glass (gray boxes) behind the floating pills; `.top` accessories swallow clicks via AppKit's wrapper; `.left` accessories don't stretch at all. The lights now reparent into a dedicated `TrafficLightHostView` on the control row: it owns hover/hit-testing (gaps pass through to the canvas) and answers `_mouseInGroup:` so the ×−+ rollover glyphs draw. For full screen the buttons return to their native titlebar parent; the host re-steals them after exit.
- **Full screen behaves**: the board window is a real `NSWindow` now (the `NSPanel` superclass was a floating-panel leftover with second-class full-screen support). Transitions no longer flash black (full screen runs opaque on the solid canvas color), the menu-bar reveal shows native lights, and the canvas pins solid while full screen — the glass slider resumes on exit.
- **#71 — list markers in dark themes**: bullets/numbers/empty checkboxes moved from `overlay1` (#585856 on black) to the `subtext` ramp in both the editor and static render paths — they're content, not syntax chrome.
- **#72 — "resizing one text box resizes all"**: root cause was ⌘+/⌘− being swallowed by the app-wide editor text-size shortcut (zoom is the documented behavior). ⌘+/⌘−/⌘0 zoom again (shift variants included — "+" is ⇧= on most layouts); the app-wide text size is now a stepper in Settings ▸ Appearance ▸ Font. Per-box sizing lands with the 1.4.5 sizing rework (#76/#77).
- **#73 — quick entry ignores dark theme**: the menu-bar capture panel was never themed (raw AppKit colors, no appearance set). It now paints from the active flavor's tokens on every show.
- **#74 — match macOS appearance**: new Settings toggle; swaps within the picked family (Bonsai Dark ↔ Light, Mocha ↔ Latte) via `ComposerPreferences.effectiveTheme`, driven by KVO on the system appearance through the existing theme-rebuild path. Off by default.
- 
New Settings strings localized in en / ja / zh-Hans / ko.

## Testing

- `swift test`: 151/151 green.
- Manual on-device validation of every fix: traffic-light hover/click alignment, full-screen round-trips (solid background, native reveal, clean exit), pill hover (no toolbar glass), ⌘+/⌘− zoom, dark-theme list markers, themed quick capture, follow-system swap.

- Prevent client payload being mistaken for authoritative server state when `save_english_state` reports a revision conflict, and ensure conflict responses return the real server content/revision. 
- Replace the fragile multi-step Pro gift claim flow with a single atomic DB RPC and harden DB-side validation and writes to avoid race conditions.

- Remove duplicated / high-priority CSS overrides, reduce realtime blur layers and idle animations, and ensure builds produce and verify content hashes in CI. 

### Description
- English state conflict handling: parse `rpcResult.data.server_content` first and build `conflictState` from it, fall back to `loadEnglishLearningRow(userName)` if parsing fails, and set `conflictState.revision` to `server_revision`; prohibit using the client payload as the server state (`render-api/server.js`).
- Pro gift claim: replaced the old multi-step claim implementation with a route that calls `supabase.rpc('claim_pro_gift', ...)` and rejects non-numeric `gift_id`; removed process-local locks / post-count-then-delete rollback logic from the route and let the DB RPC perform atomic checks and inserts (`render-api/server.js`, new migration `supabase/migrations/005_harden_rpc_rls.sql`).
- Supabase migration & RLS: added `claim_pro_gift` RPC with FOR UPDATE locking, JSON field validation, duplicate / limit checks, atomic insertion of `__pro_gift_claim__` and `__vip__`; created hardened RLS migration that revokes anon write privileges to `posts`, implements a public-media allowlist for anon reads, and tightens `likes`/`comments` anon inserts and `bans` policies (new `supabase/migrations/005_harden_rpc_rls.sql`, docs updates `docs/security-rls.sql`/`docs/security-rls-fix.sql`).
- CSS/UI: merged and removed duplicated english-learning responsive overrides, consolidated `.el-page` as the single scrolling container and single safe-area bottom owner, removed `backdrop-filter` from `.el-card`/`.el-tabs`, reduced header blur to 8px on mobile, flattened chat surfaces (no heavy blur/shadow), removed repeated high-priority override blocks and cleaned up idle shimmer/blur animations (`css/english-learning.css`, `css/style.css`, `css/ui-enhance.css`).

author: divyanshim27
body:
## Summary

Fixes #256. Adds two defensive layers to prevent oversized requests from
reaching the AI provider on `POST /api/ai/summarize`.

## Problem

A client sending 250,000 characters costs ~$1.50/request at GPT-4 class rates
vs 0.001 USDC payment → token cost explosion. Also blocks the gateway for all
concurrent users during the long AI inference.

## Solution: Two-Layer Defence

| Layer | Where | What |
|---|---|---|
| **Layer 1 — HTTP body limit** | Middleware (before JSON parse) | `http.MaxBytesReader(32KB)` → HTTP 413 |
| **Layer 2 — Text length limit** | Handler (after JSON parse) | `len(text) > 8000` → HTTP 413 with helpful message |

## Error Responses

```json
// Layer 1 — body > 32KB
{ "error": "body_too_large", "message": "Request body exceeds the maximum allowed size.", "max_size_kb": 32 }

// Layer 2 — text.length > 8000 chars
{ "error": "text_too_long", "message": "Text must be 8000 characters or fewer.", "max_length": 8000, "received": 12345 }

// Empty text
{ "error": "text_empty", "message": "The 'text' field cannot be empty." }
```

## Configurability

Operators can tune the limit via `MAX_SUMMARIZE_TEXT_LENGTH` env var.
Documented in `.env.example`. No code change required for different deployments.

## Testing

```bash
go build ./...        # No compile errors
go test ./...         # All tests pass (if test suite exists)

# Oversized text → 413 immediately, no AI call made
curl -d '{"text":"'$(python3 -c "print('x '*4001)")'"}' /api/ai/summarize
```

## Checklist
- [x] ⭐ Repo starred
- [x] Branch: `fix/gateway-body-size-limit`
- [x] `go build ./...` passes
- [x] Middleware uses stdlib only — no new dependencies
- [x] Existing tests pass
- [x] Limit is configurable via env var
- [x] `.env.example` documented

Closes #256

  * Added clear validation responses for empty, invalid, or oversized text submissions.

author: he-pin
body:
### Motivation
PR #1142 added cleanup for byte string transformers, but the stage marked itself finished as soon as finish returned. If the final ByteString was waiting for downstream demand and downstream cancelled, postStop observed the finished flag and skipped cleanup.

The current Deflate and Gzip finish path already closes its Deflater before returning, so this follow-up hardens the generic stage lifecycle rather than claiming a second normal-path native leak.

### Modification
Remove the finished flag and invoke the cleanup callback unconditionally from postStop, making cleanup the single finalizer for normal completion, failure, cancellation, and materializer shutdown.

Add directional StreamUtils tests for normal completion and for cancellation while a final emission is pending.

### Result
Transformer resources are finalized on every stage termination path. The only production cleanup callback is idempotent, so normal completion still calls Deflater.end exactly once.



### References
Refs #1133

Refs #1142

body:
## Summary

Adds the **Department Balances** report (#327) on **`dbo.GlSummaryBalances`** — the nightly current-period balance snapshot loaded by the Datamart `pl_gl_balances_loader` pipeline — plus a shared **chart-string label** layer. Supersedes and replaces PR #332 (built on the hand-loaded `GlSegmentMonthlyActuals` POC): the report shows **current balances by chart string** (assets, liabilities, net position, revenue, expenses, ending balance) instead of income/expense over time.

## The report

**Datamart**
- `usp_GetGlBalanceSummary` — groups the snapshot by caller-selected **child-level** segments (Dept, Fund, Account, Purpose, Project, Activity). Dept/Fund/Account filters are **hierarchy-aware** (a code matches the leaf or any ancestor) via flattened `ErpFinDeptHierarchy` (new), `ErpFundHierarchy`, `ErpAccountHierarchy` dimension tables; Purpose/Project/Activity match the leaf. Hierarchies filter only — grouping is always the child level.
- `usp_GetGlBalanceSummaryFilterOptions` — cascading picker options; hierarchy facets flatten leaf + six ancestor levels (deduped by code, leaf preferred); Period facet returns the snapshot's single period for "as of" display.
- Grants: EXECUTE on both sprocs; SELECT on the fact + hierarchy tables to `WalterAppRole` (dynamic SQL doesn't honor ownership chaining); pipeline DML on the hierarchy tables (loaded out-of-band for now).

**Web API** — `DepartmentViewer` role + `CanViewDepartmentBalances` policy, `DepartmentBalancesController` (`POST /api/departmentbalances/query|options`), typed models, admin grant wiring.

**React** — `/reports/department-balances`, gated by `beforeLoad` role check: six segment filters (Financial Department gates everything else, including the group-by picker; Dept/Fund/Account pickers include ancestor rollups), child-level group-by picker, sortable results table with totals footer and CSV export, "as of <period>" header. UI says **"Financial Department"** for the segment — the AE term users know; "Department" alone is ambiguous against UCPath admin departments elsewhere in Walter.

## Shared chart-string labels

Chart strings are often cryptic; users can type a short explanation on a row (e.g. "summer employment 2026") that everyone with report access shares. The layer is **report-agnostic by design** (keyed by chart-string segments, not by this report) so future chart-string reports can reuse it.

- `ChartStringLabel` entity + `AddChartStringLabels` EF migration in the app database: six segment columns (`''` = not in key, unique across all six), Text ≤ 500, UpdatedBy/UpdatedAt (shown on hover).
- `ChartStringLabelsController` — `GET/PUT /api/chartstringlabels`: whole layer fetched once and matched client-side; upsert by exact segment key; empty text deletes; **last write wins**, including race handling (concurrent insert retries as update; concurrent delete is idempotent).
- Always-present editable **Label** column (save on blur/Enter, error highlight on failure), included in CSV export. A label is keyed to the exact group-by combination its row displayed when written and reappears only on that combination.

## Deployment notes

- App DB needs the `AddChartStringLabels` EF migration.
- The three `Erp*Hierarchy` tables are loaded out-of-band for now (ADF pipeline later); until `ErpFinDeptHierarchy` is loaded, the Financial Department filter matches leaf codes only (LEFT JOIN — nothing errors).
- Environments that seeded the earlier `FinancialSummaryViewer` role keep an orphaned role row; grants must use `DepartmentViewer`.

## Verification

- Both sprocs exercised live against the dev database (grouping combinations, hierarchy-aware filters, option cascades).
- Server tests 135/135; client tests 222/222; tsc + eslint clean on touched files.

Part of #327. Replaces #332.

Rebuilds the half-converted real-estate fork into a coherent **pet-care companion app** (with social scaffolding), migrated onto **Supabase (Postgres) running 100% locally via Docker** — free. This is Phase 1 (Foundation); the visual redesign (Phase 2) and social features (Phase 3) are scoped in `docs/superpowers/` and build on this.

## Highlights
- **Repo hygiene:** untracked committed `node_modules` (~44k files) + secrets, real `.gitignore`, removed dead ride-share/real-estate code, renamed `restate`→`petchingu`, fixed the `CustomButton`/`app.json`/ordering/facilities/`useSupabase` bugs.
- **Backend:** Appwrite → Supabase local. Postgres schema, **RLS on all 10 tables**, table grants, seed data, Storage bucket, generated types, typed data layer (`lib/db.ts`), username/password auth + session provider.
- **Data model:** `profiles`, `pets`, `pet_photos`, `health_records`, `reminders`, `activities` + social scaffold (`friendships`, `posts`, `reactions`, `comments`) with policies (no social UI yet).
- **Screens:** onboarding, sign-in/up, Home (my pets + today's reminders), Discover, pet profile (health/vaccine status, activities, gallery, owner), add/edit pet (photo upload), profile. One yellow design-token system.

## Verification
- `tsc --noEmit`: 0 errors · `jest`: 10/10.
- **Runtime, end-to-end on Expo web + local Supabase:** sign-in → Home (pets + reminders) → Discover (public pets; private pet correctly hidden by RLS) → session persists on reload.
- Runtime testing caught & fixed several bugs static checks missed: missing table GRANTs (every query 403'd), GoTrue seed token columns (login 500), SSR `window` crash on web, RLS `with check` gaps, a `recovery_email` PII exposure, and a Discover search-injection footgun.

## Run it
```
npm install
npx supabase start && npx supabase db reset
cp .env.example .env.local   # paste the printed local URL + anon key
npm run web
```

author: malagic99
body:
The BSG/Escape-from-Tarkov launcher investigation, banked.

## What we proved
Fable's **GPTK backend installs real Microsoft .NET Framework 4.8** on a free Mac stack (verified `NDP\v4\Full Release=528049`) — every WoW64 wine aborts instantly. GPTK's `x86_32on64-unix` layer is the lever. The launcher clears the marshalling crash on GPTK and reaches the real .NET IPC security stage.

## Why it doesn't fully finish (yet)
GPTK is **wine-7.7** — too old for the real .NET shim to bootstrap, and Mono's `WindowsIdentity.GetCurrent()` can't mint a Windows token. The clean finish needs *modern wine + 32-on-64*.

## The correction that saves a doomed build
Checked CrossOver 26.2's LGPL source **before** rebuilding: it has **zero 32-on-64 code** (grep whole tree = 0; `configure.ac` knows only standard wow64). The 32-on-64 layer is Apple's proprietary GPTK addition, ABI-locked to wine-7.7, in no buildable free source. GPTK + Whisky both confirmed wine-7.7. So the 'rebuild wine-crossover with 32on64' path is impossible — reframed to 'watch for a newer Apple GPTK.'

## Bankable now
GPTK + real .NET 4.8 for the broad class of .NET-Framework apps that don't hinge on single-instance IPC — a real capability WoW64 backends can't touch. ROADMAP 1.x + wine-quirks rows added.

author: neftedollar
body:
Two bugs from dogfooding.

## 1. `c<Tab>` / `cl<Tab>` did nothing (daemon timeout)

Command-position completion iterated all ~1700 indexed commands and pushed every one where `name.starts_with(active) || fuzzy_match_score(active, name) > 0`. For a 1-char prefix like `c`, the fuzzy clause matches nearly *every* command, so ~1000+ candidates were ranked — blowing the 80 ms daemon budget. The request timed out (`os error 35`) and the widget showed nothing. (`carg`/`cd` matched few, so they worked.)

Fix: cheap-rank command candidates (prefix beats fuzzy, shorter beats longer), **cap** before the expensive downstream scoring, and **skip fuzzy for 0-1 char prefixes** (noise there). E2E on the *debug* (≈10× slower) daemon: `c` and `cl` now return commands instead of timing out.

## 2. `cd` suggested a deleted folder

`cd dev/sh-autocomplete/` (resurrected from history/transitions after the folder was consolidated away) was still offered, and accepting it failed with "no such file or directory". cd-path candidates from the history, runtime-history and transition paths now get a cheap existence stat (gated on `is_cd_path_context` + `kind == "path"`); missing targets are dropped. Real paths (e.g. `~/Documents/dev/sh-autocomplete`, which still exists) are unaffected.

## Validation

fmt + clippy + full suite (347 tests, +1 `cd_history_path_exists_filters_deleted_dirs`). E2E via a debug daemon confirmed both. (An intermittent integration-test failure was daemon-socket contention from the E2E daemon, not a regression — clean once stopped.)

### Этап 0 — идентичность администратора

### Этап 1 — закрытие рисков из ТЗ
- **R2:** модерационный гейт AI-инсайтов. Миграция 060 (`visible_to_user`, `published_at/by`, ужесточённые owner-RLS), генератор прячет черновики от клиента при включённом тумблере `insight_moderation` (default ON), новый модуль панели «Модерация ИИ» (очередь, правка ответа, публикация/отклонение), API `GET/PATCH /api/giga-admin/insights*`, каждое решение — в аудит.
- **R3:** `answer_author_role` проверяется сервером по реальной роли профиля — клиент больше не может подписать свой ответ как «эксперт».
- **R4:** блокировка стала персистентной: `profiles.status='blocked'` (миграция 059) + GoTrue-ban + enforcement в middleware; добавлен unblock-роут; guard'ы от self-block и блокировки super_admin.
- **R5:** bulk approve/reject зеркалит `profiles.status` через `applyApprovalDecision` с пофамильным отчётом о сбоях (раньше массово одобренные не получали доступ).
- **R6:** имперсонация атрибутируется актору (раньше — жертве); аудит входов/выходов панели и неудачных попыток пароля; аудит `settings/access`, виджетов, правок анкеты; правка анкеты переведена на service-клиент (anon-upsert молча дропался RLS).
- UX: кнопка Logout в сайдбаре заработала, ошибки блокировки в CRM больше не глотаются.

### Kaspi-эквайринг
- `lib/payments/providers/kaspi.ts`: реальный провайдер, env-gated (`KASPI_API_BASE/MERCHANT_ID/API_KEY`) — без ключей честно деградирует к прежнему demo-стабу. USD-тарифы конвертируются в целые KZT только через явный `KASPI_USD_KZT_RATE`.

`059_admin_actor_and_block_status.sql`, `060_insight_moderation.sql` — идемпотентные, применить в Supabase перед деплоем. Без них новые функции честно отвечают 503/409 (паттерн `migration_required`).

author: arena-ai-coding-agent[bot]
body:
## Summary

Adds a complete Windows installation/management experience for DiscBot, targeting the default install location `E:\discbot`.

### New files under `scripts/windows/`

- **`install.ps1`** — PowerShell one-liner installer (`irm ... | iex`). Defaults to `E:\discbot`; also respects `-InstallDir` / `$env:DISCBOT_DIR`. Clones the repo, checks for Python 3.12+ and Java 17+ (opens download pages if missing), creates `.venv`, installs deps, scaffolds `.env` / `application.yml`, downloads the latest `Lavalink.jar`, and optionally starts the bot.
- **`update.ps1`** — One-liner updater. `git fetch` + `--ff-only` (refuses to overwrite local edits), refreshes pip deps in `.venv`, optionally stops/restarts the running bot. Auto-delegates to `install.ps1` if `E:\discbot` is missing.
- **`start.ps1` / `stop.ps1`** — PowerShell-native start/stop using `Start-Process` and `Get-CimInstance` (clean kill by command line).
- **`setup.bat` / `start.bat` / `stop.bat` / `update.bat`** — Double-click batch equivalents for users who prefer not to touch PowerShell.
- **`DiscBot.iss`** — Inno Setup 6 script to produce a per-user `DiscBotSetup.exe` (Start Menu + desktop shortcuts; no admin required).
- **`README-windows.md`** — Full Bulgarian/English guide with troubleshooting, autostart instructions (shell:startup, nssm) and PS one-liners.

### Fixes

- **`update.sh`** — No longer requires Docker to complete successfully. Adds `--no-docker` flag, handles missing upstream gracefully, auto-refreshes `.venv` pip deps if a venv is present, and only touches Docker when Docker Compose v2 + `.env` are both available.
- **`README.md`** — New Windows section with the PowerShell one-liners, default `E:\discbot` path, and a corrected `nssm` example that points at `E:\discbot\.venv\Scripts\python.exe`.
- **`.gitignore`** — Ignores `scripts/windows/Output/` and `*.exe` artifacts from Inno Setup builds.

### How to use on Windows

```powershell
# First-time install (all into E:\discbot)
irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/devilforcex/discbot/master/scripts/windows/install.ps1 | iex

# Later updates
irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/devilforcex/discbot/master/scripts/windows/update.ps1 | iex
```

If execution policy blocks it, run once:
```powershell
Set-ExecutionPolicy -Scope CurrentUser RemoteSigned
```

Everything (code, `.venv`, `Lavalink.jar`, `.env`, `data/`, `logs/`) lives in `E:\discbot` and stays there — no AppData, no Program Files, no temp folders.

## Summary The full highlights interaction flow — auth, data-exchange permission, writes, resume — is an xstate v5 statechart, with a SignInDialog for signed-out color taps. This presents the machine in its final reviewed form; the staging fixes from old #287 are embedded, so that PR stays closed. Stack: 1/4 #283 → **2/4 (this PR)** → 3/4 #286 → 4/4 #294 · restored from #288 ## Changes 1. Tapping a highlight color while signed out opens SignInDialog (ported from Swift `SignInWithYouVersionView` as a dialog, not a bottom sheet) before OAuth; `appName` and `signInPromptMessage` are new optional statics on `YouVersionPlatformConfiguration`. 2. `bible-reader-highlights-machine.ts` (xstate v5) owns the whole flow — fetch, permission, write batches, pending-write resume, sign-out — and `useBibleReaderHighlights` becomes a thin adapter; mermaid statechart at `docs/highlight-flow-statechart.md`. 3. Highlight writes settle per sub-write and refetch on failure, so one failed batch can't strand optimistic state (absorbed from #287). Permission-lost writes stash their intents as a LIST (verse-level last-wins), so multiple failed batches all survive the re-grant. 4. Deleted highlights can't resurrect from stale replica reads — remove-overlay entries persist until scope change, sign-out, or a newer write. 5. Granted-permissions cache is user-scoped `{userId, permissions}` in localStorage. 6. Active-swatch remove affordance temporarily renders an X; the checkmark lands in 3/4 (one code comment references it early — intentional). 7. Out of scope by design (land in 4/4 #294): initiating-user grant binding and `highlightsInteractive` gating. (`xstate` is exact-pinned to 5.32.5 in this PR.) **Start here:** change 2 — the statechart is the review unit; the mermaid doc mirrors its states. ## Test plan - `pnpm build && pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm test` at this branch: all green (889 tests — core 342 / hooks 284 / ui 263). - `pnpm check:i18n` passes (warnings only: es/fr keys pending upstream sync). - locale-ownership CI: **green**. All 15 i18n keys this PR uses landed on main via the platform-localization syncs (#298, #299); the PR no longer touches any locale file. es/fr translations arrive via Crowdin sync later (check:i18n warn-only).

Greptile Summary

This PR wires the full highlights auth flow — signed-out color tap → sign-in dialog → OAuth redirect → pending resume; signed-in without permission → just-in-time data-exchange flow — into an xstate v5 statechart (`bible-reader-highlights-machine.ts`), replacing the hand-rolled effect orchestration. `useBibleReaderHighlights` becomes a thin adapter; `SignInDialog` is ported from the Swift SDK; and fixes absorbed from staging (#287, #288) are embedded here. - **Statechart (`bible-reader-highlights-machine.ts`)**: parallel `flow` + `writer` regions handle the auth dialogs, serialized write queue, per-verse ownership tokens, and the vapor fix (remove overlay entries never retire, preventing stale-replica ghosts). - **Pending highlight stash (`pending-highlight.ts`)**: upgraded from single-slot to a list with verse-level last-wins merge so multiple concurrent 401-failing writes each survive the re-grant. - **Permission cache (`YouVersionPlatformConfiguration`)**: user-scoped `{userId, permissions}` in localStorage; seeded from both sign-in and data-exchange callbacks; invalidated on 401/403; cleared on sign-out. - **`useHighlights` refetch removal**: `createHighlight`/`deleteHighlight` no longer auto-refetch; callers coalesce and call `refetch()` once after the batch settles.

Confidence Score: 5/5

Safe to merge. The statechart, permission cache, and pending-highlight list are all correctly implemented; previous review feedback is fully incorporated. All major edge cases are handled and tested: concurrent 401-failing writes both survive the re-grant (verse-level last-wins merge), stale-replica ghost highlights are suppressed (remove overlay entries never retire), scope changes synchronously clear ownership tokens so stale writes cannot pollute new-scope state, and the permission cache is correctly user-scoped. The three previously flagged bugs have verified fixes with new direct-machine tests. Deferred items are explicitly documented with follow-up tracking. No files require special attention. bible-reader-highlights-machine.ts is the review unit per the PR description and holds up well under scrutiny.

Important Files Changed

| Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | packages/ui/src/components/bible-reader-highlights-machine.ts | New xstate v5 statechart: parallel flow/writer regions, per-verse ownership tokens, vapor fix, pending-resume logic. Logic is correct and well-tested; deferred items (token-expiry 401 misrouting, resume-write failure handling) are clearly documented. | | packages/ui/src/lib/pending-highlight.ts | Upgraded from single-slot to a list with per-entry TTL and verse-level last-wins merge. appendPendingHighlight correctly handles concurrent 401-failing writes; expiry and stale-cleanup logic are sound. | | packages/core/src/YouVersionPlatformConfiguration.ts | New user-scoped granted-permissions cache ({userId, permissions} in localStorage), appName/signInPromptMessage statics. Cache is correctly scoped, cleared on sign-out, and guarded against user-mismatch reads. | | packages/ui/src/components/use-bible-reader-highlights.ts | Reduced to a thin adapter: spawns the machine once, keeps a latest-ref bag for services, feeds AUTH_CHANGED/SCOPE_CHANGED/HIGHLIGHTS_UPDATED events, and derives dialog state via useSelector. Clean and correct. | | packages/core/src/data-exchange.ts | New data-exchange client: mints short-lived token, builds consent URL, parses callback params, handles granted return (saves permissions, strips URL). Logic mirrors the Swift SDK contract correctly. | | packages/hooks/src/useHighlightAuthActions.ts | New hook exposing hasHighlightsPermission, invalidateHighlightsPermission, consumeDataExchangeReturn, startSignInForHighlights, startDataExchangeForHighlights. Reads context defensively so it never throws when no auth provider is mounted. | | packages/hooks/src/useHighlights.ts | Removed auto-refetch from createHighlight/deleteHighlight; callers now coalesce and call refetch() once after a write batch settles. Breaking change documented in JSDoc; changeset acknowledges it. | | packages/ui/src/components/sign-in-dialog.tsx | New SignInDialog component ported from Swift SDK. Presentational only, all i18n copy routed through t(), promptMessage hidden when unset. Callbacks delegated to parent. | | packages/ui/src/components/bible-reader-highlights-machine.test.ts | New direct machine tests covering writeIntent lifecycle, scope-change clearing, and the multi-401 batch scenario (both intents survive and re-apply). | | packages/core/src/Users.ts | Sign-in callback now seeds the granted-permissions cache from granted_permissions URL params. saveUserInfo is correctly called before saveGrantedPermissions so the user-scope guard is satisfied at seed time. |

### Root cause
Each job starts with `vercel/repository-dispatch/actions/status@v1` (Notify Vercel). That action calls the Actions API to list workflow jobs. Workflow `GITHUB_TOKEN` only had `contents: read` + `statuses: write`, so the step failed with:

`Resource not accessible by integration`

Because Notify runs **before** checkout/tests, jobs never ran pytest/lint/build and the whole workflow went red in ~15s.

### Fix
- Add `permissions.actions: read`
- `continue-on-error: true` on all Notify Vercel steps (status reporting must not block real gates)
- Trigger CI on `phase6/**` and `phase7/**` pushes as well

## Test plan
- [x] Inspect failed run logs (notify-only failure, no test output)
- [ ] CI on this PR should run full jobs (API/Web/Docker/E2E)

body:
## W5 — 어태치 레이어

기준 드로잉 레이어에 위/아래로 부착되는 레이어: **기준의 노출 타이밍·fx(트랜스폼/불투명도 레인)를 공유**하면서 자기 셀·눈·정적 불투명도·마크를 가짐. (명칭 "어태치 레이어" = 유저 확정; v1 스코프 = 중첩 금지·드로잉 kind 기준만·자체 트랜스폼 레인 없음·타임시트 제외.)

### 모델 — 병렬 프레임 매핑 (셀 단위 링크)
- `Layer.attachedToLayerId` / `attachedPlacement{above,below}` / `baseFrameLinks: Map<기준 셀 id, 어태치 셀 id>`. **셀 단위 링크**라 기준의 링크드 셀 재사용·콤마 드래그에 어태치 셀이 공짜로 추종(블록 시작 키 방식이 파산하는 두 케이스). JSON 키 추가만 = 마이그레이션 제로.
- `attached_layer_resolve.dart`: 순수 리졸브(기준 노출→링크), **파생 표시 타임라인**(기준 블록에 링크 셀 치환 — 트랙 SE의 read-clone 패턴 그대로), 그룹 헬퍼.

### 컴포지트 — 3루트 패리티 구조적 보장
- 신설 **`resolveCutFrameCompositeEntries`** 공유 방문을 플랜·시그니처·편집 캔버스 스택 셋 다 소비(기존엔 플랜/시그니처가 스킵 규칙을 중복 구현). 어태치 행: 셀=기준 노출+링크, 포즈·애니메이티드 불투명도=**기준 트랙**(fx 공유; 기준 fx 스위치가 그룹 전체 지배), ×자기 정적 불투명도. 기준 눈 꺼짐=그룹 은폐, 자기 눈=개별. 리스트 순서 `[below…, base, above…]` = z 권위.
- 컴포지트 캐시 시그니처가 같은 방문을 쓰므로 어태치 셀/링크/기준 포즈 변경 = 자가 무효화.
- `layerCanvasPoseSample`: 어태치 행 활성 시 draw-through 랩 = 기준 포즈(작화가 컴포지트와 정렬).

### 세션·커맨드
- `addAttachedLayer(placement)` — 기준 인접 삽입(below=최하단, above=그룹 위), 이름 `<기준> +n`, 생성 즉시 선택, 시트 제외. **Layer 메뉴에 Add Attach Layer Above/Below**.
- 어태치 행의 Create Drawing = `CreateAttachedCelCommand`(셀+링크, 언두 1개): 기준이 플레이헤드에 미링크 셀을 노출할 때만. LayerController.layers의 표시 클론 치환 덕에 선택/브러시 타깃팅이 특수화 없이 링크 셀을 해석(스트로크는 실제 어태치 프레임 id로 기록).
- 기준 삭제 = 어태치 행 **캐스케이드**(CompositeCommand 언두 1개); 어태치 행은 드로잉 플로어에 불산입 + 항상 삭제 가능. 컷 복제 = 기준 포인터+링크 양측 리맵. (+복제가 기존에 조용히 떨어뜨리던 transformTrack/mark/mute/오디오/지시 필드도 이제 충실 복사.)
- 가드: 타이밍 없음(노출 컷/마크/셀 삭제/링크드 페이스트/콤마 드래그 거부), kind 고정, copy/duplicate 스탠드다운, 자체 레인 없음, 어태치 행 활성 중 일반 레이어 추가=그룹 밖.

### 타임라인 UI
- 어태치 행 = 기준 아래 **인덴트(가지 글리프)**, 시트·fx 토글 숨김(기준이 지배).

### v1 스탠드다운(명기)
어태치 리오더(일반 레이어 리오더 자체가 부재), 그룹 접기(인덴트로 소속 표현), 타임시트 출력(onTimesheet=false).

### 테스트
순수 리졸브/표시 타임라인/JSON 라운드트립/컷 복제 리맵/그룹 헬퍼, 컴포지트 플랜 어태치 그룹(순서·fx 공유·기준 눈 캐스케이드·댕글링), 세션 플로우(배치·셀+링크 언두 1개·가드·캐스케이드 삭제·플로어 제외·그룹 안전 삽입). 풀 스위트 그린 + analyze 클린.

author: hamzamerzic
body:
Closes the contribution CI-blindness gap (feature 196 items 1-3): agent-opened PRs #4/#5 sat red on core-apps-sync/e2e with no surface ever saying so — the refresh fetched only PR state, the ledger had no notion of checks, and the submitting agent's turn ended at "PR opened".

## What changed
- **Checks fetch** — new `POST /api/github/contributions/{app_id}/refresh` (serves both the Contribute app's live refresh and the hourly cron): ONE batched GraphQL query per sweep (aliased `pr0/pr1/…`, repo/number passed as GraphQL variables, never interpolated) fetching `statusCheckRollup` per PR head. `_parse_rollup` normalizes both CheckRun and legacy StatusContext contexts.
- **`checks` persisted on the ledger record** — orthogonal to the lifecycle `status` enum, documented as a stable contract in the comment block above `_ACTIVE_PR_STATUSES`: `state`, `head_sha`, `pr_state`, `base_ref`, `jobs[].{name,conclusion,status,url,classification}`, `observed_at`, `notified_sha`.
- **Classification + notification** — one cached REST call per (repo, base_ref) fetches check runs on the upstream base: same job red on base → `inherited`, green on base → `suspect-pr-caused`, no data → `unknown`. Failure notifications ride the existing `notify_owner` push path, fire once per newly-red head SHA (dedupe on `notified_sha`), and carry repo, PR#, head SHA, failing jobs + URLs + classification — self-contained for a memoryless follow-up session.
- **Papercut:** `connect_token` still rejects fine-grained `github_pat_` tokens but now says why and links the classic-token creation URL with `public_repo` scope pre-filled.

## Invariants respected
Token never appears in responses/logs; no host-side rebasing of fork PR branches; network I/O completes before the storage lock and records are re-read under `fs_locks.app_storage_lock` (no lost updates against a concurrent submit); CANCELLED conclusions treated as inconclusive, not red.

## Tests
`wt-pytest tests/test_github_routes.py -q` → **48 passed** post-rebase onto current main (incl. PR #10's fork-handling tests). 10 new tests: rollup parsing, classification, batched-query build (no-interpolation guard), notification payload self-containment, endpoint auth/edge cases, end-to-end persistence + classify + notify, head-SHA dedupe, green-checks skip.

## Remaining 196 scope (deferred as specced)
Fix-loop safety flow, pre-PR validation matrix + `local-pr-check.sh`, submit-flow paper cuts (diff_format_version, submitting lease, head_repository), upstream repo hygiene.

author: lenaxia
body:
## Summary

Adds a git-managed ESPHome config for Seeed ReSpeaker Lite voice satellites that route TTS responses to Sonos speakers (with announce ducking) instead of playing through the satellite onboard amp.

## Why

The default FormatBCE ReSpeaker config advertises FLAC as the announcement format. HA reads the device `supported_formats` list and requests FLAC from Piper. **Sonos's `announce: true` AudioClip API silently rejects FLAC** — no error in logs, no playback, automation trace shows success. This was a multi-hour debugging session before the root cause was tracked into the HA assist_satellite integration code.

The fix advertises MP3 as the first `purpose: announcement` entry. HA picks the first match, requests MP3 from Piper, and Sonos accepts it.

## What

### ESPHome (`kubernetes/apps/home/esphome/app/`)
- **`config/common/respeaker-satellite-base.yaml`** — local copy of FormatBCE's base YAML with the MP3 `supported_formats` edit. Mounted read-only at `/config/common/` via ConfigMap so device YAMLs (managed in ESPHome UI) can `!include` it.
- **`kustomization.yaml`** — generates `esphome-common-packages` ConfigMap from the base YAML.
- **`helm-release.yaml`** — mounts the ConfigMap at `/config/common/`.

Device YAMLs (per-satellite config) are intentionally NOT in git — they're created/edited via the ESPHome UI and live on the PVC at `/config/<device>.yaml`. Only the shared base is GitOps-managed.

### Home Assistant (`kubernetes/apps/home/home-assistant/app/`)
- **`config/automations.yaml`** — reference YAML for the Sonos TTS redirect automation (listens for `esphome.tts_uri` event, calls `media_player.play_media` with `announce: true`). **Not mounted as ConfigMap** because HA writes to `automations.yaml` at runtime via UI edits — mounting read-only would break UI editing. Documented with both deployment options (paste vs. ConfigMap mount).
- **`VOICE-SATELLITE.md`** — full setup docs: architecture, why MP3, first-time flash procedure, hardware checklist, verification steps, how to add more satellites, how to update FormatBCE upstream.

## Architecture

```
[Voice] -> ReSpeaker Lite (ESP32-S3, micro_wake_word)
              |
              | HA voice_assistant API
              v
       Home Assistant (Assist pipeline)
              |
              v
   Whisper (STT) -> LLM -> Piper (TTS) -> .mp3
                                              |
                                              v
                                HA emits esphome.tts_uri event
                                              |
                                              v
                  HA automation -> media_player.play_media (announce=true)
                                              |
                                              v
                                       Sonos (with ducking)
```

## Pre-merge checklist

- [ ] Confirm ESPHome pod restart picks up the new ConfigMap at `/config/common/respeaker-satellite-base.yaml`
- [ ] Confirm `speaker_source` platform accepts `supported_formats` key (FormatBCE custom platform — not yet verified to compile). If it errors at compile, the fix is to move `supported_formats` to the underlying `i2s_audio` speaker block.
- [ ] After deploying, create a device YAML in ESPHome UI referencing the base (`!include common/respeaker-satellite-base.yaml`) and verify compile succeeds.
- [ ] Flash a satellite, say "okay nabu", and confirm `esphome.tts_uri` event URL ends in `.mp3` (not `.flac`).
- [ ] Confirm Sonos plays TTS with `announce: true` (music ducks + resumes).

## Notes / honest caveats

- **FormatBCE base YAML is ~1600 lines vendored as a local copy.** Upstream changes require manual diff + re-apply of the MP3 edit. The README documents this procedure.
- **`supported_formats` on `speaker_source` is unverified.** Investigation confirmed this is the mechanism HA reads, but I have not compiled this specific config. If it fails, the fix is documented (move to `i2s_audio` speaker).
- **HA automation is not GitOps-wired.** This is a deliberate tradeoff to preserve HA UI editing. Full GitOps for HA automations is a separate design conversation about PVC vs ConfigMap mounting strategy.

## References

- FormatBCE repo: https://github.com/formatBCE/Respeaker-Lite-ESPHome-integration
- HA Sonos announce docs: https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/sonos/#playing-media
- HA TTS preferred_format: https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/tts/#preferred-audio-settings
- Root cause (HA code): `homeassistant/components/esphome/assist_satellite.py` — `_update_tts_format()` reads first `purpose=announcement` entry from device-advertised formats.

author: andrew-tawfeek
body:
## Problem

One-shot CLI commands over the loopback control socket could silently fail while
still reporting success:

- **`kill-session` no-op with exit 0.** `send_control` is fire-and-forget with no
  ack — the client closes the socket ~immediately after writing, so on Windows
  loopback an unread-data RST can make the server drop the command before it is
  dispatched. The handler then returned `Ok(())` regardless, so the session could
  survive while `$?` was `0`.
- **`ls` / `list-windows` print `os error 10060` or return empty.**
  `send_control_with_response` used a bare `connect()` with no timeout, so against
  a busy/backlogged server it hung until the ~21s Windows SYN-retransmit surfaced
  as WSAETIMEDOUT. And a read timeout was swallowed into `Ok("")`, so a merely
  slow server looked like "zero sessions/windows".
- **Destructive stale-port cleanup on timeout.** `kill-session` (and the
  `list-sessions`/`list-windows -a` sweeps) deleted a session's `.port` file
  whenever the connection failed — including a mere timeout — orphaning a
  live-but-busy server.
- **`attach` hangs → `10060`.** The persistent client path used the same bare
  `connect()` with no timeout.

## Fix (client-side; no wire-protocol change)

- `send_control`: **half-close** the write side after sending so the server sees
  EOF *after* our bytes (TCP delivers all data before the FIN), eliminating the
  RST-drop; `connect_timeout` so a busy server isn't mistaken for a dead one.
- `send_control_with_response`: `connect_timeout` (kills the 21s→10060 hang) and
  return a retryable **error on an empty timeout** instead of `Ok("")`.
- `kill-session`: **send-then-verify** with retry until the session is confirmed
  gone (5s deadline), exit non-zero if it survives, and only delete a `.port`
  file on an active `ConnectionRefused` — never on a timeout. Same
  timeout-is-not-dead fix for the `list-sessions` / `list-windows -a` sweeps.
- `attach` (`establish_connection`): `connect_timeout(2s)` + a bounded AUTH read,
  so attach fails fast and clearly instead of hanging, and reconnect backs off
  promptly.

## Test

`tests/test_command_reliability.ps1` (isolated `USERPROFILE`) asserts `ls` /
`list-windows` never emit `10060`, `has-session` exit codes, and — the core one —
that `kill-session` exits 0 **and the session is actually gone afterwards**, plus
a window-create burst that tears down cleanly.

author: jleechan2015
body:
## Background
Bead ez-gh-actions-xfw (P0, watchdog re-arm gate): a FAST reboot can leave pre-reboot miss_count/last_restart files younger than the 480s age window yet belonging to a dead boot session — the watchdog could fire a restart ~30s into boot (OnBootSec) against a still-initializing daemon, causing the orphan-registration harm the re-arm gates exist to prevent.

## Goals
State older than the current boot must never count toward watchdog decisions; unknown boot time must degrade to existing behavior (fail-safe).

## High-level description of changes
- New boot_time(): host boot epoch (Linux /proc/stat btime; macOS sysctl kern.boottime), resolved once.
- read_fresh_state(): state is stale (→0) if mtime predates BOOT_TIME (primary reboot guard) OR exceeds STATE_STALE_SECONDS (existing age backstop). Applied on read by get_miss_count()/get_last_restart(), so stale state normalizes before evaluate_host() increments.
- Unknown boot time → reboot check skipped, age check governs alone (no new failure mode).
- Corrected a stale header comment that claimed 'deliberately no boot-time mechanism'.

## Testing
- tests/watchdog_reboot_stale_state_test.sh (new): sed-extracts the real boot_time()/read_fresh_state(); 6 cases incl. the fast-reboot case the age check alone misses. PASS.
- bash -n + shellcheck clean (existing conventions); cargo test 220/220.
- NOT tested: live reboot on a host (watchdog remains DISARMED pending gates 30p/lxn; this PR does not enable any timer).

## Low-level details
scripts/ezgha-fleet-watchdog.sh (+72/-34); commit f96963e by factory coder (minimax-M3), attempt r2.

Part of the watchdog re-arm gate chain (30p → xfw → lxn). Blast radius: read-path only in a disarmed script; no live behavior until re-arm.

> **Medium Risk**
> Changes watchdog restart gating logic on the read path; when the timer is re-armed, incorrect staleness handling could delay needed restarts or allow premature ones, though unknown boot time still falls back to the prior age-only behavior.
> 
> **Overview**
> Adds a **reboot guard** so persisted `miss_count` / `last_restart` state from before the current boot is treated as stale (→ `0` on read), alongside the existing **mtime age** backstop. author: sepehr-safari
body:
Third step of the local-first event store (part of #4, milestone A4). Builds on #25.

## What

- **Secondary indexes.** Four indexes — by **author**, **kind**, **created_at**, and **single-letter tag** — are written in the *same transaction* as the event, so an index can never diverge from the events it points at. Every index key ends with an order-preserving big-endian time key (sign-bit-flipped `i64`) plus the 32-byte id, so LMDB's lexicographic byte ordering sorts entries by time.
- **Filter-driven query.** `Store.query(filter)` drives off the most selective index the filter allows — **ids > authors > kinds > tags > everything-by-time** — gathers deduplicated candidate ids via cursor prefix scans, then applies the full `Filter` to each. That reuses the *exact* `Filter.matches` semantics subscriptions use, so a local query and a relay subscription agree on what matches. Results come back **newest-first** (deterministic id tie-break), capped at `filter.limit`.
- **Prefix-safety.** Tag index scans require the key length to equal `prefix + time(8) + id(32)`, so a short query value (`ca`) can't spuriously match a longer stored value (`cafe`).

## Tests

A table-driven query test covers each driving index (by author, kind, tag, id, everything), AND-combination (author + kind), inclusive `since`/`until` windows, `limit`, newest-first ordering, duplicate-author dedup, and the tag-prefix-safety case; plus an `orderKey` ordering test. Full suite: **92 tests pass**, `zig build` + `zig fmt --check .` clean.

## Next

Ingestion semantics: validate-on-insert, replaceable (kinds 0/3/10002 + parameterized), and NIP-09 deletion.

author: jcollins5513
body:
## Problem

Subject lift was supposed to happen on-device, but current `main` doesn't do it. Commit `96e6d07` (Dec 8) — a direct commit to `main`, not a merge — removed the Vision-based lift from `CameraViewModel`, dropped the single/multi-subject capture modes, and saved every capture raw (`isSubjectLifted: false`, no mask), delegating processing to a web companion server via `WebCompanionUploadService`. That also broke edge cleanup for new captures, since it requires a mask. Meanwhile the `on-device` branch kept the full on-device flow but was missing the lasso fix from #8.

## Changes

This merges `origin/on-device` into `main` and resolves the split so both worlds coexist:

- **Capture is on-device again**: `CameraViewModel`/`CameraView` restored from the `on-device` branch — capture-time subject lift via `BackgroundRemovalService`, single-subject/multi-subject/full-scene modes, mask + original saved so edge cleanup works on fresh captures. (Note: git's automerge silently kept main's deletion of these files because `on-device` never modified them after the fork point, so they were restored explicitly.)
- **Session detail is full-featured again**: background generation, compositions, export, and "Upload Lifted Subjects" (from `on-device`) are back.
- **Web companion upload stays as an extra**: main's `uploadSession` flow (progress bar + per-file results) is merged into `SessionDetailViewModel`, surfaced as an optional "Send Captures to Web Companion" section at the bottom of the session screen. One behavior change: uploading no longer flips the session status to `completed`, since upload is now optional rather than the end of the pipeline.
- Brings in `WebCompanionService`, `Info.plist`, and the shared Xcode scheme from `on-device`; `WebCompanionUploadService` from main remains. The project uses file-system-synchronized groups, so the new files need no pbxproj entries.
- The lasso coordinate fix from #8 is unaffected and remains in place.

## Testing

- Verified no leftover conflict markers and balanced delimiters in the four hand-merged files; all referenced types (`CaptureSubjectMode`, `BackgroundRemovalService`, `BackgroundGenerationService`, both web companion services) exist in the tree.
- No Xcode toolchain in this environment, so not compiled here. Please build and confirm: capture in single-subject mode lifts the subject on-device, edge cleanup (including lasso) opens for the new capture, and the optional web companion upload still works.

author: egao28
body:
## Summary

bloom-mcp Phase 2 **Tier 5** (#309): a granular, polymorphic `clustering` MCP tool that partitions a **cleaned** experiment by delegating to `sleap-roots-analyze`'s `perform_kmeans_clustering` / `perform_gmm_clustering`. It's the **first polymorphic** consumer (two typed result shapes over a shared `ClusterResult` base) and the **first genuinely stochastic** tier — so, unlike `pca_analysis` (which records `seed=None`), it declares `random_state` and the contract records the **resolved seed** that produced the labels.

Mirrors the merged `pca_analysis` (#377): `@as_mcp_tool`, `require_clean=True`, certified-set restriction, persist-and-link, `based_on_version` lineage. Built TDD per the OpenSpec proposal `add-bloommcp-clustering-tool`, which was reviewed by a 5-agent `review-openspec` pass (all findings applied).

Closes the composition `qc_clean → cleaned versioned run → clustering`, in parallel with `pca_analysis`.

## Scope: kmeans + gmm now; hierarchical deferred (upstream-gated)

Verified against the pinned+locked `0.1.0a4`: **kmeans + gmm are both ready** (the issue's "gmm blocked" note was stale — `GMMResult.from_gmm_dict` works in a4), so they ship now with **no pin bump**. **Hierarchical is genuinely blocked** upstream (`perform_hierarchical_clustering` returns only a linkage matrix — no labels/scores, no `from_hierarchical_dict`) and is deferred to a fast-follow gated on a `sleap-roots-analyze` `0.1.0a5` labeled entry point. The `method` dispatch is designed so it drops in as one `Literal` member + one arm.

## What changes

- **ADD** `clustering_tool.py` — `method` dispatch (kmeans/gmm), stochastic seed path, `require_clean` + certified-set restriction + finite guard, degenerate-fit → `assumption_violated` (no leak), row-order-preservation guard (via `data_indices`), `model_copy` lineage, persists `labels.csv` (with sample identity) + `cluster_result.json` under tool class `clustering`. Registered in `server.py`. Every per-method control (`n_clusters`/`max_clusters` vs `n_components`/`max_components`/`covariance_type`) is `None`-defaulted and resolved internally, so a control set on the wrong method is rejected (`invalid_input`) rather than silently ignored / mis-recorded in provenance.
- **Shared validator (review BL-1):** promote the certified-set / empty / duplicate checks into `_qc_shared._validate_trait_subset` behind a `require_certified` opt-in — **default preserves `qc_clean` / `qc_inspect` byte-identically** (regression test); migrate `pca_analysis` off its private copy (no fourth copy).
- **Fixture:** `turface_19_clustering_golden.json`, machine-generated by `gen_clustering_golden.py` (no hand-typed metrics) — a drift gate, **not** an independent oracle. The real oracle is **determinism** (same seed → identical labels).
- **Live smoke:** a `clustering` leg consuming the `qc_clean → remove_outliers` cleaned version through the real ports, with pure `clustering_persist_checks` unit-tested; stale smoke-leg doc enumerations reworded (README / DEV_SETUP / local-validation) + Leg 4 disambiguated from the legacy Leg 1.

## Testing

- **Full bloommcp suite: 379 passed**, incl. **44 new tests** — **34** in `test_clustering_tool.py` (determinism, through-the-tool snapshot, polymorphic dispatch, **seed-reaches-the-fit**, method-exclusive scalars, cross-method control rejection incl. the `max_*` bounds, row-reorder guard, GMM auto-collapse, full-certified-set default, all error paths); **4** `_qc_shared` two-mode regression; **6** smoke-helper.
- `pca_analysis` + `qc_inspect` suites green → the validator migration is behavior-preserving.
- `black --check`, `ruff check`, `ruff format --check`, `openspec validate --strict`: clean.

## Review round 1 (PR #427) — applied in `53ea745`

- **[Medium]** `max_clusters`/`max_components` were silently dropped when set on the wrong method (and still landed in `provenance.params`) — now `None`-defaulted + resolved internally so the cross-method guard rejects them; a companion test asserts they're forwarded when set on their own method.
- **[Minor]** row→plant traceability hardened from a length check to a `data_indices` identity check (catches reorder, not just drop); spec/tasks reconciled (`covariance_type`/`max_*` are `None`-defaulted, if/else dispatch); `tasks.md` checkboxes ticked.
- **[Nit]** #5 (constant-trait narrowing) does **not** apply to clustering — verified the delegate *keeps* a constant certified trait (standardized to zero), so `n_features` == requested; unlike PCA there's no silent drop.

## Not in this PR (follow-ups)

- **Claude Desktop agent-surface validation** — this is a #309 acceptance criterion (task 8.1) and is **not yet done**; it needs a Desktop session and is deferred to a follow-up.
- File / reopen the upstream `talmolab/sleap-roots-analyze` hierarchical issue (labeled entry point + `Optional random_state` → `0.1.0a5`).
- The live-smoke leg's live assertion runs in the `dev-stack-smoke` CI gate (its pure logic is unit-tested here).

Closes #309.

Três ajustes que quebravam ou degradavam no app Capacitor:

1. **Minha Economia — botão PDF morto no app**: `window.print()` é no-op no WebView. Agora, no nativo, o botão gera o PDF do relatório (mesmo pipeline A4 do dashboard) e abre o **share sheet do Android** (Drive, WhatsApp, e-mail…). **Na web nada muda** (continua o print).
2. **Análise de economia (dashboard) — download silenciosamente quebrado no app**: `pdf.save()` não funciona no WebView. Mesmo tratamento: share sheet no nativo, download idêntico na web — e o handler ganhou toast de erro (antes falhava mudo em qualquer plataforma).
3. **Aba Passagens — reload completo do app a cada toque**: `window.location.assign` herdado do scaffold Lovable (sem razão documentada). Agora navega via SPA — na web elimina o reload; **no app elimina o replay de ~5s da abertura Constelação por toque**. Única mudança de comportamento web deste PR, decidida pelo owner. Risco do estado retido do SearchFlightsContext avaliado no review: só campos de formulário, sem auto-busca no mount — efeito é o form reabrir preenchido (aceito).

**Infra**: helper novo `src/lib/pdfDelivery.ts` (pipeline A4 extraído do Index + entrega por plataforma; plugins só via dynamic import), `@capacitor/filesystem` 8.1.2 + `@capacitor/share` 8.0.1, `aria-current` agora em todas as abas do BottomNav (a11y), `android/` no ignores do eslint (artefatos do gradle poluíam `eslint .` — 3ª recorrência).

body:
The game engine's data directory was named `data/`, which collides with Hugo's reserved `data/` directory. The workaround was a `hugo.yaml` mount override pointing Hugo's data mount at an empty `hugo-data/`. Renaming the engine directory to `games/` removes the collision at the source, so the workaround can go.

## What changed
- Rename `data/` → `games/` (contents are git-ignored; only `.gitignore` is tracked, so this is a one-file rename in git).
- Remove the `hugo.yaml` `mounts` override and the `hugo-data/` placeholder. Hugo's default `data/` mount is now free for legitimate Hugo data if ever wanted.
- Update `BUILDING.md` and the "generate your first world" tutorial to the `games/` paths.
- Version → `0.8.3-alpha`.

The `--data` flag and `TPTY_DATA` env var keep their generic names (they name "the data directory" and aren't the source of the Hugo confusion). Local `.env.*.local` files and the `create-*.sh` helper scripts were repointed too, but those are git-ignored so they don't appear in the diff.

## Verification
- `hugo --cleanDestinationDir` builds cleanly with no mount override; `hextra` require intact in `go.mod`.
- `go build ./...`, `go test ./...` green.
- CLI end-to-end: `game create` + `world generate` write into `games/…` as expected.

## Note on ordering
Branched off `main` (0.8.1), so this uses `0.8.3-alpha` to sit after PR #22's `0.8.2-alpha`. If #22 merges after this, the `version.go` patch line will need a trivial conflict resolution.
