author: walkmanofwar
body:
## Summary

A genuinely separate feature axis, as requested: how many raw resources (Orokin Cell, Ferrite, Neurodes, ...) does the player need to craft everything still missing, and how many *more* do they need given what they already own.

### The data-source investigation

Checked WFCD/warframestat first, since every other integration in this tool uses it. Dead end, confirmed thoroughly:
- Live-tested `/items`, `/warframes/{item}`, and the full unfiltered item record against Rhino, Chroma, Ash Prime, and Braton — none carry more than an incidental one-off resource (Rhino shows only "1x Neurode", nowhere near its real build cost).
- Confirmed via [WFCD/warframe-items#276](https://github.com/WFCD/warframe-items/issues/276) (closed "not planned") this is a permanent upstream decision, not a field-selection fix on our end.

The **Warframe Wiki**'s `Module:Blueprints/data` has full recipes — but only as raw Lua table source (`?action=raw`), no JSON API, no stability contract. Presented this tradeoff explicitly; the user chose to build it anyway over dropping the feature.

### Implementation

- **`blueprint_costs.py`**: a small hand-rolled tokenizer/parser for this Lua dialect (data-only — tables, strings, numbers, booleans, `--` comments, no expressions — so no full Lua interpreter dependency). A parse or fetch failure degrades to an empty dict, never a crash or a fabricated number.
- **Two real parsing bugs found and fixed** by diffing raw-vs-parsed key counts (1147 raw entries → only 680 parsed at first):
  1. The module has multiple top-level categories (`Blueprints` for weapons, `Suits` for Warframes) that must be merged — this alone was silently hiding **every single Warframe** (467 of 1147 entries).
  2. Weapon sub-parts embed their own `Cost` block (self-contained recipe) but Warframe sub-parts don't — each is its own top-level `"<Frame> <Part>"` entry instead, and Prime frames need word-overlap dedup on top of that (`"Ash Prime"` + `"Prime Chassis"` → sibling `"Ash Prime Chassis"`, not the naive double-up `"Ash Prime Prime Chassis"`).
- Coverage is **inherently partial** (~70% of the masterable catalog — e.g. Sentinels aren't in the wiki module at all); unmatched equipment is silently omitted, never estimated, and the UI/CLI say so explicitly.
- `private_inventory.owned_resources()`: counts held raw materials from a live inventory, built from exactly the component entries `items.is_part_component` already excludes as "not a farmable part" — can never disagree with the acquisition chain about what counts as a resource.
- `service.build_resource_needs()`: pure aggregator (no I/O), called from `cli.py`/`web.py` after `plan_route` returns — same "fetch-after-plan" pattern as `select_price_candidates`/`build_buy_vs_farm`.
- New "Crafting resources needed" collapsible card in the web UI + matching CLI section. Shows gross totals when no inventory is available, or an actual shortfall (`short_by`) when one is.

## Test plan

- [x] `python -m pytest -q` — 99 passed (18 new: Lua tokenizer/parser, both recursion shapes, Prime dedup, unknown-name safety, fetch/parse-failure fallback, resource aggregation with shortfall math, `owned_resources` extraction)
- [x] Live end-to-end: real API call for `["Rhino", "Volt Prime", "Ash Prime"]` returns a correctly-summed, correctly-sorted 12-resource total (2750 Rubedo, 2500 Ferrite, 2450 Circuits, ...)
- [x] Synthetic shortfall test: need 2 Neurodes/own 1 → short 1; need 1500 Ferrite/own 99999 → short 0 (floors at zero)
- [x] Visual browser verification (Chrome extension): card expands to show the exact same sorted total as the direct API test; console clean
- [x] `npm run build` — clean, no errors

author: ianmayo
body:
## Summary

`/speckit.plan` + `/speckit.tasks` for spec 284 (the Copilot-Chat-drives-Debrief spike, whose spec merged in #670). Design artifacts + task breakdown — no implementation code yet.

- `plan.md` — architecture, constitution check, **Verification Approach**, project structure
- `research.md` — 8 resolved design decisions
- `data-model.md` — LM tool input + boundary types
- `contracts/lm-tools.md`, `contracts/telemetry-record.schema.json`
- `quickstart.md` — demo scenarios + instrumentation runbook
- `tasks.md` — 51 tasks across 7 phases (incl. Phase 6.5 Automated Verification)
- `evidence/opening-context.md` — cached blog opener (mermaid Hook)
- `CLAUDE.md` — active-technologies entry (agent-context script)

## Architecture

Four tools contributed via the **VS Code Language Model Tools API** (`vscode.lm.registerTool`), quarantined in a new `apps/vscode/src/copilot/` folder: `debrief_searchPlots`, `debrief_summarizeCurrentPlot`, `debrief_listTools`, `debrief_runTool`. The extension mediates every call, so it carries live editor context (open plot, current selection). Search and execution reuse existing surfaces — `stacService.listItems` + `debrief.openPlot`, and the `calcService.executeTool` Python stdio path.

## Key decisions resolved during planning

| Decision | Resolution |
|----------|-----------|
| FR-007 search placement | Client-side in TypeScript over `stacService.listItems` — least-work; reuses the existing open-plot command. No new Python API. |
| Edit round-trip (FR-011) | Reuse `mapPanel.updatePlotFeatures` but **suppress the Tools-panel path's immediate `writeGeoJson`** — chat edits stay dirty/undoable and never touch disk. The central design point. |
| Undo (FR-012) | Plot editor is a webview custom editor with app-managed session state, not VS Code's native undo stack. "Single undo" maps to session revert; exercised in the extension-host test, reported as a finding if it's a gap. |
| Model identity | The LM Tools API does not expose the active model — routing quality is measured by the gated probe / operator annotation, recorded as a known limitation. |
| Provenance (FR-023) | Reuse `LogService.recordToolResult` + carry the analyst utterance in metadata; no LinkML schema change for a spike. |
| Engine | Bump `engines.vscode` `^1.85.0` → `^1.99.0` (agent-mode tool integration landed in 1.99). |

## Automated verification (no human, no Copilot)

A developer verifies the whole feature with one command — no live chat session. Only the model's tool *selection* is non-deterministic; everything below the tool boundary is deterministic and gated in CI:

- **Unit** (vitest, mocked) — delegation/gating/routing
- **Integration** (vitest, real debrief-calc + fixture STAC catalog, FR-029) — the real search + Python round-trip
- **Extension-host** (`vscode-test` + `vscode.lm.invokeTool`, no model, FR-030) — edit applies, session dirty, **zero on-disk writes** (FR-011), decline applies nothing, `openPlot` opens
- **Scripted-transcript replay** (FR-031) — the 8 scenarios as canned tool-calls; the SC-002 gate in place of a manual demo
- **Gated model-routing probe** (FR-032) — nightly Anthropic probe for routing quality; skips cleanly without a key

The live Copilot session is now **supplementary** evidence (blog screenshots), not the correctness gate. `pnpm --filter @debrief/vscode test:unit && test:integration` is the one-command verdict (SC-009).

## Constitution check

No violations. The cloud-LLM dependency is additive/optional and spike-scoped (Article I permits optional online features); all writes route through the existing writer/`saveSession` path (Article IV); provenance preserved (Article III); strict types throughout (Article XV).

## Notes for reviewers

- No implementation code yet — next step is `/speckit.implement` (or work the phases manually from Setup + Foundation).
- Task IDs ascend T001–T051; new automated-verification work is Phase 6.5 (T033–T038).

body:
## Port Receipt Vault to Next.js 14 (App Router) + React

Same app, same look, same Firebase/Cloudinary backend — rebuilt on a real framework with a build pipeline, plus a couple of mobile/UX fixes.

### What changed
- **Framework:** plain HTML/CSS/JS → **Next.js 14 (App Router) + React 18**. The single `app.js` is split into:
  - `lib/` — pure, testable helpers (`receipt.js` OCR/parse/compress, `cloudinary.js`, `firebase.js`, `config.js`)
  - `components/` — `Login`, `AppShell`, `Dashboard`, `Capture`, `Receipts`, `Export`, `ConsentBanner`, `Toast`
  - `app/` — `layout.js` (fonts via `next/font`), `page.js` (auth gate + Firestore subscription), `globals.css`
- **Dependencies bundled via npm** (Firebase, Chart.js, Tesseract.js) instead of CDN `<script>` tags — removes the old Subresource-Integrity concern.
- **`privacy.html`** kept as a static file in `public/`.

### Fixes
- **Gallery picker on phones.** The old single input used `capture="environment"`, which locks phones to the camera. Now there are two inputs — **Take a photo** (camera) and **Choose from gallery** (photo library).
- **Google avatar not loading.** Added `referrerPolicy="no-referrer"` to the profile image — `lh3.googleusercontent.com` blocks requests with an unknown referrer.

### Notes
- Firebase/Cloudinary config is unchanged (still yours, public by design — security is in the Firestore rules).
- `vercel.json` now sets `"framework": "nextjs"`; Vercel auto-detects the rest.
- `npm install && npm run dev` → http://localhost:5173. `npm run build` is green.
- README updated with the new structure, setup, and deploy steps.

body:
Ports the Discord channel v1 (local runtime) onto `moda-labs/bobi-agent`
main. The work was developed and reviewed on a working fork (since deleted);
the design doc is preserved in the forge team workspace. Milestones M1–M3; the remote/Durable-Object
driver (M4) and polish (M5) remain follow-ups per the design doc.

Implements the Discord channel for local deployments end-to-end: inbound over a
persistent Gateway WebSocket held by the local event server, outbound over
plain REST through the existing channel gateway.

## What's ported
- **M1 — protocol core + normalizer** (`event-server/core`): sans-IO
  `DiscordGatewaySession` (opcodes, IDENTIFY/RESUME, heartbeat bookkeeping,
  close-code policy — 4004/4013/4014 fatal with no reconnect; resume-first
  reconnect protects Discord's 1000/day IDENTIFY budget) and the
  `MESSAGE_CREATE` normalizer (`adapters/discord.ts`) mirroring the WhatsApp
  adapter. v1 scope: DMs, bot @mentions, replies-to-bot only; bot-authored
  messages dropped (loop prevention); snowflake = event id.
- **M2 — outbound adapter + registration**: `discordAdapter` in the channel
  registry (send/edit/typing/history/files, 2000-char budget, `edit-fallback`
  streaming, `transport: socket`); signed-only `POST /discord/apps` in core,
  upstream bot-token verification, bubble-scoped send credential, and the
  `discord:<application_id>` global grant-gated topic.
- **M3 — local runtime driver**: `DiscordGatewayManager`
  (`src/discord-gateway-local.ts`) inside the existing local Node process
  (shares the in-memory storage adapter). Exponential backoff with jitter,
  resume-first reconnect, handshake watchdog, fatal-code parking surfaced in
  `/health`, env bootstrap (`BOBI_ES_DISCORD_*`).
- **Python wiring**: `register_discord_apps` at session start, `_detect_discord`
  subscription, `authorize_resources` generalized over whatsapp/discord,
  `ensure_running` env forwarding, Discord connector card in `bobi setup`.
- **Docs/skills**: `skills/discord-setup.md`, `docs/EVENT_SERVER.md` Discord
  section.

## Drift reconciled against upstream main (0.43.0)
The fork PR branched from `4c0e3ee`, a direct ancestor of upstream main
(shared linear history). Cherry-picked the 4 commits; the following drift was
resolved in a dedicated reconciliation commit:

- **Repo split (#713)**: `event-server/src/index.ts` (the Cloudflare Worker)
  moved to the private `bobi-deploy` repo. The fork PR's Worker-side
  `/discord/apps` wiring belongs there, not here, so that hunk is dropped.
  M4's remote driver is a follow-up in the private repo's domain.
- **Publishable events-core dist (#711)**: relative imports now carry `.js`
  extensions. `adapters/discord.ts` and `gateway/discord.ts` updated to match,
  so the pack + scratch-consumer publish smoke resolves `./gateway/discord`
  and `./adapters/discord` as plain-Node ESM.
- **`discordApi` typed its body as `BodyInit`**, which is undefined under the
  event-server root typecheck (no `dom` lib); switched to the structural
  `string | FormData` union that `whatsappApi` already documents.
- **`tests/test_adapters.py`**: `discord` is now a builtin adapter, moved from
  the "unknown service" assertion to the registered-services assertion.
- **`tests/test_import_boundaries.py`**: classified `discord-gateway-local`
  under the phase-2 public-`src/` partition.

## Verification (local)
- `event-server`: `npx tsc --noEmit` clean; `npx vitest run` **352 passed**
  (incl. 25 Discord state-machine/normalizer + 8 new core registration tests);
  `npm run smoke -w core` (pack + node/ts scratch consumer) passed.
- Python unit: `pytest tests/ --ignore=tests/integration --ignore=tests/e2e`
  **3025 passed**. 7 failures are pre-existing and reproduce identically on
  clean upstream main (missing `shellcheck`, ambient `~/.bobi`
  install-sensitive `resolve_root`/`setup_actions`, `DEFAULT_EVENT_SERVER`
  slack-manifest tests) — not introduced by this port.
- Discord integration: `pytest tests/integration/test_discord_gateway.py`
  **5 passed** (IDENTIFY without the privileged intent, `/health` surface,
  `MESSAGE_CREATE` → grant-filtered delivery to a subscribed deployment socket,
  resume-after-drop keeps delivering, outbound `bobi reply`).

## Not in scope (v1)
Full-channel firehose, slash commands/interactions, sharding, and the remote
Durable Object driver (M4) — the Worker has no Gateway driver yet, noted in the
docs and the registration response.

## Vercel Web Analytics Implementation

Successfully configured Vercel Web Analytics for the annecy.finance static HTML website.

### Project Context
This is a static HTML website (no framework, no build process) for Annecy M&A, a business focused on M&A services in the Annecy region of France.

### Changes Made

**Modified:**
- `index.html` - Added Vercel Web Analytics script tag in the `<head>` section

### Implementation Details

Following the official Vercel documentation (https://vercel.com/docs/analytics/quickstart and https://vercel.com/docs/analytics/package), I added the Vercel Web Analytics script using the CDN approach for vanilla HTML projects:

```html
<script defer src="https://cdn.vercel-insights.com/v1/script.js"></script>
```

The script was placed in the `<head>` section, after the stylesheet link and before the closing `</head>` tag. This follows Vercel's recommended approach for static HTML sites.

### Key Points

1. **No package installation required** - For static HTML sites, Vercel Analytics uses a CDN-hosted script instead of npm packages
2. **Automatic tracking** - Once deployed to Vercel, the script will automatically track page views and visitor data
3. **Zero configuration** - The script works out of the box with sensible defaults
4. **Privacy-friendly** - Vercel Analytics is designed to be privacy-friendly and doesn't use cookies
5. **Dashboard activation** - Analytics must be enabled in the Vercel dashboard for the project before data collection begins

### Next Steps

To complete the setup:
1. Deploy the site to Vercel using `vercel deploy` or through the Vercel dashboard
2. Enable Web Analytics in the Vercel dashboard by navigating to Analytics in the sidebar and selecting this project
3. Click the "Enable" button to activate analytics collection
4. After deployment, verify the installation by checking the browser's Network tab for requests to Vercel's analytics endpoints
5. Analytics data will appear in the Vercel dashboard after a few hours/days of traffic

### Testing

Since this is a static HTML site with no build process, no additional testing was required. The HTML remains valid and all existing functionality is preserved.

author: nicholas-lonsinger
body:
## Summary
A single test — `cancelDispatchedPullAsksOwnerToAbort` in `FileProviderServiceSourceTests` — is responsible for essentially every recent Build & Test failure. It passed `fetchReplyTimeout: 2` into the code under test purely to keep a harmless post-cancel background timer from lingering. On a starved macos-26 CI scheduler that 2s reply timer fires *before* the test's own `cancellation.cancel()`, completing the pull with `serverUnreachable` and failing the `NSUserCancelledError` assertions.

Retry-on-failure (`maximumTestRepetitions: 2`, `retryOnFailure`) has been masking this: across the last 20 *green* runs, ~7 had this exact test fail on the first attempt and pass on retry. Visible failures on `main` since 2026-07-09 are all this test.

## Root cause
`performPull` in `FileProviderServiceSource` arms a reply-timeout timer the moment a pull dispatches over a live connection, and (by design — documented there) never cancels it; whichever of reply / connection-error / reply-timeout fires first wins via `OnceCompletion`. The test needs the pull to be *in flight* when it cancels, so the reply timeout must not fire before `cancel()`. A 2s bound is well within CI's `@MainActor` scheduling jitter.

## Changes
- **`FileProviderServiceSourceTests`**: use `makeSource()`'s full 120s default reply timeout instead of `fetchReplyTimeout: 2`. The lingering timer is a no-op after cancel and does not delay suite completion, so the small bound bought nothing and cost a flake. Comment rewritten to explain the race.
- **`SpiceClipboardServiceTests`**: convert `pipeEOFDisconnects`'s `waitUntil { !service.isConnected }` poll to the canonical event-driven `waitForChange` (`isConnected` is an `@Observable` stored property; matches the 17 existing `waitForChange { service.isConnected }` sites in `VsockControlServiceTests`). Found while auditing poll sites; removes a poll rather than blessing it.
- **`CLAUDE.md` → "Async waits in tests"**: new rule — an injected production timeout must be either the behavior under test (small is correct) or sized past any scheduler stall (production default / ≥60s), never a small "tidy" value. This failure mode is orthogonal to the existing event-driven-wait guidance: the flaky test *already* used event-driven `AsyncGate` waits.

## Test plan
- [x] `make test-package` — all 239 KernovaKit tests pass (FileProviderServiceSource suite green)
- [x] `make test-suite SUITE=KernovaTests/SpiceClipboardServiceTests` — `pipeEOFDisconnects` passes
- [x] `make lint` clean
- [ ] Green CI on the PR

## Notes
This is PR 1 of 3 from an investigation into intermittent Build & Test failures. The follow-ups (CI retry visibility so `retryOnFailure` stops silently masking flakes; and applying the #506 shared-state-isolation treatment to the remaining leaky `UserDefaults`/pasteboard test suites) land as separate PRs.

author: johnnywilson16
body:
## Summary

Fixes #34.

`_finalize_numeric` used `float(nonnull.abs().max()) < float(2**63 - 1024)` to decide whether an integral column fits int64. Two real defects:

- **Magnitude-only check:** `-2**63` is a valid int64, but its magnitude (`2**63`) fails the check → needless float64 demotion of legitimate data.
- **Boundary exclusion:** `2**63 - 1024` — the largest float64 below `2**63` — converts to int64 exactly, but strict `<` rejected it → float64 demotion.

## Why the issue's proposed fix is unsafe

The issue suggests `_INT64_SAFE = float(2**63 - 1)` with `<=`. That constant **rounds up to `2**63`** in float64 (`float(2**63 - 1) == float(2**63)` is `True`), so the proposed guard would admit `float(2**63)` and let `.astype("int64")` wrap around — it would introduce the very overflow the issue worries about. Notably, the *current* code does not actually overflow (float rounding aligns at the 1024-ulp boundary); its failure mode is wrong dtype decisions, not corruption. The PR description of record for #34 should reflect that.

## Fix

Compare `min()`/`max()` in Python-int space against exact int64 bounds (`_fits_int64`). Python ints are arbitrary-precision → no rounding at the boundary; `int()` is exact because integrality (`% 1 == 0`) is checked first; `inf` raises `OverflowError` → treated as not fitting.

## Behavior/compat

Values in `{-2**63} ∪ [2**63 - 1024]` (and int64-extreme integers arriving via object/int paths) now finalize as int64/Int64 instead of float64 — numerically identical, dtype now correct. Everything else unchanged.

## Tests

- `test_finalize_numeric_int64_boundaries_no_overflow_no_demotion` and `test_finalize_numeric_int64_min_not_rejected_by_abs_asymmetry` — both fail on main (float64 demotion), pass with the fix; also pin that `float(2**63)` stays float64 and the nullable Int64 path is exact.
- `test_huge_integer_strings_still_stay_float_end_to_end` — pipeline-level control (2**64 stays float64).

## Verification

```
pytest tests/test_dtypes.py -q             # 25 passed
pytest -m "not online and not large"       # green, coverage 93.49% (gate 93)
ruff check src tests && mypy src/freshdata # clean
```

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Improved numeric type handling near the int64 boundaries.
  * Values within the exact int64 range now convert correctly without unnecessary conversion to float64.
  * Values outside the representable range continue to be safely handled as float64.
  * Corrected handling of the minimum int64 value and very large integer-like inputs.

author: baggepinnen
body:
Adds a `polar` keyword option to `CSMakie.nyquistplot` that draws the Nyquist curve in a `Makie.PolarAxis` instead of a Cartesian `Axis`. This provides native polar \"graph paper\": circles of constant magnitude and rays of constant phase, drawn and re-ticked automatically by Makie when the axis limits change, with correct aspect ratio by construction. Requested in discussion [JuliaControl/ControlSystems.jl#1064](https://github.com/JuliaControl/ControlSystems.jl/discussions/1064).

A `rlimits` keyword (forwarded to `PolarAxis`) allows limiting the radial axis, which is useful for systems with poles on or near the imaginary axis where the Nyquist curve reaches very large magnitudes.

All existing options (`Ms_circles`, `Mt_circles`, `unit_circle`, `critical_point`, MIMO grid layout, adaptive downsampling) work in polar mode as well; Cartesian coordinates are converted point-wise to `(angle, radius)`.

## Example

```julia
using ControlSystemsBase, GLMakie  # or CairoMakie

P = tf(4, [1, 2, 1, 0])  # 4 / (s(s+1)²)
CSMakie.nyquistplot(P; polar=true, rlimits=(0, 3), unit_circle=true, Ms_circles=[1.7])
```

body:
## Summary

Keeps the Google review ask alive in the hybrid world — as a **server-driven step in the close flow**, sequenced after the baseline batch so a promoter's required questions are never sacrificed for the ask.

## Why it had to move

In template sessions the legacy fast-path's model-emitted `[CHAT:END]` would end the chat **before** required delivery — and promoters are exactly whose ratings you want on dashboards. V4 also forbids model-announced wrap-ups.

## New hybrid promoter sequence

`interview → baseline batch → review ask → parse yes/no → templated final close`

- Fires from both close entry points (turn-count close and batch exhaustion, with a session refresh in case the qualifying NPS just landed via widget)
- `parseReviewReply` is conservative: clear yes only, negation beats embedded "ok", "why not" recognized as agreement, ambiguity = no
- Records to `sessions.google_review_response` — the existing CompletionCard link-reveal works unchanged
- **Legacy sessions keep the model-driven fast-path byte-for-byte** (addendum now gated to the legacy prompt key)

## Test plan

- [x] 12 new tests; 411 server green
- [ ] Staging: score a 9+ in a template session, complete the baseline, verify ask → yes → link on the completion card

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes session close-phase behavior and when review links appear for hybrid promoters; parsing is conservative but misclassification could still affect UX.
> 
> **Overview**
> Hybrid template sessions now run a **server-driven** Google review step after required survey widgets are done, instead of relying on the legacy model fast-path that could end the chat early or conflict with V4 wrap-up rules.
> 
> The close flow gains `awaiting_review_response`: qualifying promoters (reviews enabled, NPS at/above client threshold, no prior response) get `fireReviewAsk` from **turn-count/terminal close** and from **baseline-batch exhaustion** in `POST /answer` (with a session refresh when NPS may have just been set). The next user message is classified by conservative `parseReviewReply`, stored on `sessions.google_review_response`, then answered with a templated `generateFinalClose` and `chat_end: true` so the existing CompletionCard link reveal still works.
> 
> **Legacy** sessions keep the model-driven promoter fast-path; that prompt addendum is now gated to `promptKey === "system_prompt"` only. Promoters on hybrid skip playback and go straight to review ask → final close.

### Motivation
- Provide a safe Flight Alerts V1 that lets users save/view flight itinerary fields and receive trip-linked reminders without introducing fake or live flight status claims. 
- Ensure flight reminder scheduling remains centralized and non-blocking, and keep all user-facing text localized for en/tr/es/fr/de/ar/ru/zh.

### Description
- Data model: add optional outbound/return flight leg support (`TripFlightLegDetails`, `outbound` / `return`) while preserving legacy fields for compatibility and normalization in `src/contexts/TripsContext.tsx` and `src/services/tripsService.ts`.
- Create/Edit Trip: make flight input optional and compact, validate date/time only when the user enters flight fields, and use localized helper copy (`CreateTripScreen.tsx`).
- Trip Detail: render a safe “Uçuş bilgileri” section showing only saved itinerary fields (outbound/return flight, airline, flight number, airports, date/time) and a reminder-ready indicator if a related reminder exists (`TripDetailScreen.tsx`).
- Flight Alerts screen: rebuild the existing flight deals screen as a saved-trip flight reminders list that reads reminders from saved trips and routes guests to `Login` with localized copy (`FlightDealsScreen.tsx`).
- Reminder generation & notifications: keep scheduling centralized via `generateTripReminderPlan` and `notificationService`; outbound/return reminders are created only when the normalized leg departure date exists and invalid/past reminders are skipped (`src/services/tripReminderPlan.ts`, `src/services/notificationService.ts`).
- Tax Free safety: return-flight reminder copy safely suggests checking Tax Free documents/receipts without claiming airport-specific desks or live processes (localized keys updated).
- Localization: add/update Flight Alerts V1 keys for en, tr, es, fr, de, ar, ru, zh in `src/translations/translations.ts` and ensure required Turkish phrases are present.
- QA tooling: add `tools/checkFlightAlertsV1.ts` to enforce no seeded/mock/demo flight alerts, no live-status labels unless a real provider is detected, optional flight fields behavior, centralized scheduling usage, guest Login routing, and locale coverage.
- Safety changes: no fake flight status or new flight API added; flight engine remains read-only and provider check detected no real provider so UI never shows live flight statuses (`src/services/flightEngine.ts` remains provider-less).
- Files changed (key): `src/contexts/TripsContext.tsx`, `src/services/tripsService.ts`, `src/services/tripReminderPlan.ts`, `src/screens/CreateTripScreen.tsx`, `src/screens/TripDetailScreen.tsx`, `src/screens/FlightDealsScreen.tsx`, `src/translations/translations.ts`, `tools/checkFlightAlertsV1.ts`, small safety locale fixes in `src/services/transportationV2Service.ts` and `tools/checkTransportationV2.ts`.

author: threadedstack-steward
body:
## What changed
`repos/backend/src/services/endpoints/proxyEndpoint.ts` stashes the upstream HTTP status code onto the shared request object (http-proxy-middleware's `proxyRes`/`error` callbacks receive the same underlying object as `execute`'s `req` — Express decorates Node's `IncomingMessage` in place) so the retry loop and error handler can read it back. This was done via five separate `(x as any).__proxyStatusCode` casts, plus one unrelated `(response as any).setHeader(...)` cast that wasn't needed (`ServerResponse` already types `setHeader`).

Replaced all five `__proxyStatusCode` casts with a single local `TProxyStatusCarrier` type (`{ __proxyStatusCode?: number }`) intersected with the actual inferred parameter type at each site, and dropped the unnecessary `setHeader` cast. No behavior change — this is a type-safety tightening only.

## Why
`as any` on a shared mutable field discards all type checking at both the write and read sites — a typo in the property name in any one spot (e.g. `__proxyStatuscode`) would silently break retry/error-status logic (used on the high-traffic `/proxy` request path) with zero compiler warning. The typed carrier keeps the intentional cross-callback mutation pattern but makes it type-checked.

## Verification
- `pnpm --filter @tdsk/backend types` — clean, no errors.
- `npx vitest run --config configs/vitest.config.ts src/services/endpoints/proxyEndpoint.test.ts` — 26/26 passing (existing retry/error/redirect/transform coverage, unchanged behavior).
- `npx vitest run --config configs/vitest.config.ts src/services/endpoints/` — 65/65 passing across all endpoint executor tests.

author: ilyaask
body:
## Summary

- add the unregistered project Create core
- distinguish definite failure, success, and uncertain create outcomes
- preserve a validated canonical project ID with the planned name when recovery is possible
- reject mismatched response names instead of silently changing Terraform desired state
- report every malformed durable response field in uncertain-outcome diagnostics
- cover request expansion, SDK failures, ambiguous responses, malformed responses, and mismatched names

## Why this is v1 work

This is the next bounded project-resource slice after the durable project client and schema/model helpers. The package remains unregistered until complete CRUD satisfies the Terraform Plugin Framework resource contract without placeholder lifecycle methods.

## API and Terraform behavior

- project creation uses the durable Kernel Go SDK client with SDK retries disabled
- SDK 4xx responses are definite failures
- transport errors, 5xx responses, nil responses, malformed responses, and response-name mismatches are uncertain outcomes
- uncertain outcomes tell the operator to inspect Kernel and import the canonical project ID before applying again when Terraform is not already tracking it
- a valid ID returned on an uncertain outcome is preserved with the planned name
- all malformed response fields are included in the single uncertain-outcome diagnostic
- no lookup-by-name recovery is attempted because it could adopt a pre-existing project
- partial-state behavior was verified against Terraform Plugin Framework v1.19.0, the version pinned by this repository

## Tests run

- `gofmt -l cmd internal`
- `go test ./internal/resources/project -run 'TestCreateProject'`
- `go test -race ./internal/resources/project -run 'TestCreateProject'`
- `go test -short -timeout=2m ./...`
- `go vet ./...`

All commands passed. `gofmt -l` produced no output.

## Acceptance status

Not run. This core is intentionally unregistered and has no live Terraform surface. End-to-end project acceptance remains deferred until full CRUD, import, and provider registration land.

## Review status

The original implementation passed the sequential deslop, incremental self-review, autoreview, Dave Cheney Go, eblog, and final agreement gates.

Sayan's follow-up findings are addressed:

- replaced the unreadable pasted test output with concise reproducible commands
- corrected the framework verification reference to v1.19.0
- aggregate every flatten diagnostic detail instead of reporting only `flattenDiags[0]`
- added a regression test where both project ID and name are malformed

No findings were rejected.

## Deferred

- Terraform Framework lifecycle adapters and provider registration
- project Read, Update, Delete, and Import
- live acceptance tests
- project resource examples and generated docs
- runtime and session operations remain outside Terraform

body:
## SEC-3 — close the all-pods/all-ports intra-namespace ingress hole

Ports the one manifest change from the stale `sec3-backend-networkpolicy` branch onto current main (that branch is behind on Go and is **not** being merged — it will be closed as PR #27), and adds a Kyverno guardrail so the hole cannot recur.

### Changes
- **`k8s/policies/backend-network-policies.yaml`** — replace `ingress.from: [- podSelector: {}]` (every pod, all ports) with a **scoped** rule: specific client `podSelector.matchLabels` + a specific `ports:` entry. The `hostNetwork` node-CIDR `ipBlock` rule (port 8080) and `default-deny-ingress` are unchanged.
- **`k8s/policies/disallow-open-intra-namespace-ingress.yaml`** — new Kyverno `ClusterPolicy` (`validationFailureAction: Enforce`) denying any NetworkPolicy whose `ingress[].from[]` has an empty `podSelector` ({} = every pod). Targets **only** ingress from-peers, not `spec.podSelector` (the legit "applies to all pods" selector).
- **tests** — 3 fixtures (scoped→pass, open→denied, default-deny→not flagged) + result assertions.

### Verification
- `kyverno test k8s/policies/tests` → **6 passed / 0 failed**.
- `kyverno apply` cross-check → the open policy fails validation (guardrail actually denies it).

### Deploy safety
Verified no other NetworkPolicies exist cluster-wide (none in helm charts), so the cluster-wide Enforce guardrail blocks nothing legitimate on ArgoCD sync.
